1	# DataQ on AWS — Terraform (OpenTofu) runbook
2	
3	A second, parallel deployment of DataQ (Azure stays the deployed prod — see
4	`deploy/terraform/azure/`), into a fresh, dedicated AWS account. Unlike the
5	Azure stack, nothing here is shared with another stack: this account exists
6	only for this deployment.
7	
8	## What it creates
9	
10	| Resource | Purpose |
11	|---|---|
12	| VPC, 2 public subnets, IGW, route table | Networking. No NAT Gateway (decision: public-subnets-no-NAT, ~$33/mo saved — ECS tasks get no public inbound access, only the ALB→frontend path is internet-reachable) |
13	| `aws_ecs_cluster.app` + 3 Fargate services (api, worker, frontend) + 1 task def (migrate) | The app itself. api is internal-only (Cloud Map DNS `api.dataq.local`); frontend is the sole public surface (behind the ALB); worker runs embedded celery-beat, `desired_count=1` always (cannot scale to zero) |
14	| `aws_cloudfront_distribution.app` → `aws_lb.app` (ALB, HTTP :80) | Public ingress. CloudFront terminates HTTPS on its default `*.cloudfront.net` cert (#1345 — Cognito requires an HTTPS redirect URI); the ALB admits only CloudFront's origin-facing ranges and forwards to the frontend target group |
15	| `aws_db_instance.app` (RDS Postgres, `db.t4g.micro`) | The app's own database — this stack creates it directly (no shared-server bootstrap dance like the Azure stack, since this account is dedicated) |
16	| `aws_elasticache_replication_group.app` (`cache.t4g.micro`, TLS + auth token) | Celery broker + rate-limit store |
17	| `aws_cognito_user_pool.app` + SPA client | OIDC identity provider, validated by the backend's provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026 amendment) — not Azure AD |
18	| `aws_secretsmanager_secret.*` (2, infra-owned) + IAM grants | `database-url`/`redis-url` (infra-owned, referenced by ARN in task defs) + the app's own runtime grant under `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX` (`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`) |
19	| `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` + `aws_iam_role.github_deploy` | GitHub Actions → AWS auth for the Deploy workflow, OIDC federation, no stored access keys |
20	| CloudWatch Log Groups (4) | Container logs. No APM/tracing wired up yet — the OTel core is vendor-neutral but the exporter shipped so far is Azure-only |
21	
22	## Prerequisites
23	
24	- **OpenTofu** (`tofu`), not Terraform — same ADR 0024 rationale as the Azure stack.
25	- **AWS CLI credentials** for a **scoped IAM user**, never root. This repo's own bring-up used `AWS_PROFILE=dataq-deploy` (set as the default in the operator's shell) — see the session notes for the IAM bootstrap steps (create user, attach a policy, remove root's access keys/login session).
26	- A **GitHub repo** with Actions enabled (for the OIDC federation to have something to trust).
27	- Nothing else pre-exists — this stack creates its own VPC, database, cache, etc. from scratch, unlike the Azure stack's shared-resource dependencies.
28	
29	## Apply
30	
31	```bash
32	cd deploy/terraform/aws
33	tofu init
34	# state_encryption_passphrase comes from your terraform.tfvars — see
35	# terraform.tfvars.example.
36	#
37	# Image tags (#1349): the services RUN these images from the first apply.
38	# publish-images.yml tags main merges as `main-<full sha>` (the bare `<sha>`
39	# tag is owned by the manual Azure deploy.yml and usually does NOT exist), and
40	# its `paths` filter skips merges that don't change image content — so use the
41	# last IMAGE-BEARING main commit, not the branch tip, and verify the tag
42	# exists before applying:
43	IMG_SHA=$(git log origin/main -1 --format=%H -- backend frontend pyproject.toml)
44	docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:main-${IMG_SHA}" > /dev/null  # must succeed
45	TF_VAR_app_db_password="REDACTED" \
46	tofu plan -input=false -out=tfplan \
47	  -var="image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}" \
48	  -var="frontend_image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}"
49	tofu apply -input=false tfplan
50	```
51	
52	**Cost starts here.** `tofu apply` creates real, billable AWS resources (Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, ALB). Review the plan before applying. See the root-level deployment plan (in the session that built this stack) for the cost breakdown against the AWS free-tier credit.
53	
54	## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow
55	
56	```bash
57	tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn   # → repo secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
58	tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name         # → repo variable ECS_CLUSTER
59	tofu output -raw frontend_url             # → sanity-check reachability
60	```
61	
62	```bash
63	gh secret set AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN --body "$(tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn)"
64	gh variable set ECS_CLUSTER --body "$(tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name)"
65	gh variable set AWS_REGION --body "$(tofu output -raw -json | jq -r .aws_region.value 2>/dev/null || echo us-east-2)"
66	```
67	
68	A companion `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` (not yet built) will use these
69	to `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` via OIDC, then run the same
70	build→push(GHCR)→migrate(RunTask, poll-to-terminal)→`ecs update-service`
71	sequence the Azure `deploy.yml` runs, adapted to the AWS CLI equivalents.
72	
73	## State encryption
74	
75	Same discipline as the Azure stack (`versions.tf`'s `encryption {}` block):
76	the local state holds the generated RDS/ElastiCache passwords in plaintext
77	without it. `state_encryption_passphrase` is a **data-at-rest key**, not a
78	credential — it cannot be revoked or re-minted, and losing it makes
79	`terraform.tfstate` permanently unreadable. Keep a second copy off this
80	machine. A wrong/missing passphrase fails closed
81	(`cipher: message authentication failed`) without corrupting the file.
82	
83	## Verify
84	
85	```bash
86	# Confirm exactly what got created, tagged for this stack:
87	aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources \
88	  --tag-filters Key=Purpose,Values=dataq-app-aws
89	
90	# Reachability (through the frontend — the sole public surface):
91	curl -s "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)/healthz"
92	```
93	
94	Then in a browser: sign in through Cognito end-to-end, confirm `/api` and
95	`/mcp` return 401 unauthenticated without a credential, and run one real
96	suite against a live datasource to confirm the worker path.
97	
98	## Known gaps in this pass (deliberately deferred, not silently skipped)
99	
100	- No custom domain — the public URL is the CloudFront distribution's own
101	  `*.cloudfront.net` domain (HTTPS, default cert — #1345). Once a domain is
102	  chosen: Route53 + ACM cert + an `aliases` entry on the distribution.
103	- No private-subnet/NAT hardening — see `main.tf`'s decision note.
104	- No `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` yet — this stack only provisions the
105	  infra the workflow will drive.
106	- The Cognito `client_id`-vs-`aud` accommodation in `OidcBearerScheme`
107	  (backend) needs confirming against a real token from **this** pool once
108	  it's live — see `cognito.tf`'s comment.

1	# ECS Fargate — api (internal, Cloud Map DNS), worker (Celery + embedded
2	# beat, min=max=1 desired count — mirrors the Azure Container App's
3	# min_replicas=1 rationale: it can't scale to zero because it runs beat), and
4	# frontend (public via the ALB). All three run images from GHCR (public,
5	# anonymous pull — ADR 0023), same as the Azure stack.
6	
7	resource "aws_ecs_cluster" "app" {
8	  name = "dataq-app"
9	
10	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app" }
11	}
12	
13	# One shared security group for every ECS task: self-referencing ingress lets
14	# api/worker/frontend talk to each other (and to Redis/RDS, which have their
15	# own SGs allowing traffic FROM this one), plus a narrow allow from the ALB
16	# SG for the frontend's published port.
17	resource "aws_security_group" "ecs_tasks" {
18	  name = "dataq-app-ecs-tasks"
19	  # EC2 SG descriptions allow ONLY a-zA-Z0-9. _-:/()#,@[]+=&;{}!$* (#1357) —
20	  # no em-dash, and no '>' either (the first fix missed that).
21	  description = "DataQ ECS tasks - internal task-to-task traffic + ALB to frontend"
22	  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
23	
24	  egress {
25	    from_port   = 0
26	    to_port     = 0
27	    protocol    = "-1"
28	    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
29	  }
30	
31	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-ecs-tasks" }
32	}
33	
34	resource "aws_security_group_rule" "ecs_tasks_self_ingress" {
35	  # Narrower than "every port" on purpose: the only task-to-task call within
36	  # this security group is frontend -> api on 8000 (Cloud Map DNS). worker
37	  # and frontend serve nothing another task calls, so opening the full
38	  # 0-65535 range would grant blast-radius no actual traffic pattern needs.
39	  type                     = "ingress"
40	  from_port                = 8000
41	  to_port                  = 8000
42	  protocol                 = "tcp"
43	  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id
44	  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id

46

57	# internally (DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api.dataq.local:8000, alb.tf's

61	  name = "dataq.local"
62	  vpc  = aws_vpc.app.id

Test Connection for unsaved connection drafts (#351, #1116 — `POST /connections/test`, structurally cannot persist; review also surfaced the `*_secret_name` SSRF/exfiltration class on the same auth gate, filed [#1118](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1118), mitigation deferred to RBAC #740–#744); the **`anomaly` monitor kind itself** (#593, #1117 backend + #1119 authoring UI) — rolling z-score baseline with optional seasonality over `metric_value` history, reusing the existing `monitor_baselines` table (no migration), `skip` on cold start, dimension deliberately underivable → NULL (ADR 0038); the per-check metric trend view (#594, #1121) with threshold bands plus a second anomaly-baseline panel, seasonality-aware; check-version restore (#283, #1120), minting a new version rather than delegating to the PATCH-semantics `update_check`; and a zero-dependency PDF report export of a run (#345, #1122). **Live-verified 2026-08-01 against both live warehouses** (the #953 rule — for anything crossing a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence): Snowflake `RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER` row_count=34680.0 + freshness `ORDER_TS`=132.28h; Unity Catalog `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment` row_count=180.0 + freshness `scored_at`=132.48h — z-scores computed cleanly over both. Every PR carried the mandated `/code-review` agent flow; 15+ real defects were caught pre-merge, including two concurrency bugs (a baseline-UPDATE lost-update race, a stale "Connected" badge) and two honesty-of-display bugs (an under-reported redaction state, a threshold-band caption overclaiming below 2 eligible points); the one deferred finding is #1118 above. **Unplanned, shipped + live-verified 2026-07-28/29 — three batches in one orchestrated session (#1096–#1112, 10 PRs):** Batch 2 reliability (beat **crontabs** #1099 — a 24h interval never fires under embedded beat; **staleness signals** #1100 — stale-lineage surface + de-configured-pull purge + the API-side workspace dead-poll alert on the new `workspace_health` table) and Batches 3+4 assets/lineage (**ADR [0040](docs/adr/0040-warehouse-inventory-sync-table-enumeration-seam.md)** — the table-enumeration seam + opt-in per-connection **inventory sync** #1103, so a table with no suite/run/edge is visible-unmonitored instead of invisible (the prod `reference`-schema report); asset **paging + honest truncation** #1105; S3-compatible **endpoint identity** #1106; **GET_LINEAGE per-seed traversal + Snowpark scratch stitching** #1110 — prod's Snowflake lineage lifted from view-level to full tier, live-verified). The recurring lesson bit twice more (#1112): mocked tests stayed green through **two stacked driver-boundary crashes** in one SQL literal (pyformat `%`, then Snowflake's own string parser eating `ESCAPE '\'`) — for warehouse SQL, run the exact statement live before push. **Unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — IaC CLI moved Terraform → OpenTofu (ADR 0024 amendment):** Terraform has been BUSL-1.1 since v1.6 and was the one source-available binary still touching a project ADR 0031 puts on record as MIT-distributed. **Nothing was in violation** — rule 40 governs the dependency tree (what DataQ *ships*) and the CLI never enters an image — so this is coherence, not compliance; the timing argument is #505, since converting one Azure stack is contained and converting three is not. **The acceptance bar was equivalence, not a clean plan**, because the stack already carries pre-existing drift (#1086 — prod's ADR-0034 lineage env vars are absent from `containerapps.tf`, so an apply would DELETE them; the rendered plan hides this behind a positional `env` shuffle and only `show -json` reveals it): both CLIs were run against live Azure, plans exported with `-out`, rendered via `show -json`, and the normalized `resource_changes` diffed — **byte-for-byte identical** (40 changes, `no-op=38 update=2`), provider versions preserved exactly, only the registry host + hashes moved. The *rendered* text plans DO differ (branding, refresh ordering, column alignment, hidden-attribute counts), which is why eyeballing them would not have settled it. State, providers, and the `deploy/terraform/<cloud>/` path are unchanged — `terraform {}` is OpenTofu's own block name. Harness stack converted in the same pass, **plan-only** (a blanket harness apply arms ADF triggers). The swap is **convention, not enforcement** — nothing is OpenTofu-exclusive yet, which is what keeps it reversible; the `encryption {}` follow-up is the one-way door and is deliberately separate. **Unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — S3-compatible endpoints (#1063/#1065):** optional `endpoint_url` + `addressing_style` on the `s3` datasource **and** the `dbt` provider, via one shared `core/s3_endpoint.py`; unlocks MinIO / Ceph / R2 / Wasabi / Backblaze. `auto` → **path** addressing when an endpoint is set is load-bearing (MinIO serves the bucket in the path only, so boto3's virtual-host default fails every read), and `endpoint_url` rejects an embedded credential per the #754/#826 rule. **Live-proven against MinIO** — suite 4/4 over 643 real rows, arrival-time freshness read off `LastModified` — because a non-AWS server is a different implementation and those values cross a driver boundary. It arose from an **Azure-free harness readiness exercise** (local Airflow + MinIO landing zone, all flows green incl. a live Snowflake load; Azure untouched, all five harness apps stayed `Stopped`), whose Snowflake half also produced a standing rule: **nothing in the harness may require a commercial licence** — stricter than rule 40, which governs only what DataQ *ships* — after LocalStack for Snowflake was evaluated and rejected (no community tier; image exits 55). fakesnow (Apache-2.0) is the stand-in, and probing it with DataQ's real code paths found **#1067**: a Snowflake connection with no Role tests green (the test is GX-free) and fails every suite run, since GX requires a `role` query param. See [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). Follow-ups #1064/#1066. **The four open ADR-0039 follow-ups were then closed the same day (#1069/#1070/#1071):** GHCR `:latest` now republishes on merge (the eval compose is fetched from `main` while the image moved only on dispatch — verified live); the pooled secret-store clients are released on cache reset, with the AKV **credential** closed alongside the client since they hold separate transport sessions; an **orphan-secret sweep** that reports by default and purges only when configured, because what it deletes is a live warehouse credential; and **AppRole auth** (ADR 0039 phase 2) with proactive renewal and one re-login on 403, so a revoked token self-heals instead of 403ing until restart. Two lessons worth carrying: the sweep's ownership registry was wrong **twice** (Slack and Teams are separate refs on one row; `*_secret_name` keys live in JSONB) and its introspection guard was a **tautology** — it iterated the models already registered, so a new model was invisible to it; and #435 was assessed and left open with a corrected AC, since Azure CMK is **creation-time-only** and our IaC stack does not own the Postgres server. **Also unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — the secret-store seam (ADR [0039](docs/adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md), #1056/#1061):** a fourth `SecretStore` speaking the **KV v2 HTTP API, not a vendor SDK**, so one mode serves OpenBao / Vault Community / Enterprise / HCP — this closes the last seam where Azure was the only production implementation, which #505 (AWS/GCP IaC) would have walked straight into. **OpenBao** (MPL-2.0) is shipped and pinned; Vault Community is BUSL-1.1 and therefore rule-40-forbidden as a *distributed* component, supported only as a target. `SECRET_STORE=openbao` **replaces `redis`** — the plaintext store was the configured default of the published eval stack, i.e. evaluators were putting real warehouse credentials into an unencrypted key-value store. **Redis stays** (Celery broker + ADR 0035 rate limits). Two defects the review caught are worth carrying forward: **an outage must never be reportable as a state** — every caller branches on the exception TYPE and none reads the message, so folding "vault sealed" into `SecretNotFoundError` made an admin page render "not set" and silently skipped alert delivery (`AzureKeyVaultStore` had shipped that since Week 2); and a **`Settings` validator now fails a bad secret-store config at boot**, because the store built lazily and would otherwise die mid-run in a worker. Prod's 13 `conn-*` Key Vault keys were also renamed to one readable convention (`conn-<type>-<qualifier>-<env>-<shortid>`) — copy → read-back verify → repoint → re-test → purge, piloted on one connection first, 11/11 re-verified, and both Airflow connections verified on Key Vault **and** OpenBao. See [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). **DEPLOYED + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-19** (then `dff6d958`; prod redeployed to `c401572d` 2026-07-26; prod redeployed again to `bb40f0b7` 2026-08-03 — all three Container Apps (api/worker/frontend) rolled via the Deploy workflow ([run 30789647178](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/30789647178)), migrate job Succeeded, post-deploy smoke green (healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401 gates hold, authenticated `/me` verified, beat+watchdog clean on the new revision); **prod redeployed to `7018d772` 2026-08-08** — the 2026-08-08 session's eleven merges (#1185/#1188–#1192/#1194/#1198/#1201/#1204 — six-issue fix batch incl. the UC custom-SQL fix, identifier-column display, batch-target UI) rolled via [run 31261342996](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31261342996), migrate no-op (no schema change), full smoke green + a UC suite run 7/7 on the new revisions — see below): the W4 work is on prod and exercised against real datasources. **Prod redeployed to `f637a18e` 2026-08-09** — a full real-user pre-deploy QA pass (2 fresh OTP users, all 4 datasource types, deliberate PASS/FAIL/ERROR + edge-case scenarios via Playwright, no DB shortcuts) found and fixed a live, pre-existing production defect: **#1273** — `decimal.Decimal` values in a legitimately-failed Snowflake/UC NUMERIC-column check crashed the entire result's JSONB insert (`sanitize_json` had no `Decimal` branch), silently discarding the run's results; a passing check on the same column never surfaces the bug, which is why it went unnoticed since `jsonsafe.py` shipped. Fixed in [#1276](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1276) mirroring the file's existing numpy/pandas coercion pattern; mutation-verified regression tests + a live pre/post-fix repro against real Snowflake data. Two more findings filed, both non-blocking: [#1274](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1274) (Iceberg over S3-compatible storage — pyarrow's own S3 client rejects credentials boto3 accepts; scoped to non-ADLS Iceberg backends, likely not this deployment) and [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation warnings, cosmetic). Also attempted to resolve the user-reported "columns still stretched" report — **that diagnosis was wrong and is corrected below** ([#1282](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1282)): the claim recorded here was that [#1184](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1184)'s own fix was already live and only [#1208](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1208) (the RunDetail "Observed" column) was undeployed. Both halves were false. The user re-reported the stretched columns against this very deploy, and pulling the live prod chunks settled it: **both fixes were in the shipped bundle and neither had ever worked, in any environment.** Every DataQ table renders `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, which rc-table turns into `width: max-content` on the `<table>`; an intrinsic-sizing keyword sizes the table from its content, neutering `table-layout: fixed` and demoting the `<colgroup>` width to a non-binding hint — so a column's `width` + `ellipsis` are **inert**, and a long ADF error rendered ~1917px wide against a declared 260px. The covering test asserted `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — true, and meaningless, because jsdom performs no layout. Fixed by bounding the **inner element** (`boundedTextStyle`) rather than the column, with the regression assertion moved to Playwright where widths can actually be measured. **Standing practice this produced: "merged" is not "deployed", and "deployed" is not "works" — verify a fix against the running artifact AND against observed behavior before reporting it as done.** Rolled via [run 31342076551](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31342076551), migrate job Succeeded, post-deploy smoke green (healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401 gates hold, `/docs` serves the SPA shell not Swagger, authenticated `/me` verified, beat+watchdog clean, Key Vault secret store initialized on the new revision) — **plus a live suite run** ("Snowflake — Orders (all paths)", 7 checks, 6 pass/1 fail/1 skip, `succeeded`) confirming the #1273 fix holds against real prod data. **Prod redeployed twice more the same day — to `77068358`, then to `eba60b4d` (current)** ([run 31347217502](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31347217502), [run 31350288817](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31350288817)); both migrate jobs no-op (zero migration files in either delta), both smokes green, and the fixes **verified in the running artifact and in the browser**, not merely merged: the deployed chunk `ellipsisColumn-*.js` carries `boundedTextStyle`, and the Failure-reason cell that had rendered ~1917px now measures 260px with 3423px of content clipped, Observed 220px, the pipeline table 1379px instead of 2969px. The second roll carried two post-deploy-smoke findings from the first: **#1286** (the fix’s own regression — a 150px bound wrapped the copy button and grew every pipeline-runs row 56px→77px; measured the threshold on live prod and shipped 120) and **#1285** (pre-existing — orchestration poll failures were classified through the datasource message set, so both Airflow connections said “missing warehouse or role … check the suite’s run target” while the harness Airflow app was simply Stopped; an orchestration connection has none of those four things). Both confirmed live afterwards: 20/20 Provider-run cells clipped at 120px with a uniform 56px row height, and the 02:51Z poll wrote the new orchestration-shaped reason. A live suite run on each revision (8 checks) confirmed the worker path against real Snowflake. **Verification lesson from this session, now standing practice: “merged” is not “deployed”, and “deployed” is not “works” — a stale-looking grep in the wrong chunk nearly produced a second wrong answer, and the first poll after the roll still showed the old message because the draining revision served it.** Orchestration (Airflow trigger → poll → dispatch) was also verified end-to-end in the local harness this session, after fixing a stale `DATAQ_LOADER`-scoped Snowflake credential in the harness's own (untracked, separate-repo) local stack — see [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). **ADLS** — volume read 643 rows off the resolved batch and arrival-time freshness reported 531.8h from the blob's last-modified: the harness genuinely stopped producing, which is precisely the incident #520 exists to catch and which an in-file MAX cannot see. **Snowflake** — `order_ts` (lower-case, emitted unquoted so the warehouse folds it) and `ORDER_TS` (upper-case, now quoted) returned **identical** timestamps, proving #937 both fixes mixed case and preserves the fold; volume over 32,840 real rows. **Unity Catalog** — freshness works **for the first time ever** (239.06h, lower/UPPER identical, confirming the backtick dialect). The dimension backfill (#952) classified **all 30 real prod checks, zero unclassified**, and real asset scorecards show genuine signal. **Live testing found a bug three green suites could not: UC freshness had NEVER worked** (#953) — the Databricks connector returns a TIMESTAMP's MAX as a **str** and the age math accepted only datetime/date, so a datasource the feature matrix marks ✅ produced no reading since #426. No unit test could see it: the type comes from the **driver**, and every fixture hands in a real datetime — the same fixture-encodes-our-model shape as #823 and the #520 Parquet bug. **Lesson: for anything whose type or value crosses a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence.** Also filed [#954](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/954): two prod Snowflake PATs are dead, and a **datasource** connection with a dead credential has no visible state until a run fails — I had to read worker logs to find out why, since #839's health signal covers only *orchestration* connections. That is the #828 blindness in a new place. **W4 CLOSED 2026-07-19, 8/8** — `schema_drift` (#592) shipped 2026-07-17, and this session cleared the remaining four in two groups. **Flat-file (#476, #520):** every backend CSV read hardcoded the pandas default comma, so a `;`/tab/pipe file parsed as ONE column named after the whole header — silently; all four reads now share one sniffing seam ([#934](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/934)). #476's casing half was **relocated by checking the code instead of the ticket** — the profiler's Core builders already quoted correctly; the only unquoted path was `monitors.py`'s f-string, fixed by returning a Core `Select` so the CONNECTION's dialect quotes it ([#937](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/937)); hand-rolled `"` quoting would have been actively wrong on UC, which uses backticks. Flat files gained freshness/volume monitors incl. **arrival-time freshness** — the case a warehouse can't express, since an in-file MAX is blind to a producer that stopped sending files ([#940](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/940)). **Dimension & score (#124, #889):** ADR [0038](docs/adr/0038-dq-dimension-classification.md) — seven canonical dimensions, closed vocabulary, derived default → stored → overridable, derivation deliberately partial so **NULL means unclassified and renders as a coverage gap** ([#945](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/945)); then `services/rollup.py` as the one histogram + score + latest-run query ([#948](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/948)) and the asset scorecard on top ([#950](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/950)).

**The lesson of the week is one shape, seen five times: a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing, and "passes" is not "passes for the right reason."** (1) #520's Parquet freshness was broken on **every** Parquet file — Arrow-backed timestamps make `is_datetime64_any_dtype` False — and the suite was green because every fixture hand-built a numpy frame (#823 shape). (2) #124's export/import **silently classified every check in prod**, an ADR violation inside the PR that added the ADR; the tests missed it *by construction* — one POPPED the key rather than setting it null, and the only null that round-tripped was custom SQL, where derivation *also* returns `None`. (3) #889's `uncovered` meant "no results", not "no checks", so a check authored today read as missing until its next run — green because every fixture seeded a check AND a result together. (4) The #948 tie-break test was a **coin flip** (`max()` over random UUIDs matches the arbitrary answer ~50% of the time); I had "verified" it once and got lucky. (5) A `defaultdict` whose read created keys defeated my own mutation check for (3). **Mutation-checking every regression test is now the habit** — it caught (5), and (4) was caught by a reviewer doing it for me. Also recorded: the UI found two defects tests could not — a card asserting what the field below it denied, and a "Not covered" list hidden in exactly the state where it mattered most.

description: "AWS parallel-deployment track — APPLIED AND LIVE 2026-08-15 (CloudFront + ECS + RDS + ElastiCache + Cognito, sign-in live-verified); next = deploy-aws.yml workflow, #1355 origin secret, #1338 runbook docs"

**What this is:** DataQ running in parallel on a from-scratch AWS account (`us-east-2`, dedicated, `AWS_PROFILE=dataq-deploy`); Azure stays primary prod. Stack: `deploy/terraform/aws/` (OpenTofu, ADR 0024 conventions).

## State as of 2026-08-15 (apply session)

**LIVE.** `tofu apply` completed — 54 resources: VPC/no-NAT, ECS Fargate api (internal, Cloud Map `api.dataq.local`) + worker (embedded beat, desired=1) + frontend, RDS `db.t4g.micro`, ElastiCache `cache.t4g.micro` (TLS+auth), Cognito pool `us-east-2_ET9Q8FMe1` + SPA client, Secrets Manager (infra bootstrap + app runtime grant), GitHub OIDC deploy role, **CloudFront `d29cc3r7frs6eb.cloudfront.net`** = the HTTPS public surface (distribution `E19W6CPQ40J7EH`; ALB SG admits only CloudFront origin-facing prefix list). Images pinned at apply: `main-724e1b23…` (both). Migrate task ran `alembic upgrade head` (exit 0). Smoke green: healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401, `/config.js` full OIDC contract.

**Pre-apply review batch (all merged same day):** #1345→PR#1352 (CloudFront — Cognito requires HTTPS redirect URIs; callback = `https://<dist>/` root-with-slash, matching the SPA; XFF trusted hops 1→3), #1346→PR#1350 (**userinfo fallback** — Cognito access tokens carry NO `email`/`aud`; both REST + MCP validators fall back to the issuer's userinfo endpoint, shared SHA-256-keyed TTL cache, fail-closed on outage, sub-match check; review added `_json_dict` non-object-200 guard + cache lock + discovery memoization), #1347→PR#1351 (`DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE` runtime override — Cognito rejects `offline_access` with `invalid_scope`; AWS sets `openid email profile`), #1348→PR#1353 (deploy IAM: `ecs:cluster` condition denies task-definition actions — split; RegisterTaskDefinition family-scoped to `task-definition/dataq-app-*`), #1349→PR#1354 (ALB health check `/healthz`→`/` — nginx proxies healthz to the api; image tags now REQUIRED vars, format `main-<sha of last image-bearing main commit>`, verify with `docker manifest inspect` — bare `<sha>` tags don't exist, docs-only tips have no image).

**Apply-time find:** #1357 — EC2 SG descriptions allow ONLY `a-zA-Z0-9. _-:/()#,@[]+=&;{}!$*` (`tofu validate` can't see API-side constraints); bit TWICE (em-dashes #1358, then `>` #1359). Partial applies are safe — state intact, re-apply continues.

**Live-verified (the #953 rule, discharged):** real browser Cognito sign-in via hosted UI → `/dashboard`; decoded access token had no `email`, no `aud` (only `client_id`, `token_use=access`) yet `/me` returned correct email + display name + `is_workspace_admin=true` — proving the userinfo fallback, scope override, HTTPS callback chain, and #1340's `client_id`-vs-`aud` accommodation on a real token.

**Operational facts:**
- Cognito user `royarijit1995@gmail.com` exists (email_verified, name "Arijit Roy"); test password was rotated to a random value after the test — user should self-reset via the hosted UI's Forgot password (Cognito default email works for verified addresses).
- `terraform.tfvars` (gitignored) holds `state_encryption_passphrase` — **user must back it up off-machine; losing it makes tfstate unrecoverable.** DB password: in encrypted state + Secrets Manager only.
- GitHub wired: secret `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, vars `ECS_CLUSTER=dataq-app`, `AWS_REGION=us-east-2`.

**Done — all five findings fixed, re-tested, the AWS stack is applied, and DataQ is live on AWS with a real Cognito sign-in verified end-to-end.**

## The deployment

- **Public URL:** `https://d29cc3r7frs6eb.cloudfront.net` (CloudFront default cert — read it anytime with `tofu output frontend_url`)
- 54 resources in `us-east-2`: ECS Fargate api/worker/frontend (images `main-724e1b23`), RDS, ElastiCache, Cognito, Secrets Manager, GitHub OIDC deploy role, CloudFront fronting the ALB (whose SG admits only CloudFront origin-facing ranges)
- Migrate task ran `alembic upgrade head` clean (exit 0, through the new `users.oidc_issuer` migration); all three services steady
- Smoke green: healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api` + `/mcp` both 401 unauthenticated, `/config.js` serving the full OIDC contract

## The fixes (one PR per issue, all reviewed at low effort, all merged)

| Issue | PR | What shipped |
|---|---|---|
| #1345 HTTPS callback | [#1352](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1352) | CloudFront front (your call), ALB locked to CloudFront ranges, callback URLs corrected to the SPA's real `origin/` shape, XFF hops 1→3 |
| #1346 no email claim | [#1350](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1350) | userinfo-endpoint fallback in both REST + MCP validators, hashed-key TTL cache, fail-closed on outage, OIDC sub check |
| #1347 offline_access | [#1351](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1351) | `DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE` runtime override (AWS sets `openid email profile`); Azure unchanged |
| #1348 IAM deny | [#1353](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1353) | condition split; review tightened `RegisterTaskDefinition` to `dataq-app-*` families |
| #1349 health/images | [#1354](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1354) | health check `/healthz`→`/`; image tags now required, with a GHCR-verified `main-<sha>` recipe |

The reviews earned their keep: they caught a 500-class hole in my own userinfo fix (non-JSON 200 escaping the outage guard), proved against live GHCR that my first image-tag recipe pointed at nonexistent tags, and corrected an IAM overclaim against the AWS Service Authorization Reference. The apply itself surfaced one more only-live-can-see bug — EC2's SG-description charset (#1357, bit twice: em-dashes, then `>`) — fixed in #1358/#1359.

## The live verification (the part validate/plan can never give you)

A real browser sign-in through the Cognito hosted UI landed on `/dashboard`, and the decoded access token confirmed the review's central prediction: **it carries no `email` and no `aud`** — yet `/me` returned `royarijit1995@gmail.com`, "Arijit Roy", `is_workspace_admin: true`. That's the userinfo fallback, the scope override, the HTTPS callback chain, and the `client_id`-vs-`aud` accommodation all proven on real tokens. Verification comments posted on #1345–#1347.

## Two things you need to do

1. **Back up the state-encryption passphrase** in `deploy/terraform/aws/terraform.tfvars` (gitignored) somewhere off this machine — it can't be re-minted, and losing it makes the state unrecoverable.
2. **Your Cognito account** (`royarijit1995@gmail.com`) exists but I rotated the test password to a random value after the browser test (it had appeared in the session transcript). Use "Forgot password" on the sign-in page to set your own.

## What's next (not in today's scope)

`deploy-aws.yml` (the IAM role + `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`/`ECS_CLUSTER`/`AWS_REGION` are already wired), #1355 (CloudFront origin secret), #1338 (runbook doc), confirming XFF hops against one live log line, and configuring a datasource + running a real suite to exercise the AWS worker path. Docs (progress.md + CLAUDE.md headline) and memory are updated; repo has zero open PRs.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - DataQ: FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL platform; Azure ACA is primary prod; AWS is a new parallel deployment (dedicated account 251783195294, us-east-2, AWS_PROFILE=dataq-deploy)
   - OpenTofu (`tofu`, not Terraform — ADR 0024/BUSL); local state with pbkdf2/AES-GCM encryption (passphrase in gitignored terraform.tfvars, unrecoverable if lost — user must back up off-machine)
   - Provider-neutral OIDC (`OidcBearerScheme`, ADR 0026 amendment): OIDC discovery + PyJWT/JWKS, RS256-only, manual audience check with Cognito `client_id`-vs-`aud` accommodation
   - Cognito facts verified live: access tokens carry NO `email`, NO `aud` (only `sub`/`client_id`/`token_use`/`scope`); redirect URIs must be HTTPS except localhost; `offline_access` is not a Cognito scope (invalid_scope); refresh tokens issued on code grant regardless
   - Userinfo endpoint fallback: fetch identity claims when token lacks email; SHA-256-keyed bounded TTL cache (300s/1024 max); fail-closed on outage (empty-email upsert poisons `uq_users_email_lower` — second user 409s forever); OIDC Core §5.3.2 sub-match check
   - `DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE` runtime contract addition (ADR 0028): full scope-string override for providers rejecting the default `openid profile email offline_access [apiScope]`
   - CloudFront as HTTPS front (default *.cloudfront.net cert, CachingDisabled + AllViewer managed policies, 60s origin timeouts, PriceClass_100); ALB SG restricted to `com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing` managed prefix list
   - XFF trusted hops = 3 on AWS (CloudFront + ALB + nginx each append; `entries[len - hops]` semantics in rate_limit.py)
   - EC2 SG description charset: ONLY `a-zA-Z0-9. _-:/()#,@[]+=&;{}!$*` — no em-dash, no `>`; `tofu validate` cannot catch API-side constraints
   - Image tagging: publish-images.yml tags main merges `main-<full sha>` (bare `<sha>` belongs to Azure deploy.yml only); paths filter skips docs-only merges — use last image-bearing commit + `docker manifest inspect` verification
   - IAM: `ecs:cluster` condition key not populated by RegisterTaskDefinition/DescribeTaskDefinition (→ implicit deny); RegisterTaskDefinition DOES support resource-level scoping (`task-definition/dataq-app-*`); DescribeTaskDefinition needs `*`
   - Project conventions: one functionality per commit/PR, `Fixes #N`, /code-review (low effort) on every PR, fixup commits (never force-push), squash-merge after CI green, docs/progress.md Snapshot update per merge, findings end "fixed or filed", #953 rule (driver-boundary claims need live verification)

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **backend/app/core/auth.py** (PR #1350 + fixup): Added `_json_dict(response)` (raises ValueError on non-JSON-object 200 bodies — used by discovery, userinfo both paths, AND `_refresh_jwks`); `discover_oidc_config(issuer)` (full discovery doc; `discover_jwks_uri` now wraps it); `_cached_discovery(issuer)` (per-issuer memo); `_userinfo_cache`/`_discovery_cache` guarded by `_oidc_cache_lock = threading.Lock()`; `_userinfo_cache_get/put` keyed by `hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()` with TTL 300s, max 1024, expired-then-oldest eviction; `_merge_userinfo(claims, userinfo)` (returns None on sub mismatch, fills email/name); `fetch_userinfo(issuer, token)` (sync, for MCP; returns None when no userinfo_endpoint, raises httpx.HTTPError/ValueError on outage/malformed); `OidcBearerScheme` gained `_userinfo_endpoint` from `load_config` (via `asyncio.to_thread(_cached_discovery, ...)`) and in `_verify` after aud check:
     ```python
     if not claims.get("email") and self._userinfo_endpoint is not None:
         userinfo = _userinfo_cache_get(token)
         if userinfo is None:
             try:
                 response = await self._client.get(self._userinfo_endpoint, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
                 response.raise_for_status()
                 userinfo = _json_dict(response)
             except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) as exc:
                 log.warning("oidc_userinfo_unavailable", issuer=self._issuer, error=str(exc))
                 return None
             _userinfo_cache_put(token, userinfo)
         merged = _merge_userinfo(claims, userinfo)
         if merged is None:
             log.warning("oidc_userinfo_sub_mismatch", issuer=self._issuer)
             return None
         claims = merged
     ```

Imports `httpx`, `_merge_userinfo`, `fetch_userinfo`.

# ALB behind CloudFront (#1345) — CloudFront is the sole public surface
# (ADR 0028 §5's api-goes-internal posture, one hop further out). Only the
# frontend target group exists; api/worker have no ALB listener and are
# reached only via Cloud Map internal DNS (ecs.tf).
#
# The listener stays plain HTTP :80: TLS terminates at CloudFront (Cognito
# requires an HTTPS redirect URI, and there is no custom domain — see
# cloudfront.tf). The security group admits only CloudFront's origin-facing
# ranges (AWS-managed prefix list), so the ALB is not reachable from an
# arbitrary internet address. Stated honestly: those ranges are shared by ALL
# CloudFront distributions, so a third party could still origin-point their
# own distribution at this ALB's (discoverable) DNS name; what that yields is
# plain-HTTP origin access through their edge — no auth bypass (the app
# validates Cognito tokens itself) and no XFF spoofing (the trusted-hops
# depth counts appends, which their edge also performs). Full closure is a
# secret custom origin header verified at nginx — follow-up #1355.

# AWS-managed, auto-updated list of CloudFront origin-facing IP ranges.
data "aws_ec2_managed_prefix_list" "cloudfront_origin" {
  name = "com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing"
}

resource "aws_security_group" "alb" {
  name        = "dataq-app-alb"
  description = "ALB - inbound HTTP from CloudFront origin-facing ranges only"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id

  ingress {
    description     = "HTTP from CloudFront"
    from_port       = 80
    to_port         = 80
    protocol        = "tcp"
    prefix_list_ids = [data.aws_ec2_managed_prefix_list.cloudfront_origin.id]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-alb" }
}

resource "aws_lb" "app" {
  name               = "dataq-app"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "application"
  subnets            = aws_subnet.public[*].id
  security_groups    = [aws_security_group.alb.id]

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-alb" }
}

resource "aws_lb_target_group" "frontend" {
  name        = "dataq-app-frontend"
  port        = 8080
  protocol    = "HTTP"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
  target_type = "ip" # required for Fargate tasks (no EC2 instance id)

  health_check {
    # `/` (the SPA index), NOT `/healthz` — nginx PROXIES /healthz to the api,
    # so checking it here made frontend target health mean "the api is up":
    # an api outage would have had the ALB recycling perfectly healthy
    # frontend tasks in a loop, masking the real failure (#1349). `/` is
    # served by nginx locally; frontend health now means "nginx + bundle up".
    # The api's own health stays observable via its ECS service + /healthz
    # through the site.
    path                = "/"
    healthy_threshold   = 2
    unhealthy_threshold = 3
    interval            = 15
    timeout             = 5
  }

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-frontend" }
}

resource "aws_lb_listener" "http" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.app.arn
  port              = 80
  protocol          = "HTTP"

  default_action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.frontend.arn
  }
}

locals {
  # No custom domain yet — CloudFront's own domain is the deployment's public
  # HTTPS URL (#1345). Depends only on the distribution (which depends only on
  # the ALB), so nothing later in the graph waits on the ECS service itself —
  # mirroring the Azure stack's deterministic-FQDN trick that breaks the
  # frontend<->api circular dependency.
  frontend_url     = "https://${aws_cloudfront_distribution.app.domain_name}"
  api_internal_url = "http://api.dataq.local:8000"
}

# DataQ frontend image — build the Vite SPA, serve the static dist via nginx.
# Build context = frontend/ :  docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile frontend/
#
# ONE generic image, nothing baked in (ADR 0028): no cloud, no secret, no
# auth-bypass. Auth config is injected at RUNTIME — nginx serves /config.js from
# the DATAQ_AUTH_* env below (envsubst at startup), and the SPA reads it before
# the bundle runs. So the same image serves the eval stack (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass)
# and a real deployment (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc + authority/clientId/scope) — set the
# env at `docker run`, no rebuild. Replaces the #472 two-image (:latest/:dev) split.
#
# The deploy workflow builds + pushes this image and rolls the `dataq-app-frontend`
# Container App (ADR 0028 §5 cutover — the Static Web App is gone; SWA couldn't
# inject runtime config). See deploy/terraform/azure/frontend.tf.

# Pin the build stage to the native BUILD platform (amd64 on CI runners) even for
# an arm64 target image: a Vite SPA compiles to architecture-independent static
# assets, so there's no reason to run `pnpm build` under arm64 QEMU emulation — it
# only made the multi-arch publish pathologically slow / flaky (12min good case →
# 45min stall, #512). buildx cross-builds: this stage runs native, and only the
# tiny per-arch nginx `serve` stage below is built for each target platform, with
# the arch-independent dist COPYed in. $BUILDPLATFORM is a buildx-predefined arg.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
RUN corepack enable

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

COPY . .
RUN pnpm build

FROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve
# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages, lets the
# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push it, and inherits anonymous-pull visibility —
# ADR 0023, mirrors backend/Dockerfile).
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ frontend (React SPA served by nginx)"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
# Template (not a static conf): the nginx entrypoint envsubst's it at startup so
# the API upstream + auth config are runtime-configurable.
COPY nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template
# Opt into the nginx image's built-in resolver detection: its
# 15-local-resolvers.envsh only exports ${NGINX_LOCAL_RESOLVERS} (the
# /etc/resolv.conf nameservers, used by the proxy `resolver` directive) when this
# flag is set. Cloud-neutral (ADR 0028) — no resolver IP baked in; works in
# compose (127.0.0.11) and ACA/K8s (cluster DNS) alike.
ENV NGINX_ENTRYPOINT_LOCAL_RESOLVERS=1
# Runtime config env (ADR 0028) — MUST be defined (even if empty) so envsubst
# always substitutes them in /config.js; empty → SPA is unconfigured (fail-closed),
# bypass needs an explicit DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass. DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM defaults to
# the compose `api` service.
ENV DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api:8000 \
    DATAQ_AUTH_MODE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE=""
EXPOSE 8080

# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

# ElastiCache Redis — AWS-native managed Redis for the Celery broker + rate
# limits (ADR 0035). Decision: managed ElastiCache, not self-hosted-on-Fargate
# like the Azure stack's Redis Container App — the user's explicit choice for
# the AWS deployment (see the approved plan's cost note: a few dollars/month
# more than self-hosting, ongoing).
#
# aws_elasticache_replication_group (not aws_elasticache_cluster): the
# replication-group resource is what actually supports auth_token +
# transit_encryption_enabled cleanly. One node, no read replica — this is a
# single Celery broker, not a fan-out cache.

resource "aws_elasticache_subnet_group" "app" {
  name       = "dataq-app-redis"
  subnet_ids = aws_subnet.public[*].id
}

resource "aws_security_group" "redis" {
  name        = "dataq-app-redis"
  description = "Redis - inbound only from the ECS tasks security group"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id

  ingress {
    description     = "Redis from ECS tasks"
    from_port       = 6379
    to_port         = 6379
    protocol        = "tcp"
    security_groups = [aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-redis" }
}

# ElastiCache auth_token: 16-128 printable ASCII chars, excluding '/', '"',
# '@'. `special = false` sidesteps the excluded-character set entirely rather
# than trying to allow-list a safe subset.
resource "random_password" "redis_auth" {
  length  = 32
  special = false
}

resource "aws_elasticache_replication_group" "app" {
  replication_group_id = "dataq-app"
  description          = "DataQ Celery broker + rate-limit store"
  engine               = "redis"
  engine_version       = "7.1"
  node_type            = "cache.t4g.micro"
  num_cache_clusters   = 1
  port                 = 6379

  subnet_group_name  = aws_elasticache_subnet_group.app.name
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.redis.id]

  # TLS + password required together — same defense-in-depth posture as the
  # Azure stack's self-hosted Redis (--requirepass over an internal-only
  # ingress). transit_encryption_enabled is what makes auth_token usable at
  # all on this resource.
  transit_encryption_enabled = true
  auth_token                 = random_password.redis_auth.result

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-redis" }
}

locals {
  # rediss:// (TLS) scheme — transit_encryption_enabled requires TLS
  # connections; redis-py/celery both understand the scheme.
  redis_url = "REDACTED"
}

  --title "AWS worker crash-loops: Celery rejects the ElastiCache rediss:// URL without ssl_cert_reqs" \
  --label "bug,deployment" \
  --body "## What
The AWS stack's \`dataq-app-worker\` ECS service has been crash-looping since the 2026-08-15 apply (25+ stopped tasks, exit 1). The api and frontend are healthy, so the post-apply smoke (healthz/SPA/auth gates) never saw it — the worker has **never** successfully started on AWS.

## Root cause
\`deploy/terraform/aws/elasticache.tf\` builds \`REDIS_URL\` as \`rediss://:<auth>@<endpoint>:6379/0\`. Celery's redis result backend hard-fails on a \`rediss://\` URL that lacks an explicit \`ssl_cert_reqs\` query parameter:

\`\`\`
Unrecoverable error: ValueError('A rediss:// URL must have parameter ssl_cert_reqs and this must be set to CERT_REQUIRED, CERT_OPTIONAL, or CERT_NONE')
\`\`\`

(celery 5.6.3, \`celery/backends/redis.py:296\`.) The same URL feeds the api's Celery **producer**, so the first suite dispatch on the api would hit the identical error — every async path on AWS is dead, not just the worker.

Kombu also logs \"Secure redis scheme specified (rediss) with no ssl options, defaulting to insecure SSL behaviour\" for the broker side — i.e. without the param the broker connection wouldn't verify the server cert either.

## Why validate/plan/smoke missed it
API-side/runtime-only: the URL is syntactically valid, tofu can't see it, and the smoke checked only the public surface. Same class as #1357 — only a live run is evidence (#953 rule).

## Fix
Append \`?ssl_cert_reqs=required\` to the URL in \`elasticache.tf\`. Verified against the pinned versions that all three consumers accept the lowercase spelling: celery 5.6.3 maps it to \`ssl.CERT_REQUIRED\`, redis-py 5.3.1 accepts it in \`from_url\`, kombu 5.6.2 parses it. ElastiCache serves an Amazon-CA cert, so full verification (\`required\`) works with system CAs — no reason to weaken it.

Then \`tofu apply\` (updates the Secrets Manager \`redis-url\` version in place) + force a new deployment of api and worker so tasks re-resolve the secret." 2>&1 | tail -2

2. **Docs** — deployment guide env-var reference for \`REDIS_URL\` states the rule + the exact celery error string for searchability, plus a troubleshooting entry.

from backend.app.services import connection_service as svc

router = APIRouter(tags=["connections"])


class ConnectionCreate(ApiModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    type: str
    env: str
    config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    secret: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Credential; write-only, never returned")
    catalog_secret: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Second credential a connection type may need (currently the Iceberg "
            "SQL-catalog DB password, #1181); write-only, never returned"
        ),
    )


class ConnectionUpdate(ApiModel):
    name: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=128)
    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    secret: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Rotate the credential; write-only")
    catalog_secret: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Rotate the second (catalog) credential; write-only"
    )


class ConnectionRead(ApiModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: uuid.UUID
    name: str
    type: str
    env: str
    config: dict[str, Any]
    has_secret: bool
    created_by: uuid.UUID

    # Poll health (#828) — orchestration connections only; NULL/0 elsewhere. A failing
    # poll used to live purely in the logs, so a dead integration looked identical to a
    # healthy-but-quiet one. `last_poll_error` is a CLASSIFIED reason, never raw
    # exception text (which can carry a SAS/DSN/token).
    last_polled_at: datetime | None = None
    last_poll_error: str | None = None
    consecutive_poll_failures: int = 0

    # Run-derived health (#954) — DATASOURCE connections. Nothing polls a
    # datasource, so a dead credential used to be invisible until a run failed,

class SuiteTarget(ApiModel):
    """Datasource-shaped run target (#215) — which table / flat-file path / Unity
    Catalog name the suite's checks run against. Same shape as the column-profiler
    request; `run_target.resolve_target` validates the right fields per connection
    type (`table` for SQL, `path` for flat files, `catalog` for Unity Catalog).

    A flat-file target can instead select a **batch** of files: `pattern` (a regex
    whose first capture group is the batch key) + `strategy` (`latest`/`specific`,
    with `batch` for `specific`) + optional `prefix` (A4). The exact field
    combination is validated by `run_target.resolve_target` per connection type, so
    those rules live in one place — this model only declares the storable keys."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    table: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="schema", max_length=255)
    catalog: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    # Iceberg addresses a table by ``namespace.table``; run_target folds it in.
    namespace: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    path: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024)
    file_format: Literal["csv", "parquet"] | None = None
    # Flat-file batch selection (A4); validated in run_target, not here.
    pattern: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024)
    strategy: Literal["latest", "specific"] | None = None
    batch: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    prefix: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024)
    # Scale-aware execution (#595): bound what a run materialises. Accepted only
    # on the full-load datasources — `run_target.resolve_target` refuses it
    # elsewhere with a 422 rather than ignoring it.
    sampling: SuiteSampling | None = None

input.command:
gh issue create \
  --title "AWS/Cognito: Sign out lands on Cognito error page 'Client does not exist' (400)" \
  --label "bug,priority/P2" \
  --body "Found during the 2026-08-15 AWS E2E while switching users on the live AWS deployment.

**Repro:** signed-in user → avatar menu → Sign out. The SPA's oidc-client-ts \`signoutRedirect()\` follows the discovery document's \`end_session_endpoint\` and lands on:

\`\`\`
https://dataq-app-l4y8n8.auth.us-east-2.amazoncognito.com/error?error=Client+does+not+exist   (HTTP 400)
\`\`\`

**Impact:** the *local* session IS cleared (oidc-client-ts removes the stored user before redirecting, and a subsequent visit shows the sign-in page), but (a) the user is dumped on a raw Cognito error page instead of returning to the app, and (b) the **Cognito hosted-UI session cookie is NOT terminated** — clicking Sign in again silently re-authenticates as the old user without a password prompt. On a shared machine that second half is a real logout-doesn't-log-out defect.

**Suspected cause:** Cognito's \`/logout\` endpoint is not OIDC RP-Initiated-Logout-conformant — it requires \`client_id\` + \`logout_uri\` (which must exactly match one of the app client's \`logout_urls\`), while oidc-client-ts sends the standard \`id_token_hint\` + \`post_logout_redirect_uri\`. Azure AD accepts the standard params, which is why this never showed on the primary deployment.

**Likely fix (frontend, provider-neutral):** in the auth client's sign-out path, when the authority's end-session call needs it, pass \`extraQueryParams: { client_id, logout_uri }\` (oidc-client-ts supports \`signoutRedirect({ extraQueryParams })\`) — or build the logout URL from config when \`end_session_endpoint\` is Cognito-shaped. Must stay generic per ADR 0028 (no Cognito branching on issuer hostname without a config flag).

The Terraform side is already correct: \`logout_urls = [\"<frontend_url>/\"]\` is set on the app client." 2>&1 | tail -1

3	# Manual-only for now (workflow_dispatch): apply-ready scaffolding that never
4	# fires on its own until the Azure resources exist + secrets/vars are set. Once
5	# the infra is provisioned (see deploy/README.md), flip on the push trigger:
6	#   push:
7	#     branches: [main]
8	on:
9	  workflow_dispatch:
10	    inputs:
11	      image_tag:
12	        description: "Image tag to build + deploy (blank → the commit SHA, an immutable tag)"
13	        default: ""
14	
15	concurrency:
16	  group: deploy-production
17	  cancel-in-progress: false
18	
19	# OIDC federated login to Azure (no stored client secret). The federated cred +
20	# the listed vars/secrets must be configured first — see deploy/README.md.
21	# packages:write lets the GITHUB_TOKEN push the backend image to GHCR (ADR 0023).
22	permissions:
23	  id-token: write
24	  contents: read
25	  packages: write
26	
27	env:
28	  # GHCR registry (ADR 0023) — public packages, lowercase owner. ACA pulls them
29	  # anonymously, so no registry credential is stored on the apps/job.
30	  #
31	  # Default the tag to the commit SHA (#382): `latest` is mutable, so a push
32	  # racing the deploy could make the migrate job, API, worker, and frontend each
33	  # resolve a *different* image; the SHA tag is immutable, so all roll the exact
34	  # build this run produced. A manual `image_tag` input still overrides it. On a
35	  # push:[main] trigger `inputs` is empty, so it falls back to the SHA too. Backend
36	  # + frontend share the one tag.
37	  IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag || github.sha }}
38	  IMAGE_FRONTEND: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || github.sha }}
39	
40	jobs:
41	  backend:
42	    name: Backend — build, migrate, deploy (API + worker)
43	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
44	    environment: production
45	    steps:
46	      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
47	
48	      # Fail fast on unset repo vars (#539 post-mortem): an empty --name reaches
49	      # ARM and the containerapp extension masks the 4xx as KeyError:
50	      # 'properties' — four deploys failed before --debug exposed that
51	      # FRONTEND_APP_NAME was simply never configured. Never let an empty var
52	      # masquerade as a transient again.
53	      - name: Preflight — required repo vars
54	        run: |
55	          set -euo pipefail
56	          fail=0
57	          for pair in "AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP=${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
58	                      "API_APP_NAME=${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
59	                      "WORKER_APP_NAME=${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
60	                      "MIGRATE_JOB_NAME=${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}"; do
61	            [[ -n "${pair#*=}" ]] || { echo "::error::repo variable ${pair%%=*} is not set"; fail=1; }
62	          done
63	          exit $fail
64	
65	      - name: Azure login (OIDC)
66	        uses: azure/login@v3

name: Deploy

# Manual-only for now (workflow_dispatch): apply-ready scaffolding that never
# fires on its own until the Azure resources exist + secrets/vars are set. Once
# the infra is provisioned (see deploy/README.md), flip on the push trigger:
#   push:
#     branches: [main]
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      image_tag:
        description: "Image tag to build + deploy (blank → the commit SHA, an immutable tag)"
        default: ""

concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

# OIDC federated login to Azure (no stored client secret). The federated cred +
# the listed vars/secrets must be configured first — see deploy/README.md.
# packages:write lets the GITHUB_TOKEN push the backend image to GHCR (ADR 0023).
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
  packages: write

env:
  # GHCR registry (ADR 0023) — public packages, lowercase owner. ACA pulls them
  # anonymously, so no registry credential is stored on the apps/job.
  #
  # Default the tag to the commit SHA (#382): `latest` is mutable, so a push
  # racing the deploy could make the migrate job, API, worker, and frontend each
  # resolve a *different* image; the SHA tag is immutable, so all roll the exact
  # build this run produced. A manual `image_tag` input still overrides it. On a
  # push:[main] trigger `inputs` is empty, so it falls back to the SHA too. Backend
  # + frontend share the one tag.
  IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag || github.sha }}
  IMAGE_FRONTEND: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || github.sha }}

jobs:
  backend:
    name: Backend — build, migrate, deploy (API + worker)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Fail fast on unset repo vars (#539 post-mortem): an empty --name reaches
      # ARM and the containerapp extension masks the 4xx as KeyError:
      # 'properties' — four deploys failed before --debug exposed that
      # FRONTEND_APP_NAME was simply never configured. Never let an empty var
      # masquerade as a transient again.
      - name: Preflight — required repo vars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          fail=0
          for pair in "AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP=${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
                      "API_APP_NAME=${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
                      "WORKER_APP_NAME=${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
                      "MIGRATE_JOB_NAME=${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}"; do
            [[ -n "${pair#*=}" ]] || { echo "::error::repo variable ${pair%%=*} is not set"; fail=1; }
          done
          exit $fail

      - name: Azure login (OIDC)
        uses: azure/login@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      # Push to GHCR (ADR 0023). The GITHUB_TOKEN has packages:write on this repo's
      # registry; no Azure/ACR credential is involved in the image push.
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Retried (#539): a registry blip on the base-image pull (Docker Hub 502,
      # Deploy #3) or on the GHCR push shouldn't fail the deploy — a re-run hits
      # the local layer cache, so retries are cheap.
      - name: Build + push backend image to GHCR
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          # && chain, not two statements: functions called from retry's
          # condition context have errexit suppressed inside, so a plain
          # sequence would still push after a failed build.
          build_push() {
            docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" . && docker push "$IMAGE"
          }
          retry build_push

      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-compatible
      # (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new schema. Runs the
      # one-off migrate Container Apps Job (provisioned per deploy/README.md).
      # `az containerapp job start` only *starts* the execution and returns, so we
      # capture the execution name and poll it to a terminal state — the rollout
      # below must not begin until the migration has actually SUCCEEDED, and a
      # failed migration must abort the deploy (fail-closed) rather than roll the
      # apps onto an un-migrated schema.
      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Roll the job's image on the template FIRST, then start it with no
          # --image override. Passing --image to `job start` replaces the
          # container template without the IaC-configured command
          # (`sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"`), so the execution
          # falls back to the image's default CMD (uvicorn) and never migrates.
          # Updating the template preserves that command (mirrors the api/worker
          # `az containerapp update --image` steps below).
          # Both az calls are retried (#539): the containerapp extension crashes
          # with KeyError: 'properties' on transient ARM errors, masking them.
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          retry az containerapp job update \
            --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --image "$IMAGE"
          exec_name=""
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            exec_name=$(az containerapp job start \
              --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
              --query name -o tsv) && break
            echo "::warning::job start failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in $(( attempt * 30 ))s (#539)"
            (( attempt < 3 )) && sleep $(( attempt * 30 ))
          done
          if [[ -z "$exec_name" ]]; then
            echo "::error::could not start the migration job after 3 attempts."; exit 1
          fi
          echo "Started migration execution: $exec_name"
          # Poll to a terminal state. Besides the 15-min wall-clock cap, bound the
          # number of *consecutive* empty/unexpected statuses: a control-plane
          # hiccup or a CLI status-field rename would otherwise leave the loop
          # polling a status it never recognises until the full deadline, tying up
          # the prod concurrency group with no signal (#397). A recognised
          # in-progress status resets the counter; `|| true` keeps a transient
          # query failure a retry (counted as unknown) rather than a hard step
          # abort under `set -e`.
          deadline=$(( SECONDS + 900 ))  # 15-minute cap
          unknown=0
          unknown_max=18  # ~3 min of consecutive empty/unexpected status → abort
          while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
            status=$(az containerapp job execution list \
              --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
              --query "[?name=='$exec_name'].properties.status | [0]" -o tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
            echo "migration status: ${status:-<pending>} (unknown streak: $unknown)"
            case "$status" in
              Succeeded) echo "Migration succeeded."; exit 0 ;;
              Failed|Degraded|Stopped) echo "::error::Migration $status — aborting before app rollout."; exit 1 ;;
              Running|Processing|Pending) unknown=0 ;;
              *)
                unknown=$(( unknown + 1 ))
                if (( unknown >= unknown_max )); then
                  echo "::error::Migration status empty/unexpected ('${status:-<empty>}') $unknown times in a row — aborting before app rollout."
                  exit 1
                fi
                ;;
            esac
            sleep 10
          done
          echo "::error::Timed out waiting for migration to complete."; exit 1

      # Both rolls are retried and then VERIFIED against the live template
      # (#539): the extension can crash while *rendering* a response, so the
      # step's exit code alone doesn't prove the app is on the new image.
      - name: Deploy API
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          retry az containerapp update \
            --name "${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --image "$IMAGE"
          live=$(az containerapp show \
            --name "${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --query "properties.template.containers[0].image" -o tsv)
          [[ "$live" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::API image mismatch after update: $live"; exit 1; }

      - name: Deploy worker
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          retry az containerapp update \
            --name "${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --image "$IMAGE"
          live=$(az containerapp show \
            --name "${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --query "properties.template.containers[0].image" -o tsv)
          [[ "$live" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::worker image mismatch after update: $live"; exit 1; }

  frontend:
    name: Frontend — build image, deploy to Container App
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed/aborted
    # migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against an un-rolled
    # or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).
    needs: backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Same fail-fast as the backend job (#539 post-mortem) — this is the var
      # whose absence burned deploys #1/#2/#4.
      - name: Preflight — required repo vars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          fail=0
          for pair in "AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP=${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
                      "FRONTEND_APP_NAME=${{ vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME }}"; do
            [[ -n "${pair#*=}" ]] || { echo "::error::repo variable ${pair%%=*} is not set"; fail=1; }
          done
          exit $fail

      - name: Azure login (OIDC)
        uses: azure/login@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # One generic image (ADR 0028) — nothing baked in. Auth config + the /api
      # proxy upstream are injected at runtime by the Container App env
      # (DATAQ_AUTH_* / DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM in deploy/terraform/azure/frontend.tf), so
      # there are NO VITE_* build args here and no per-environment rebuild. amd64
      # only (ACA is amd64); the multi-arch :latest is published by
      # publish-images.yml for the BYOL/eval path.
      - name: Build + push frontend image to GHCR
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          # && chain — same errexit-suppression reasoning as the backend build.
          build_push() {
            docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE_FRONTEND" frontend && docker push "$IMAGE_FRONTEND"
          }
          retry build_push

      # Retried + verified like the API/worker rolls; on the third failure one
      # last attempt runs with --debug so the ARM response the extension masks
      # (KeyError: 'properties', #539 — Deploys #1/#2) finally lands in the log.
      - name: Deploy frontend
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          update() {
            az containerapp update \
              --name "${{ vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME }}" \
              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
              --image "$IMAGE_FRONTEND" "$@"
          }
          if ! retry update; then
            echo "::warning::final attempt with --debug to surface the masked ARM error (#539)"
            update --debug
          fi
          live=$(az containerapp show \
            --name "${{ vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --query "properties.template.containers[0].image" -o tsv)
          [[ "$live" == "$IMAGE_FRONTEND" ]] || { echo "::error::frontend image mismatch after update: $live"; exit 1; }

1	# GitHub Actions -> AWS auth for the Deploy workflow — OIDC federation, no
2	# stored access keys. Mirrors deploy/terraform/azure/github_oidc.tf's shape:
3	# an OIDC identity provider trusting token.actions.githubusercontent.com, and
4	# a role whose trust policy conditions on the exact repo+environment subject.
5	
6	# GitHub's OIDC token-signing certificate thumbprint. AWS's OIDC provider
7	# resource requires this argument, though AWS has stopped strictly validating
8	# it against the TLS chain for well-known providers — kept for API
9	# compatibility. Verify at apply time against
10	# https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
11	# if GitHub ever rotates their intermediate CA.
12	locals {
13	  github_oidc_thumbprint = "6938fd4d98bab03faadb97b34396831e3780aea1"
14	}
15	
16	resource "aws_iam_openid_connect_provider" "github" {
17	  url             = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
18	  client_id_list  = ["sts.amazonaws.com"]
19	  thumbprint_list = [local.github_oidc_thumbprint]
20	}
21	
22	data "aws_iam_policy_document" "github_deploy_assume" {
23	  statement {
24	    actions = ["sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"]
25	    principals {
26	      type        = "Federated"
27	      identifiers = [aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github.arn]
28	    }
29	    condition {
30	      test     = "StringEquals"
31	      variable = "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud"
32	      values   = ["sts.amazonaws.com"]
33	    }
34	    # Must match the workflow's `environment: production` job scoping —
35	    # exactly the same shape as the Azure federated-credential subject.
36	    condition {
37	      test     = "StringLike"
38	      variable = "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub"
39	      values   = ["repo:${var.github_repo}:environment:${var.github_environment}"]
40	    }
41	  }
42	}
43	
44	resource "aws_iam_role" "github_deploy" {
45	  name               = "dataq-app-github-deploy"
46	  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.github_deploy_assume.json
47	}
48	
49	# Least privilege, resource-scoped to exactly the ECS objects the Deploy
50	# workflow touches (update-service / run-task for the migrate task) — never
51	# account-wide. iam:PassRole is scoped to only the task/execution roles this
