name: Deploy (AWS)

# Manual-only (workflow_dispatch), mirroring deploy.yml's posture: the Azure
# stack is primary prod, so the AWS parallel deployment rolls only on an
# explicit dispatch — never on push.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      image_tag:
        description: "Image tag to build + deploy (blank → aws-<commit SHA>, an immutable tag)"
        default: ""

concurrency:
  group: deploy-aws-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

# OIDC federated login to AWS (no stored access keys — deploy/terraform/aws/
# github_oidc.tf trusts exactly repo:<this repo>:environment:production).
# packages:write lets the GITHUB_TOKEN push both images to GHCR (ADR 0023);
# ECS pulls them anonymously (public packages), so no registry credential
# exists on the AWS side.
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
  packages: write

env:
  # `aws-<sha>` — NOT the bare `<sha>` (owned by the Azure deploy.yml) and NOT
  # `main-<sha>` (owned by publish-images.yml, which skips docs-only merges):
  # this workflow always builds its own immutable tag so the migrate task, api,
  # worker, and frontend all roll the exact build this run produced (#382).
  IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
  IMAGE_FRONTEND: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
  # Statically named by deploy/terraform/aws/ (the IAM policy's
  # RegisterTaskDefinition grant is scoped to the dataq-app-* families, so
  # these are contract, not convention).
  API_SERVICE: dataq-app-api
  WORKER_SERVICE: dataq-app-worker
  FRONTEND_SERVICE: dataq-app-frontend
  MIGRATE_FAMILY: dataq-app-migrate

jobs:
  backend:
    name: Backend — build, migrate, deploy (API + worker)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Fail fast on unset repo vars/secrets (#539 post-mortem, same rule as
      # deploy.yml): never let an empty value masquerade as a transient error
      # three steps later.
      - name: Preflight — required repo vars + secrets
        env:
          DEPLOY_ROLE: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          fail=0
          for pair in "AWS_REGION=${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}" \
                      "ECS_CLUSTER=${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                      "AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN=$DEPLOY_ROLE"; do
            [[ -n "${pair#*=}" ]] || { echo "::error::${pair%%=*} is not set"; fail=1; }
          done
          exit $fail

      - name: AWS login (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Retried (#539): a registry blip on the base-image pull or the GHCR push
      # shouldn't fail the deploy — a re-run hits the local layer cache.
      - name: Build + push backend image to GHCR
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          # && chain, not two statements: functions called from retry's
          # condition context have errexit suppressed inside, so a plain
          # sequence would still push after a failed build.
          build_push() {
            docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" . && docker push "$IMAGE"
          }
          retry build_push

      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-
      # compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new
      # schema. Unlike ACA jobs, an ECS task definition carries no separately
      # stored command to clobber — the migrate family's command lives IN the
      # definition — so re-registering with only the image swapped preserves it.
      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh

          # Register a new migrate revision on the new image. describe → strip
          # the register-rejected output-only fields → register.
          td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$MIGRATE_FAMILY" \
                 --query taskDefinition --output json)
          new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
            '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
             | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                   .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
            <<<"$td")
          register() {
            aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
              --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
          }
          migrate_arn=$(retry register)
          echo "Registered migrate task definition: $migrate_arn"

          # The one-off task runs with the api service's exact network shape
          # (same subnets/SG → same RDS reachability), read live rather than
          # duplicated into repo vars that would drift from the Terraform.
          netcfg=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                     --services "$API_SERVICE" \
                     --query 'services[0].networkConfiguration' --output json)

          run_task() {
            aws ecs run-task --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
              --task-definition "$migrate_arn" \
              --launch-type FARGATE \
              --network-configuration "$netcfg" \
              --query 'tasks[0].taskArn' --output text
          }
          task_arn=$(retry run_task)
          echo "Started migration task: $task_arn"

          # Fail-closed: the rollout below must not begin until the migration
          # has actually SUCCEEDED (exit 0). `aws ecs wait tasks-stopped` polls
          # 6s × 100 (10 min) and exits 255 on waiter timeout.
          aws ecs wait tasks-stopped --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" --tasks "$task_arn"
          state=$(aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" --tasks "$task_arn" \
                    --query 'tasks[0].[containers[0].exitCode, stopCode, stoppedReason]' --output json)
          exit_code=$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$state")
          if [[ "$exit_code" != "0" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Migration failed (exit=${exit_code}, $(jq -r '.[1] + ": " + .[2]' <<<"$state")) — aborting before app rollout."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Migration succeeded."

      # Register new api/worker revisions on the new image and roll both, then
      # WAIT for the deployments to complete — the step's exit code must mean
      # "the services are actually running the new image", not "the API call
      # was accepted" (the deploy.yml #539 verify rule, ECS-shaped).
      - name: Deploy API + worker
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          roll() {
            local family=$1
            local td new_td arn
            td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$family" \
                   --query taskDefinition --output json)
            new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
              '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
               | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                     .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
              <<<"$td")
            register() {
              aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
                --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
            }
            arn=$(retry register)
            update() {
              aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                --service "$family" --task-definition "$arn" \
                --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
            }
            retry update
            echo "$family -> $arn"
          }
          roll "$API_SERVICE"
          roll "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # services-stable polls 15s × 40 (10 min); exits 255 on timeout, so a
          # stuck rollout (crash-looping new revision) fails the deploy here.
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # Verify the primary deployment really is the new image (not merely
          # stable on the OLD one after a circuit-breaker rollback).
          for svc in "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"; do
            live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                        --services "$svc" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
            live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
                         --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
            [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::$svc image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }
          done

  frontend:
    name: Frontend — build image, deploy to ECS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed or
    # aborted migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against
    # an un-rolled or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).
    needs: backend
    env:
      # Job-level so the roll step below sees the frontend image as $IMAGE and
      # the shared roll logic stays identical to the backend job's.
      IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: AWS login (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # One generic image (ADR 0028) — nothing baked in. Auth config + the /api
      # proxy upstream are injected at runtime by the task definition env
      # (DATAQ_AUTH_* / DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM in deploy/terraform/aws/ecs.tf), so
      # there are NO VITE_* build args and no per-environment rebuild. amd64
      # only (the Fargate tasks are amd64); the multi-arch :latest is published
      # by publish-images.yml for the BYOL/eval path.
      - name: Build + push frontend image to GHCR
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          build_push() {
            docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" frontend && docker push "$IMAGE"
          }
          retry build_push

      - name: Deploy frontend
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" \
                 --query taskDefinition --output json)
          new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
            '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
             | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                   .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
            <<<"$td")
          register() {
            aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
              --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
          }
          arn=$(retry register)
          update() {
            aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
              --service "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --task-definition "$arn" \
              --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
          }
          retry update
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE"
          live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                      --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
          live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
                       --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
          [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::frontend image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }

      # Post-deploy smoke through the real public surface (CloudFront). The URL
      # is deployment-specific and deliberately not tracked in the repo (#730),
      # so this runs only when the optional AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var is set —
      # skipping is loudly logged, never silent.
      - name: Smoke (public surface)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          url="${{ vars.AWS_FRONTEND_URL }}"
          if [[ -z "$url" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var not set — skipping the public-surface smoke."
            exit 0
          fi
          for path_want in "/healthz 200" "/ 200" "/api/v1/me 401"; do
            path=${path_want% *}; want=${path_want#* }
            got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "${url%/}${path}")
            [[ "$got" == "$want" ]] || { echo "::error::smoke: ${path} returned ${got}, wanted ${want}"; exit 1; }
            echo "smoke: ${path} -> ${got} (ok)"
          done

            new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
              '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
               | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                     .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
              <<<"$td")
            register() {
              aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
                --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
            }
            arn=$(retry register)
            update() {
              aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                --service "$family" --task-definition "$arn" \
                --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
            }
            retry update
            echo "$family -> $arn"
          }
          roll "$API_SERVICE"
          roll "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # services-stable polls 15s × 40 (10 min); exits 255 on timeout, so a
          # stuck rollout (crash-looping new revision) fails the deploy here.
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # Verify the primary deployment really is the new image (not merely
          # stable on the OLD one after a circuit-breaker rollback).
          for svc in "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"; do
            live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                        --services "$svc" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
            live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
                         --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
            [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::$svc image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }
          done

  frontend:
    name: Frontend — build image, deploy to ECS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed or
    # aborted migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against
    # an un-rolled or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).
    needs: backend
    env:
      # Job-level so the roll step below sees the frontend image as $IMAGE and
      # the shared roll logic stays identical to the backend job's.
      IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: AWS login (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # One generic image (ADR 0028) — nothing baked in. Auth config + the /api
      # proxy upstream are injected at runtime by the task definition env
      # (DATAQ_AUTH_* / DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM in deploy/terraform/aws/ecs.tf), so
      # there are NO VITE_* build args and no per-environment rebuild. amd64
      # only (the Fargate tasks are amd64); the multi-arch :latest is published
      # by publish-images.yml for the BYOL/eval path.
      - name: Build + push frontend image to GHCR
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          build_push() {
            docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" frontend && docker push "$IMAGE"
          }
          retry build_push

      - name: Deploy frontend
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" \
                 --query taskDefinition --output json)
          new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
            '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
             | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                   .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
            <<<"$td")
          register() {
            aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
              --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text
          }
          arn=$(retry register)
          update() {
            aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
              --service "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --task-definition "$arn" \
              --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
          }
          retry update
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE"
          live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                      --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
          live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
                       --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
          [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::frontend image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }

      # Post-deploy smoke through the real public surface (CloudFront). The URL
      # is deployment-specific and deliberately not tracked in the repo (#730),
      # so this runs only when the optional AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var is set —
      # skipping is loudly logged, never silent.
      - name: Smoke (public surface)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          url="${{ vars.AWS_FRONTEND_URL }}"
          if [[ -z "$url" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var not set — skipping the public-surface smoke."
            exit 0
          fi
          for path_want in "/healthz 200" "/ 200" "/api/v1/me 401"; do
            path=${path_want% *}; want=${path_want#* }
            got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "${url%/}${path}")
            [[ "$got" == "$want" ]] || { echo "::error::smoke: ${path} returned ${got}, wanted ${want}"; exit 1; }
            echo "smoke: ${path} -> ${got} (ok)"
          done

# Shared CI retry helper (#539) — source this, don't execute it.
#
# Both Deploy-workflow transients this covers are idempotent to re-run:
#   - `az containerapp update/job update` crashing on a transient ARM error
#     (the containerapp extension's `_polish_bad_errors` masks 409/429-style
#     responses as `KeyError: 'properties'` — Deploys #1/#2, 2026-07-02)
#   - registry blips during image build/push (Docker Hub 502 on the base-image
#     pull — Deploy #3)
#
# Usage:  retry <cmd> [args…]        # 3 attempts, 30s/60s backoff
# The command's exit code is propagated from the final attempt.

retry() {
  local attempt
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    "$@" && return 0
    if (( attempt < 3 )); then
      echo "::warning::'$*' failed (attempt ${attempt}/3) — retrying in $(( attempt * 30 ))s (#539)"
      sleep $(( attempt * 30 ))
    fi
  done
  echo "::error::'$*' failed after 3 attempts (#539)"
  return 1
}

```bash
tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn   # → repo secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name         # → repo variable ECS_CLUSTER

gh variable set AWS_REGION --body "$(tofu output -raw -json | jq -r .aws_region.value 2>/dev/null || echo us-east-2)"
```

A companion `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` (not yet built) will use these
to `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` via OIDC, then run the same
build→push(GHCR)→migrate(RunTask, poll-to-terminal)→`ecs update-service`
sequence the Azure `deploy.yml` runs, adapted to the AWS CLI equivalents.

## State encryption

Same discipline as the Azure stack (`versions.tf`'s `encryption {}` block):
the local state holds the generated RDS/ElastiCache passwords in plaintext
without it. `state_encryption_passphrase` is a **data-at-rest key**, not a
credential — it cannot be revoked or re-minted, and losing it makes
`terraform.tfstate` permanently unreadable. Keep a second copy off this
machine. A wrong/missing passphrase fails closed
(`cipher: message authentication failed`) without corrupting the file.

## Verify

```bash
# Confirm exactly what got created, tagged for this stack:
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources \
  --tag-filters Key=Purpose,Values=dataq-app-aws

# Reachability (through the frontend — the sole public surface):
curl -s "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)/healthz"
```

Then in a browser: sign in through Cognito end-to-end, confirm `/api` and
`/mcp` return 401 unauthenticated without a credential, and run one real
suite against a live datasource to confirm the worker path.

The companion `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` uses these to
`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` via OIDC, then runs the same sequence
the Azure `deploy.yml` runs, adapted to ECS:

1. build + push both images to GHCR under the immutable tag `aws-<commit sha>`
   (bare `<sha>` belongs to the Azure deploy.yml, `main-<sha>` to
   publish-images.yml — three workflows, three disjoint tag namespaces);
2. register a new `dataq-app-migrate` task-definition revision on the new
   image and `run-task` it with the api service's live network configuration,
   **waiting for exit 0** before anything rolls (fail-closed);
3. register new api/worker/frontend revisions, `update-service`, and
   `wait services-stable`, then verify the primary deployment's image really
   is the new tag (a circuit-breaker rollback to the old image must fail the
   run, not pass as "stable");
4. optional public-surface smoke (healthz/SPA 200, `/api` 401) — runs only

# DataQ on AWS — Terraform (OpenTofu) runbook

A second, parallel deployment of DataQ (Azure stays the deployed prod — see
`deploy/terraform/azure/`), into a fresh, dedicated AWS account. Unlike the
Azure stack, nothing here is shared with another stack: this account exists
only for this deployment.

## What it creates

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| VPC, 2 public subnets, IGW, route table | Networking. No NAT Gateway (decision: public-subnets-no-NAT, ~$33/mo saved — ECS tasks get no public inbound access, only the ALB→frontend path is internet-reachable) |
| `aws_ecs_cluster.app` + 3 Fargate services (api, worker, frontend) + 1 task def (migrate) | The app itself. api is internal-only (Cloud Map DNS `api.dataq.local`); frontend is the sole public surface (behind the ALB); worker runs embedded celery-beat, `desired_count=1` always (cannot scale to zero) |
| `aws_cloudfront_distribution.app` → `aws_lb.app` (ALB, HTTP :80) | Public ingress. CloudFront terminates HTTPS on its default `*.cloudfront.net` cert (#1345 — Cognito requires an HTTPS redirect URI); the ALB admits only CloudFront's origin-facing ranges and forwards to the frontend target group |
| `aws_db_instance.app` (RDS Postgres, `db.t4g.micro`) | The app's own database — this stack creates it directly (no shared-server bootstrap dance like the Azure stack, since this account is dedicated) |
| `aws_elasticache_replication_group.app` (`cache.t4g.micro`, TLS + auth token) | Celery broker + rate-limit store |
| `aws_cognito_user_pool.app` + SPA client | OIDC identity provider, validated by the backend's provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026 amendment) — not Azure AD |
| `aws_secretsmanager_secret.*` (2, infra-owned) + IAM grants | `database-url`/`redis-url` (infra-owned, referenced by ARN in task defs) + the app's own runtime grant under `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX` (`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`) |
| `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` + `aws_iam_role.github_deploy` | GitHub Actions → AWS auth for the Deploy workflow, OIDC federation, no stored access keys |
| CloudWatch Log Groups (4) | Container logs. No APM/tracing wired up yet — the OTel core is vendor-neutral but the exporter shipped so far is Azure-only |

## Prerequisites

- **OpenTofu** (`tofu`), not Terraform — same ADR 0024 rationale as the Azure stack.
- **AWS CLI credentials** for a **scoped IAM user**, never root. This repo's own bring-up used `AWS_PROFILE=dataq-deploy` (set as the default in the operator's shell) — see the session notes for the IAM bootstrap steps (create user, attach a policy, remove root's access keys/login session).
- A **GitHub repo** with Actions enabled (for the OIDC federation to have something to trust).
- Nothing else pre-exists — this stack creates its own VPC, database, cache, etc. from scratch, unlike the Azure stack's shared-resource dependencies.

## Apply

```bash
cd deploy/terraform/aws
tofu init
# state_encryption_passphrase comes from your terraform.tfvars — see
# terraform.tfvars.example.
#
# Image tags (#1349): the services RUN these images from the first apply.
# publish-images.yml tags main merges as `main-<full sha>` (the bare `<sha>`
# tag is owned by the manual Azure deploy.yml and usually does NOT exist), and
# its `paths` filter skips merges that don't change image content — so use the
# last IMAGE-BEARING main commit, not the branch tip, and verify the tag
# exists before applying:
IMG_SHA=$(git log origin/main -1 --format=%H -- backend frontend pyproject.toml)
docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:main-${IMG_SHA}" > /dev/null  # must succeed
TF_VAR_app_db_password="REDACTED" \
tofu plan -input=false -out=tfplan \
  -var="image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}" \
  -var="frontend_image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}"
tofu apply -input=false tfplan
```

**Cost starts here.** `tofu apply` creates real, billable AWS resources (Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, ALB). Review the plan before applying. See the root-level deployment plan (in the session that built this stack) for the cost breakdown against the AWS free-tier credit.

## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow

```bash
tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn   # → repo secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name         # → repo variable ECS_CLUSTER
tofu output -raw frontend_url             # → sanity-check reachability
```

```bash
gh secret set AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN --body "$(tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn)"
gh variable set ECS_CLUSTER --body "$(tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name)"
gh variable set AWS_REGION --body "$(tofu output -raw -json | jq -r .aws_region.value 2>/dev/null || echo us-east-2)"
```

A companion `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` (not yet built) will use these
to `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` via OIDC, then run the same
build→push(GHCR)→migrate(RunTask, poll-to-terminal)→`ecs update-service`
sequence the Azure `deploy.yml` runs, adapted to the AWS CLI equivalents.

## State encryption

Same discipline as the Azure stack (`versions.tf`'s `encryption {}` block):
the local state holds the generated RDS/ElastiCache passwords in plaintext
without it. `state_encryption_passphrase` is a **data-at-rest key**, not a
credential — it cannot be revoked or re-minted, and losing it makes
`terraform.tfstate` permanently unreadable. Keep a second copy off this
machine. A wrong/missing passphrase fails closed
(`cipher: message authentication failed`) without corrupting the file.

## Verify

```bash
# Confirm exactly what got created, tagged for this stack:
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources \
  --tag-filters Key=Purpose,Values=dataq-app-aws

# Reachability (through the frontend — the sole public surface):
curl -s "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)/healthz"
```

Then in a browser: sign in through Cognito end-to-end, confirm `/api` and
`/mcp` return 401 unauthenticated without a credential, and run one real
suite against a live datasource to confirm the worker path.

## Known gaps in this pass (deliberately deferred, not silently skipped)

- No custom domain — the public URL is the CloudFront distribution's own
  `*.cloudfront.net` domain (HTTPS, default cert — #1345). Once a domain is
  chosen: Route53 + ACM cert + an `aliases` entry on the distribution.
- No private-subnet/NAT hardening — see `main.tf`'s decision note.
- No `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` yet — this stack only provisions the
  infra the workflow will drive.
- The Cognito `client_id`-vs-`aud` accommodation in `OidcBearerScheme`
  (backend) needs confirming against a real token from **this** pool once
  it's live — see `cognito.tf`'s comment.

# Shared ECS deploy helpers for deploy-aws.yml — source this, don't execute it.
# Requires: aws + jq on PATH, and scripts/ci/retry.sh sourced first (retry()).
#
# One implementation of the describe → image-swap → register → update →
# wait → verify roll, so the migrate, api/worker, and frontend steps cannot
# silently diverge (PR #1365 review). Values are returned via shell variables
# assigned INSIDE the retried functions — retry() logs ::warning:: lines to
# stdout, so `var=$(retry fn)` would swallow them into the captured value.

# Register a new revision of task-definition family $1 with its (single)
# container's image swapped to $2. Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN.
ecs_register_revision() {
  local family=$1 image=$2 td new_td
  td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$family" \
         --query taskDefinition --output json)
  # del(): the output-only fields describe returns that register rejects.
  new_td=$(jq --arg img "$image" \
    '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
     | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
           .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
    <<<"$td")
  _ecs_register() {
    ECS_REGISTERED_ARN=$(aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
      --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text)
  }
  retry _ecs_register
}

# Roll service $2 on cluster $1 to image $3 (service name == family name in
# this stack). Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN to the revision it rolled to.
ecs_roll_service() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3
  ecs_register_revision "$service" "$image"
  _ecs_update() {
    aws ecs update-service --cluster "$cluster" --service "$service" \
      --task-definition "$ECS_REGISTERED_ARN" \
      --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
  }
  retry _ecs_update
  echo "$service -> $ECS_REGISTERED_ARN"
}

# Wait for the listed services on cluster $1 to stabilise. TWO waiter laps
# (each 15s x 40 = 10 min): a perfectly normal rollout can exceed one lap
# because the ALB target group's default 300s deregistration drain sits on
# the deployment-complete path — a converging deploy must not spuriously
# fail on the waiter's fixed cap (PR #1365 review).
ecs_wait_stable() {
  local cluster=$1
  shift
  if ! aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"; then
    echo "::warning::services-stable waiter lap 1 timed out — one more lap (ALB drain can push a normal rollout past 10 min)"
    aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"
  fi
}

# Verify service $2's PRIMARY deployment on cluster $1 actually runs image $3:
# an ECS deployment-circuit-breaker rollback to the old image reports stable,
# and "stable on the old code" must fail the deploy, not pass it.
ecs_verify_image() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3 live_td live_img
  live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "$cluster" --services "$service" \
              --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
  live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
               --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
  if [[ "$live_img" != "$image" ]]; then
    echo "::error::$service image mismatch after rollout: $live_img (wanted $image)"
    return 1
  fi
}

  new_td=$(jq --arg img "$image" \
    '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
     | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
           .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
    <<<"$td")
  _ecs_register() {
    ECS_REGISTERED_ARN=$(aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
      --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text)
  }
  retry _ecs_register
}

# Roll service $2 on cluster $1 to image $3 (service name == family name in
# this stack). Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN to the revision it rolled to.
ecs_roll_service() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3
  ecs_register_revision "$service" "$image"
  _ecs_update() {
    aws ecs update-service --cluster "$cluster" --service "$service" \
      --task-definition "$ECS_REGISTERED_ARN" \
      --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
  }
  retry _ecs_update
  echo "$service -> $ECS_REGISTERED_ARN"
}

# Wait for the listed services on cluster $1 to stabilise. TWO waiter laps
# (each 15s x 40 = 10 min): a perfectly normal rollout can exceed one lap
# because the ALB target group's default 300s deregistration drain sits on
# the deployment-complete path — a converging deploy must not spuriously
# fail on the waiter's fixed cap (PR #1365 review).
ecs_wait_stable() {
  local cluster=$1
  shift
  if ! aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"; then
    echo "::warning::services-stable waiter lap 1 timed out — one more lap (ALB drain can push a normal rollout past 10 min)"
    aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"
  fi
}

# Verify service $2's PRIMARY deployment on cluster $1 actually runs image $3:
# an ECS deployment-circuit-breaker rollback to the old image reports stable,
# and "stable on the old code" must fail the deploy, not pass it.
ecs_verify_image() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3 live_td live_img
  live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "$cluster" --services "$service" \
              --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
  live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
               --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
  if [[ "$live_img" != "$image" ]]; then
    echo "::error::$service image mismatch after rollout: $live_img (wanted $image)"
    return 1
  fi
}

# Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-
      # compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new
      # schema. Unlike ACA jobs, an ECS task definition carries no separately
      # stored command to clobber — the migrate family's command lives IN the
      # definition — so re-registering with only the image swapped preserves it.
      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh

          # Register a new migrate revision on the new image. describe → strip
          # the register-rejected output-only fields → register.
          td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$MIGRATE_FAMILY" \
                 --query taskDefinition --output json)
          new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
            '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
             | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                   .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
            <<<"$td")
          # Capture INSIDE the retried function: retry() echoes ::warning::
          # lines to stdout, so `var=$(retry fn)` would swallow them into the
          # captured value on any retried attempt. retry runs the function in
          # the current shell, so the assignment survives.
          register() {
            migrate_arn=$(aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
              --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text)
          }
          retry register
          echo "Registered migrate task definition: $migrate_arn"

          # The one-off task runs with the api service's exact network shape
          # (same subnets/SG → same RDS reachability), read live rather than
          # duplicated into repo vars that would drift from the Terraform.
          netcfg=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                     --services "$API_SERVICE" \
                     --query 'services[0].networkConfiguration' --output json)

          run_task() {
            task_arn=$(aws ecs run-task --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
              --task-definition "$migrate_arn" \
              --launch-type FARGATE \
              --network-configuration "$netcfg" \
              --query 'tasks[0].taskArn' --output text)
          }
          retry run_task
          echo "Started migration task: $task_arn"

          # Fail-closed: the rollout below must not begin until the migration
          # has actually SUCCEEDED (exit 0). `aws ecs wait tasks-stopped` polls
          # 6s × 100 (10 min) and exits 255 on waiter timeout.
          aws ecs wait tasks-stopped --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" --tasks "$task_arn"
          state=$(aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" --tasks "$task_arn" \
                    --query 'tasks[0].[containers[0].exitCode, stopCode, stoppedReason]' --output json)
          exit_code=$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$state")
          if [[ "$exit_code" != "0" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Migration failed (exit=${exit_code}, $(jq -r '.[1] + ": " + .[2]' <<<"$state")) — aborting before app rollout."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Migration succeeded."

      # Register new api/worker revisions on the new image and roll both, then
      # WAIT for the deployments to complete — the step's exit code must mean
      # "the services are actually running the new image", not "the API call
      # was accepted" (the deploy.yml #539 verify rule, ECS-shaped).
      - name: Deploy API + worker
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          roll() {
            local family=$1
            local td new_td arn
            td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$family" \
                   --query taskDefinition --output json)
            new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
              '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
               | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                     .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
              <<<"$td")
            # Same capture-inside-the-retried-function shape as the migrate
            # step (retry's ::warning:: lines share stdout). `arn` is roll()'s
            # local; bash locals are dynamically scoped, so the nested
            # function's assignment lands on it.
            register() {
              arn=$(aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
                --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text)
            }
            retry register
            update() {
              aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                --service "$family" --task-definition "$arn" \
                --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
            }
            retry update
            echo "$family -> $arn"
          }
          roll "$API_SERVICE"
          roll "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # services-stable polls 15s × 40 (10 min); exits 255 on timeout, so a
          # stuck rollout (crash-looping new revision) fails the deploy here.
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"
          # Verify the primary deployment really is the new image (not merely
          # stable on the OLD one after a circuit-breaker rollback).
          for svc in "$API_SERVICE" "$WORKER_SERVICE"; do
            live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                        --services "$svc" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
            live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
                         --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
            [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::$svc image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }
          done

  frontend:
    name: Frontend — build image, deploy to ECS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed or
    # aborted migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against
    # an un-rolled or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).
    needs: backend
    env:
      # Job-level so the roll step below sees the frontend image as $IMAGE and
      # the shared roll logic stays identical to the backend job's.
      IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend:${{ inputs.image_tag || format('aws-{0}', github.sha) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: AWS login (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}

run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          build_push() {
            docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" frontend && docker push "$IMAGE"
          }
          retry build_push

      - name: Deploy frontend
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/ci/retry.sh
          td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" \
                 --query taskDefinition --output json)
          new_td=$(jq --arg img "$IMAGE" \
            '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
             | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
                   .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
            <<<"$td")
          register() {
            arn=$(aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
              --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text)
          }
          retry register
          update() {
            aws ecs update-service --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
              --service "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --task-definition "$arn" \
              --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
          }
          retry update
          aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
            --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE"
          live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "${{ vars.ECS_CLUSTER }}" \
                      --services "$FRONTEND_SERVICE" --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
          live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
                       --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
          [[ "$live_img" == "$IMAGE" ]] || { echo "::error::frontend image mismatch after rollout: $live_img"; exit 1; }

      # Post-deploy smoke through the real public surface (CloudFront). The URL
      # is deployment-specific and deliberately not tracked in the repo (#730),
      # so this runs only when the optional AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var is set —
      # skipping is loudly logged, never silent.
      - name: Smoke (public surface)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          url="${{ vars.AWS_FRONTEND_URL }}"
          if [[ -z "$url" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::AWS_FRONTEND_URL repo var not set — skipping the public-surface smoke."
            exit 0
          fi
          for path_want in "/healthz 200" "/ 200" "/api/v1/me 401"; do
            path=${path_want% *}; want=${path_want#* }
            got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "${url%/}${path}")
            [[ "$got" == "$want" ]] || { echo "::error::smoke: ${path} returned ${got}, wanted ${want}"; exit 1; }
            echo "smoke: ${path} -> ${got} (ok)"
          done

Fixed with TCP keepalives (`keepalives_idle`/`interval`/`count`) on the shared engine's `connect_args`, one layer under #1102's `connect_timeout`. Review found the migrate-job engine (`alembic/env.py`, its own independent engine, exposed to the same gap and test-enforced-parity-tracked per its own docstring) hadn't been mirrored — fixed same-PR with a matching AST regression test; the driver-guard gap was deferred to #1266 above rather than fixed inline, to keep the PR focused. **#1253** (`observed_value` retention sweep): `purge_expired_sample_failures` scrubbed `sample_failures` but never the sibling list-shaped `observed_value` JSONB — correctly redacted on every read since #1252, but persisting indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep. Fixed with a shared `_purge_column` helper reused across both columns. **#1230** (PII classifier evidence-window, option 2 chosen): the #1196 sample cap narrowed the classifier's evidence to 20 rows at capture time for pandas-backed datasources, which can flip a genuinely-PII column to "not PII" on a noisy 20-row window. Fixed by persisting a compact per-column `value_signal_summary` (5 small ints) over the FULL pre-cap population alongside the capped rows, which the classifier prefers when present and validates before trusting (rejects a summary with an inflated/inconsistent sub-count). A `/code-review` round live-verified a real crash — `_valid_summary`'s except clause didn't catch `OverflowError`, so a persisted JSONB summary with a huge float (`"n": 1e400` → `inf`) 500'd the entire read path instead of degrading to "no summary" — and found the summary wasn't threaded into the sibling `partial_unexpected_list`'s redaction (only `unexpected_index_list`'s), leaving a column masked on one list still shown on the other for the same run; both fixed and mutation-checked same-PR. **#1251** (consolidate hand-rolled `SecretStore` test doubles): five files each hand-rolled a near-identical class implementing the `SecretStore` Protocol, folded into one shared `backend/tests/support/fake_secret_store.py::FakeSecretStore`. The migration surfaced a real bug along the way — FastAPI's dependency-override resolution introspects the override CALLABLE's own signature, so a bare class (not a lambda) with constructor params, even all-defaulted ones, gets those params bound as request-level params and corrupts body validation for the endpoint under test; a bare `_WriteFailStore()` override was making `POST /connections` 422 instead of ever reaching the route. Review found the fix was patched inline at only the two call sites that hit it rather than encoded at the seam — promoted into a shared `override_secret_store(app, store)` helper (documented in the module docstring) in a same-PR follow-up commit, and `test_admin.py`'s pre-existing `_with_store` now delegates to it instead of duplicating the same lambda wrap. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1260](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1260) merged, closing [#1226](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1226) — net unchanged, offset by filing [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261). **#1226**: when every alert channel failed, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` logged a full traceback per failing channel and then the caller (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) logged the SAME last-channel traceback a second time via its own bare `except Exception:`. Fixed with a plain marker attribute (`mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` in `alerting/base.py`, the same stash-on-the-object technique already used by `celery_app.py`'s `_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR`) the composite sets on the re-raised error, so both callers downgrade to a warning for an error the composite already reported, while anything the composite never saw still gets a full traceback. Two full `/code-review` rounds (8 agents total) found zero correctness defects — three concrete "could this fail" scenarios (setattr on `__slots__`-based exceptions, marker loss across the `asyncio.to_thread` hop, exception-identity loss via re-wrapping) were each traced and ruled out with evidence, not assumed away — but did surface real polish gaps, all fixed same-PR: the downgraded warning in `main.py` carried zero identifying fields (now carries `error_type`); a comment overstated what `run_poll_staleness_check` does with the exception (it never catches it — corrected); a test file had invented a THIRD near-identical "channel that raises" double instead of reusing the one two files over (deduped); and a `# pragma: no cover` on the except block had gone stale now that both branches are directly tested (removed, verified via a real coverage run that both lines are hit). One idea deliberately deferred rather than acted on: centralizing the downgrade in the structlog processor chain (the CLAUDE.md §10 "redact at the logger, not the call site" precedent) — reasonable for 3+ callers, premature for the 2 that exist today — filed as #1261. The user re-reported the stretched columns against this very deploy, and pulling the live prod chunks settled it: **both fixes were in the shipped bundle and neither had ever worked, in any environment.** Every DataQ table renders `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, which rc-table turns into `width: max-content` on the `<table>`; an intrinsic-sizing keyword sizes the table from its content, neutering `table-layout: fixed` and demoting the `<colgroup>` width to a non-binding hint — so a column's `width` + `ellipsis` are **inert**, and a long ADF error rendered ~1917px wide against a declared 260px. The covering test asserted `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — true, and meaningless, because jsdom performs no layout. Fixed by bounding the **inner element** (`boundedTextStyle`) rather than the column, with the regression assertion moved to Playwright where widths can actually be measured. **Standing practice this produced: "merged" is not "deployed", and "deployed" is not "works" — verify a fix against the running artifact AND against observed behavior before reporting it as done.** Rolled via [run 31342076551](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31342076551), migrate job Succeeded, post-deploy smoke green (healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401 gates hold, `/docs` serves the SPA shell not Swagger, authenticated `/me` verified, beat+watchdog clean, Key Vault secret store initialized on the new revision) — **plus a live suite run** ("Snowflake — Orders (all paths)", 7 checks, 6 pass/1 fail/1 skip, `succeeded`) confirming the #1273 fix holds against real prod data. **Prod redeployed twice more the same day — to `77068358`, then to `eba60b4d` (current)** ([run 31347217502](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31347217502), [run 31350288817](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31350288817)); both migrate jobs no-op (zero migration files in either delta), both smokes green, and the fixes **verified in the running artifact and in the browser**, not merely merged: the deployed chunk `ellipsisColumn-*.js` carries `boundedTextStyle`, and the Failure-reason cell that had rendered ~1917px now measures 260px with 3423px of content clipped, Observed 220px, the pipeline table 1379px instead of 2969px. The second roll carried two post-deploy-smoke findings from the first: **#1286** (the fix’s own regression — a 150px bound wrapped the copy button and grew every pipeline-runs row 56px→77px; measured the threshold on live prod and shipped 120) and **#1285** (pre-existing — orchestration poll failures were classified through the datasource message set, so both Airflow connections said “missing warehouse or role … check the suite’s run target” while the harness Airflow app was simply Stopped; an orchestration connection has none of those four things). Both confirmed live afterwards: 20/20 Provider-run cells clipped at 120px with a uniform 56px row height, and the 02:51Z poll wrote the new orchestration-shaped reason. A live suite run on each revision (8 checks) confirmed the worker path against real Snowflake. **Verification lesson from this session, now standing practice: “merged” is not “deployed”, and “deployed” is not “works” — a stale-looking grep in the wrong chunk nearly produced a second wrong answer, and the first poll after the roll still showed the old message because the draining revision served it.** Orchestration (Airflow trigger → poll → dispatch) was also verified end-to-end in the local harness this session, after fixing a stale `DATAQ_LOADER`-scoped Snowflake credential in the harness's own (untracked, separate-repo) local stack — see [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). **ADLS** — volume read 643 rows off the resolved batch and arrival-time freshness reported 531.8h from the blob's last-modified: the harness genuinely stopped producing, which is precisely the incident #520 exists to catch and which an in-file MAX cannot see. **Snowflake** — `order_ts` (lower-case, emitted unquoted so the warehouse folds it) and `ORDER_TS` (upper-case, now quoted) returned **identical** timestamps, proving #937 both fixes mixed case and preserves the fold; volume over 32,840 real rows. **Unity Catalog** — freshness works **for the first time ever** (239.06h, lower/UPPER identical, confirming the backtick dialect). The dimension backfill (#952) classified **all 30 real prod checks, zero unclassified**, and real asset scorecards show genuine signal. **Live testing found a bug three green suites could not: UC freshness had NEVER worked** (#953) — the Databricks connector returns a TIMESTAMP's MAX as a **str** and the age math accepted only datetime/date, so a datasource the feature matrix marks ✅ produced no reading since #426. No unit test could see it: the type comes from the **driver**, and every fixture hands in a real datetime — the same fixture-encodes-our-model shape as #823 and the #520 Parquet bug. **Lesson: for anything whose type or value crosses a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence.** Also filed [#954](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/954): two prod Snowflake PATs are dead, and a **datasource** connection with a dead credential has no visible state until a run fails — I had to read worker logs to find out why, since #839's health signal covers only *orchestration* connections. That is the #828 blindness in a new place. **W4 CLOSED 2026-07-19, 8/8** — `schema_drift` (#592) shipped 2026-07-17, and this session cleared the remaining four in two groups. **Flat-file (#476, #520):** every backend CSV read hardcoded the pandas default comma, so a `;`/tab/pipe file parsed as ONE column named after the whole header — silently; all four reads now share one sniffing seam ([#934](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/934)). #476's casing half was **relocated by checking the code instead of the ticket** — the profiler's Core builders already quoted correctly; the only unquoted path was `monitors.py`'s f-string, fixed by returning a Core `Select` so the CONNECTION's dialect quotes it ([#937](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/937)); hand-rolled `"` quoting would have been actively wrong on UC, which uses backticks. Flat files gained freshness/volume monitors incl. **arrival-time freshness** — the case a warehouse can't express, since an in-file MAX is blind to a producer that stopped sending files ([#940](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/940)). **Dimension & score (#124, #889):** ADR [0038](docs/adr/0038-dq-dimension-classification.md) — seven canonical dimensions, closed vocabulary, derived default → stored → overridable, derivation deliberately partial so **NULL means unclassified and renders as a coverage gap** ([#945](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/945)); then `services/rollup.py` as the one histogram + score + latest-run query ([#948](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/948)) and the asset scorecard on top ([#950](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/950)).

All three stages are done — full E2E green on AWS and `deploy-aws.yml` shipped and validated with a real production deploy.

## 1. Cognito user

Created `royarijit1995+aws-e2e@gmail.com` ("AWS E2E", email verified, non-admin). It signed in through the hosted UI and was provisioned via the userinfo fallback, exactly as the OIDC track predicted. I rotated its password to an unknown random afterward (the test password had to pass through the transcript) — use Forgot-password on the sign-in page to claim it.

## 2. Connections, suites, checks, Secrets Manager, E2E

But first, a blocker the post-apply smoke couldn't see: **the AWS worker had never started**. Celery hard-rejects a `rediss://` URL lacking `ssl_cert_reqs`, so it crash-looped since the apply (25+ dead tasks), and the api's dispatch path would have died identically. Filed **#1361**, fixed in [#1362](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1362) (`?ssl_cert_reqs=required` — verified as the one spelling celery/kombu/redis-py all accept), applied, rolled, and confirmed live: `celery ready` over TLS to ElastiCache. Generic follow-up filed as #1363.

Then the E2E, all through the live app (credentials piped inline from the local-mirror OpenBao, never printed; Azure CLI was logged out):

- **Snowflake + Unity Catalog connections created** → credentials landed in **AWS Secrets Manager** as `dataq/conn-snowflake-retail-dev-02d99a91` and `dataq/conn-unity-catalog-retail-dev-dd5ca985`; both Test Connections green against the real warehouses.
- **Suites + checks authored** (not-null, row-count, freshness monitors, one deliberate FAIL).
- **Runs executed by the AWS worker:** Snowflake `succeeded` 2/4 — a real freshness WARN at 470h and the deliberate FAIL failing as designed; UC `succeeded` **3/3** (freshness 183.6h) after I corrected my own guessed column name (which produced a properly classified per-check `error` — the error path works too). All rendered correctly in the UI.

One more find along the way: **sign-out on Cognito lands on a raw "Client does not exist" 400** and the hosted-UI session survives (silent re-auth as the old user). Filed as **#1364** — Cognito's `/logout` isn't standards-conformant; Azure AD is, which is why prod never showed it.

## 3. deploy-aws.yml — shipped and tested

[#1365](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1365) merged: OIDC role login, immutable `aws-<sha>` tags (disjoint from the Azure and publish-images namespaces), migrate RunTask gated on exit 0 using the api service's live network config, rolls via a shared `scripts/ci/ecs_roll.sh` that verifies the primary deployment's image (a circuit-breaker rollback fails the run), and a CloudFront smoke gated on the new `AWS_FRONTEND_URL` repo var. The review caught four real defects pre-merge (the literal-`None` ARN trap on run-task placement failures, waiter-vs-ALB-drain timing, triplicated roll logic, no curl timeout) — all fixed.

Then dispatched for real: [run 31909137435](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31909137435) went green first try — migrate exit 0, all three services `COMPLETED` on `aws-8f08652b`, smoke 200/200/401, and healthz confirmed live afterward.

Docs (progress.md + CLAUDE.md §13) and memory updated; all issues/PRs labeled and milestoned; branches pruned; `main` clean. One heads-up: your clipboard currently holds text you copied mid-session — I stopped using it for token passing the moment I saw it was yours.

content.text:
## Parity today (after this session)

| Capability | Azure (primary prod) | AWS | Parity |
|---|---|---|---|
| App hosting (api internal / worker+beat / frontend public / migrate) | ACA ×3 + migrate job | ECS Fargate ×3 + migrate task | ✅ full |
| Public HTTPS surface | frontend ACA ingress | CloudFront → ALB → nginx | ✅ (gap: #1355 origin secret — Azure has no analogous hole) |
| Database | shared `dataq-pg-wus3` Flexible Server | RDS `db.t4g.micro` (dedicated) | ✅ |
| Broker / rate limits | self-hosted Redis ACA | ElastiCache TLS+auth | ✅ (fixed today — the worker had never started before #1362) |
| Secrets | Key Vault (UAMI) | Secrets Manager (task-role) | ✅ — proven today: connection creds landed as `dataq/conn-*` via the app |
| Auth | Azure AD via generic OIDC | Cognito via the same `OidcBearerScheme` + userinfo fallback | ✅ sign-in; ❌ **sign-out broken (#1364)**; only 2 users exist vs Azure's demo cohort |
| CI/CD deploy | `deploy.yml` | `deploy-aws.yml` — **validated live today** | ✅ |
| Suite execution against real warehouses | SF / UC / ADLS / S3-MinIO / Iceberg configured | **SF + UC configured and green today**; other types work but aren't configured | 🟡 config, not code |
| MCP `/mcp` | live, 8 tools | 401 gate verified; no full tool E2E yet | 🟡 |
| Alert channels (Teams/Slack/email) | wired, secrets in KV | seam present; `EMAIL_FROM` empty, no channel secrets set | ❌ config |
| Observability | App Insights: OTel spans + exported logs + KQL | **CloudWatch container logs only — no span/APM exporter at all** (`tracing.py` is Azure-exporter-only, #525) | ❌ biggest real gap |
| Infra alerting (dead-poll, health) | Azure Monitor alert rules | none (no CloudWatch alarms) | ❌ |
| Durability posture | prod-ish | eval-grade: `backup_retention=1`, no deletion protection, `skip_final_snapshot`, single-AZ, public subnets/no NAT | ❌ deliberate cost choices |

## What a full Azure→AWS switch still needs (app hosting only)

**New resources / code:**
1. **APM/tracing target** — the one code seam: an OTLP/ADOT (or X-Ray) exporter branch in `backend/app/core/tracing.py` + collector/endpoint resources, or you lose #525's spans and the log export entirely. Plus CloudWatch alarms replacing Azure Monitor (service health, beat watchdog, 5xx).
2. **Custom domain** — Route 53 + ACM cert on CloudFront (today's URL is the default `*.cloudfront.net`; every OIDC redirect URI, webhook, and MCP client config keys off it, so pick the domain *before* migrating users).
3. **Email/alert channel config** — SES (or SMTP) + `EMAIL_FROM` + channel secrets (`channel-email-password`, Teams/Slack webhook URLs) into Secrets Manager.
4. **#1355** — CloudFront origin secret verified at nginx (until then any CloudFront distribution can origin-point at the ALB).
5. **Prod-grade durability** — RDS backups ≥7d + deletion protection + final snapshot, ElastiCache snapshots, ideally private subnets + NAT (or VPC endpoints) and multi-AZ; all currently traded away for cost.

**Migration work (no new code):**
6. **Data** — `pg_dump` Azure PG → RDS (users, PATs, suites, checks, run history), then **re-mint every per-connection secret** into Secrets Manager — the one-credential-becomes-N-secrets trap that caused the 3-week dead-connections incident.
7. **Identity** — recreate users in Cognito (no import of Azure AD identities; `aad_object_id`/`oidc_issuer` self-heal on next login since #1340, but each human needs a Cognito account) and **fix #1364 first** — you can't run prod on a sign-out that 400s and silently re-authenticates.
8. **Webhook re-point** — ADF/Airflow/dbt callback URLs → the new domain, secrets into Secrets Manager.
9. Confirm `RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS=3` against one real logged XFF, and #1338 (runbook docs).

Everything else — GX engine, orchestration abstraction, secret-store seam, alerting seam, GHCR images — is already cloud-neutral and needs nothing. The honest summary: **functional parity is essentially there as of today; what's missing for a *switch* is observability, identity/domain migration, and durability hardening — config and ops, not application code, except the tracing exporter.**

1	/**
2	 * Auth configuration — sourced at RUNTIME, not build time (ADR 0028).
3	 *
4	 * The container serves `/config.js` (rendered from env by nginx at startup) which
5	 * sets `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__` before the app bundle runs. That means one
6	 * generic image with nothing baked in — no cloud, no secret, no auth-bypass.
7	 * When no such global is present — `pnpm dev`, and the static/SWA build until the
8	 * ADR-0028 cutover — we fall back to the build-time `VITE_*` env (bypass there
9	 * stays DEV-gated, so a production static bundle can't enable it).
10	 *
11	 * The injected contract is provider-neutral (`DATAQ_AUTH_*`): `mode` + a standard
12	 * OIDC-shaped `authority` / `clientId` / `apiScope`. Azure is one populated shape
13	 * (`authority = https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`); no `AZURE` in
14	 * the contract.
15	 *
16	 * Mode is computed once at module load:
17	 * - 'real'         — `mode:'oidc'` with authority + clientId present. The generic
18	 *                    OIDC auth client (oidc-client-ts — ADR 0028/#504) drives
19	 *                    redirect-flow login + token acquisition.
20	 * - 'otp'          — ONLY when `mode:'otp'` is explicitly set (ADR 0032). Email
21	 *                    one-time codes; the credential is an HttpOnly cookie the SPA
22	 *                    never sees, so there is nothing else to configure here.
23	 * - 'dev_bypass'   — ONLY when `mode:'bypass'` is explicitly set. Fail-closed:
24	 *                    never inferred from missing config. Renders a fixed dev user.
25	 * - 'unconfigured' — anything else. AuthGate shows a setup-needed banner.
26	 *
27	 * The `otp` value is one half of a **pair of coordinated selectors** (ADR 0032
28	 * decision 2): the backend infers its own mode from `AUTH_EMAIL_*` + the signup
29	 * allowlist and never reads this one. Set both or neither — this alone yields a
30	 * code form whose endpoints 503.
31	 */
32	
33	export type AuthMode = 'real' | 'otp' | 'dev_bypass' | 'unconfigured';
34	
35	/** The runtime auth contract injected via `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__.auth`. */
36	export interface DataqAuthConfig {
37	  /**
38	   * 'bypass' = no IdP (local/eval); 'otp' = email one-time codes (ADR 0032);
39	   * 'oidc' = IdP sign-in. Absent/unrecognised → unconfigured.
40	   */
41	  mode?: 'bypass' | 'otp' | 'oidc';
42	  /** OIDC issuer/authority URL (e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0). */
43	  authority?: string;
44	  /** The public SPA client id registered with the IdP. */
45	  clientId?: string;
46	  /** Full scope string requested for the API access token (Azure: api://<api-client-id>/<scope>). */
47	  apiScope?: string;
48	  /**
49	   * Complete OVERRIDE of the requested OAuth scope string (#1347). When set, it
50	   * replaces the default `openid profile email offline_access [apiScope]`
51	   * entirely. Needed because scope support is provider-specific: AWS Cognito
52	   * rejects `offline_access` (`error=invalid_scope` — not one of its system
53	   * scopes), so a Cognito deployment sets e.g. "openid email profile" here
54	   * (Cognito issues refresh tokens on the code grant regardless).
55	   */
56	  scope?: string;
57	}
58	
59	declare global {
60	  interface Window {
61	    __DATAQ_CONFIG__?: { auth?: DataqAuthConfig };
62	  }
63	}
64	
65	/**
66	 * Build-time fallback for `pnpm dev` (no injected /config.js). Maps the legacy
67	 * VITE_* Azure vars onto the generic contract so local dev is unchanged. Bypass
68	 * still requires the explicit VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true opt-in.
69	 */
70	function fromBuildEnv(): DataqAuthConfig {
71	  const tenantId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID;
72	  const clientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID;
73	  const apiClientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID;
74	  const scope = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE || 'user_impersonation';
75	  // Belt-and-suspenders: bypass in the build-env fallback stays gated on a DEV
76	  // build, so a production static bundle (e.g. the SWA deploy, which serves this
77	  // fallback path — the /config.js stub sets no global) can never enable auth
78	  // bypass even if VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true were baked in. The image path never
79	  // reaches here (nginx injects window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__).
80	  const bypass = import.meta.env.DEV && import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS === 'true';
81	  // `pnpm dev` against a locally-running OTP backend. Explicit opt-in only — an
82	  // unrecognised value falls through to the OIDC/unconfigured branches rather
83	  // than being coerced into a mode. Not DEV-gated like bypass, because unlike
84	  // bypass this mode *is* a real authenticator: turning it on in a production
85	  // bundle grants nothing without a mailbox and a server-side allowlist.
86	  const otp = import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_MODE === 'otp';
87	  return {
88	    // OTP is checked BEFORE bypass (#1150). `VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true` is the
89	    // long-standing dev default and lives in the compose file; an explicitly
90	    // named mode has to win over a leftover boolean, or the local stack would
91	    // render "no sign-in at all" while its backend was serving email codes —
92	    // the split-brain the two-selector contract exists to prevent. Safe
93	    // direction: this can only ever REPLACE a bypass with a real authenticator.
94	    mode: otp ? 'otp' : bypass ? 'bypass' : tenantId && clientId ? 'oidc' : undefined,
95	    authority: tenantId ? `https://login.microsoftonline.com/${tenantId}/v2.0` : undefined,
96	    clientId: clientId || undefined,
97	    apiScope: apiClientId ? `api://${apiClientId}/${scope}` : undefined,
98	  };
99	}
100	
101	// The injected runtime config wins; the build-time env is the dev-only fallback
102	// used only when no /config.js was served (i.e. `pnpm dev`).
103	const injected = typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__?.auth : undefined;
104	const cfg: DataqAuthConfig = injected ?? fromBuildEnv();
105	
106	export const authConfig = {
107	  authority: cfg.authority,
108	  clientId: cfg.clientId,
109	  apiScope: cfg.apiScope,
110	  scope: cfg.scope,
111	} as const;
112	
113	export const authMode: AuthMode = (() => {
114	  // Fail-closed: bypass and otp ONLY on their explicit flag, never inferred.
115	  if (cfg.mode === 'bypass') return 'dev_bypass';
116	  // Checked before the OIDC branch so a deployment that leaves stale
117	  // authority/clientId values behind while switching to `otp` gets the mode it
118	  // asked for, rather than silently continuing to render an IdP redirect.
119	  if (cfg.mode === 'otp') return 'otp';
120	  if (cfg.authority && cfg.clientId) return 'real';
121	  return 'unconfigured';
122	})();
123	
124	/** Human-readable auth-method label per mode (Profile + Settings "Authentication" rows). */
125	export const AUTH_METHOD_LABELS: Record<AuthMode, string> = {
126	  real: 'OIDC (SSO)',
127	  otp: 'Email one-time code',
128	  dev_bypass: 'Dev bypass (no IdP)',
129	  unconfigured: 'Not configured',
130	};
131	
132	/** The label for the mode this deployment is actually running in. */
133	export const authMethodLabel = AUTH_METHOD_LABELS[authMode];
134	
135	export const DEV_USER = {
136	  name: 'Dev Bypass User',
137	  username: 'dev-bypass@dataq.local',
138	  homeAccountId: 'dev-bypass',
139	  isDev: true as const,
140	};

# ONE generic image, nothing baked in (ADR 0028): no cloud, no secret, no
# auth-bypass. Auth config is injected at RUNTIME — nginx serves /config.js from
# the DATAQ_AUTH_* env below (envsubst at startup), and the SPA reads it before
# the bundle runs. So the same image serves the eval stack (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass)
# and a real deployment (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc + authority/clientId/scope) — set the
# env at `docker run`, no rebuild. Replaces the #472 two-image (:latest/:dev) split.
#
# The deploy workflow builds + pushes this image and rolls the `dataq-app-frontend`
# Container App (ADR 0028 §5 cutover — the Static Web App is gone; SWA couldn't
# inject runtime config). See deploy/terraform/azure/frontend.tf.

# Pin the build stage to the native BUILD platform (amd64 on CI runners) even for
# an arm64 target image: a Vite SPA compiles to architecture-independent static
# assets, so there's no reason to run `pnpm build` under arm64 QEMU emulation — it
# only made the multi-arch publish pathologically slow / flaky (12min good case →
# 45min stall, #512). buildx cross-builds: this stage runs native, and only the
# tiny per-arch nginx `serve` stage below is built for each target platform, with
# the arch-independent dist COPYed in. $BUILDPLATFORM is a buildx-predefined arg.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
RUN corepack enable

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

COPY . .
RUN pnpm build

FROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve
# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages, lets the
# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push it, and inherits anonymous-pull visibility —
# ADR 0023, mirrors backend/Dockerfile).
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ frontend (React SPA served by nginx)"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
# Template (not a static conf): the nginx entrypoint envsubst's it at startup so
# the API upstream + auth config are runtime-configurable.
COPY nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template
# Opt into the nginx image's built-in resolver detection: its
# 15-local-resolvers.envsh only exports ${NGINX_LOCAL_RESOLVERS} (the
# /etc/resolv.conf nameservers, used by the proxy `resolver` directive) when this
# flag is set. Cloud-neutral (ADR 0028) — no resolver IP baked in; works in
# compose (127.0.0.11) and ACA/K8s (cluster DNS) alike.
ENV NGINX_ENTRYPOINT_LOCAL_RESOLVERS=1
# Runtime config env (ADR 0028) — MUST be defined (even if empty) so envsubst
# always substitutes them in /config.js; empty → SPA is unconfigured (fail-closed),
# bypass needs an explicit DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass. DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM defaults to
# the compose `api` service.
ENV DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api:8000 \
    DATAQ_AUTH_MODE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE=""
EXPOSE 8080

input.content:
# SES — the email alert channel (#1368), the AWS-native counterpart of the
# SMTP creds the Azure stack keeps in Key Vault. Everything here is gated on
# var.alert_email: empty (the default) creates nothing and the app's email
# channel stays off (config.py enables it only when EMAIL_TO + EMAIL_USERNAME
# + EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME are all set).
#
# Sandbox posture, stated honestly: a fresh SES account can only send FROM and
# TO verified identities, so alert_email is both the sender and the sole
# recipient — fine for a single-operator deployment; production fan-out needs
# an SES production-access request (an AWS support form, not Terraform).
#
# The identity requires a ONE-TIME human step: SES emails a verification link
# to alert_email at create time, and sends fail with "Email address is not
# verified" until it is clicked. Check with:
#   aws ses get-identity-verification-attributes --identities <alert_email>

resource "aws_ses_email_identity" "alert" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  email = var.alert_email
}

# Dedicated IAM user for SMTP: SES SMTP credentials ARE an IAM access key —
# the username is the key id and the password is Terraform's derived
# ses_smtp_password_v4 (the documented SigV4 derivation, region-specific).
# Scoped to SendRawEmail only (what SMTP submission uses), from this identity.
resource "aws_iam_user" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name  = "dataq-app-ses-smtp"
  tags  = { Name = "dataq-app-ses-smtp" }
}

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  statement {
    actions   = ["ses:SendRawEmail"]
    resources = [aws_ses_email_identity.alert[0].arn]
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_user_policy" "ses_smtp" {
  count  = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name   = "dataq-app-ses-smtp-send"
  user   = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ses_smtp[0].json
}

resource "aws_iam_access_key" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  user  = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
}

# The SMTP password goes into Secrets Manager UNDER THE APP PREFIX
# (dataq/channel-email-password): the task env's EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME
# already names `channel-email-password`, which the app resolves through its
# own SecretStore (SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager + AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX
# = dataq/) at send time — same read path as every connection credential, no
# extra task-definition secret injection.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "channel_email_password" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name  = "dataq/channel-email-password"
  # The app's sweep/rotation owns secrets under dataq/, but this one is
  # infra-owned: recovery_window 0 so a destroy/recreate cycle doesn't collide
  # with a soft-deleted name.
  recovery_window_in_days = 0
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "channel_email_password" {
  count         = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.channel_email_password[0].id
  secret_string = aws_iam_access_key.ses_smtp[0].ses_smtp_password_v4
}

locals {
  # Consumed by ecs.tf's app env. Region-matched SMTP endpoint; STARTTLS :587
  # (the app's email_smtp_port default).
  ses_smtp_host  = "email-smtp.${var.aws_region}.amazonaws.com"
  email_username = var.alert_email == "" ? "" : aws_iam_access_key.ses_smtp[0].id
}
