# SES — the email alert channel (#1368), the AWS-native counterpart of the
# SMTP creds the Azure stack keeps in Key Vault. Everything here is gated on
# var.alert_email: empty (the default) creates nothing and the app's email
# channel stays off (config.py enables it only when EMAIL_TO + EMAIL_USERNAME
# + EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME are all set).
#
# Sandbox posture, stated honestly: a fresh SES account can only send FROM and
# TO verified identities, so alert_email is both the sender and the sole
# recipient — fine for a single-operator deployment; production fan-out needs
# an SES production-access request (an AWS support form, not Terraform).
#
# The identity requires a ONE-TIME human step: SES emails a verification link
# to alert_email at create time, and sends fail with "Email address is not
# verified" until it is clicked. Check with:
#   aws ses get-identity-verification-attributes --identities <alert_email>

resource "aws_ses_email_identity" "alert" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  email = var.alert_email
}

# Dedicated IAM user for SMTP: SES SMTP credentials ARE an IAM access key —
# the username is the key id and the password is Terraform's derived
# ses_smtp_password_v4 (the documented SigV4 derivation, region-specific).
# Scoped to SendRawEmail only (what SMTP submission uses), from this identity.
resource "aws_iam_user" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name  = "dataq-app-ses-smtp"
  tags  = { Name = "dataq-app-ses-smtp" }
}

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  statement {
    actions   = ["ses:SendRawEmail"]
    resources = [aws_ses_email_identity.alert[0].arn]
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_user_policy" "ses_smtp" {
  count  = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name   = "dataq-app-ses-smtp-send"
  user   = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ses_smtp[0].json
}

resource "aws_iam_access_key" "ses_smtp" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  user  = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
}

# The SMTP password goes into Secrets Manager UNDER THE APP PREFIX
# (dataq/channel-email-password): the task env's EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME
# already names `channel-email-password`, which the app resolves through its
# own SecretStore (SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager + AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX
# = dataq/) at send time — same read path as every connection credential, no
# extra task-definition secret injection.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "channel_email_password" {
  count = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  name  = "dataq/channel-email-password"
  # The app's sweep/rotation owns secrets under dataq/, but this one is
  # infra-owned: recovery_window 0 so a destroy/recreate cycle doesn't collide
  # with a soft-deleted name.
  recovery_window_in_days = 0
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "channel_email_password" {
  count         = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.channel_email_password[0].id
  secret_string = aws_iam_access_key.ses_smtp[0].ses_smtp_password_v4
}

locals {

# DataQ on AWS — Terraform (OpenTofu) runbook

A second, parallel deployment of DataQ (Azure stays the deployed prod — see
`deploy/terraform/azure/`), into a fresh, dedicated AWS account. Unlike the
Azure stack, nothing here is shared with another stack: this account exists
only for this deployment.

## What it creates

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| VPC, 2 public subnets, IGW, route table | Networking. No NAT Gateway (decision: public-subnets-no-NAT, ~$33/mo saved — ECS tasks get no public inbound access, only the ALB→frontend path is internet-reachable) |
| `aws_ecs_cluster.app` + 3 Fargate services (api, worker, frontend) + 1 task def (migrate) | The app itself. api is internal-only (Cloud Map DNS `api.dataq.local`); frontend is the sole public surface (behind the ALB); worker runs embedded celery-beat, `desired_count=1` always (cannot scale to zero) |
| `aws_cloudfront_distribution.app` → `aws_lb.app` (ALB, HTTP :80) | Public ingress. CloudFront terminates HTTPS on its default `*.cloudfront.net` cert (#1345 — Cognito requires an HTTPS redirect URI); the ALB admits only CloudFront's origin-facing ranges and forwards to the frontend target group |
| `aws_db_instance.app` (RDS Postgres, `db.t4g.micro`) | The app's own database — this stack creates it directly (no shared-server bootstrap dance like the Azure stack, since this account is dedicated) |
| `aws_elasticache_replication_group.app` (`cache.t4g.micro`, TLS + auth token) | Celery broker + rate-limit store |
| `aws_cognito_user_pool.app` + SPA client | OIDC identity provider, validated by the backend's provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026 amendment) — not Azure AD |
| `aws_secretsmanager_secret.*` (2, infra-owned) + IAM grants | `database-url`/`redis-url` (infra-owned, referenced by ARN in task defs) + the app's own runtime grant under `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX` (`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`) |
| `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` + `aws_iam_role.github_deploy` | GitHub Actions → AWS auth for the Deploy workflow, OIDC federation, no stored access keys |
| CloudWatch Log Groups (4) | Container logs. No APM/tracing wired up yet — the OTel core is vendor-neutral but the exporter shipped so far is Azure-only |

## Prerequisites

- **OpenTofu** (`tofu`), not Terraform — same ADR 0024 rationale as the Azure stack.
- **AWS CLI credentials** for a **scoped IAM user**, never root. This repo's own bring-up used `AWS_PROFILE=dataq-deploy` (set as the default in the operator's shell) — see the session notes for the IAM bootstrap steps (create user, attach a policy, remove root's access keys/login session).
- A **GitHub repo** with Actions enabled (for the OIDC federation to have something to trust).
- Nothing else pre-exists — this stack creates its own VPC, database, cache, etc. from scratch, unlike the Azure stack's shared-resource dependencies.

## Apply

```bash
cd deploy/terraform/aws
tofu init
# state_encryption_passphrase comes from your terraform.tfvars — see
# terraform.tfvars.example.
#
# Image tags (#1349): the services RUN these images from the first apply.
# publish-images.yml tags main merges as `main-<full sha>` (the bare `<sha>`
# tag is owned by the manual Azure deploy.yml and usually does NOT exist), and
# its `paths` filter skips merges that don't change image content — so use the
# last IMAGE-BEARING main commit, not the branch tip, and verify the tag
# exists before applying:
IMG_SHA=$(git log origin/main -1 --format=%H -- backend frontend pyproject.toml)
docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:main-${IMG_SHA}" > /dev/null  # must succeed
TF_VAR_app_db_password="REDACTED" \
tofu plan -input=false -out=tfplan \
  -var="image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}" \
  -var="frontend_image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}"
tofu apply -input=false tfplan
```

**Cost starts here.** `tofu apply` creates real, billable AWS resources (Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, ALB). Review the plan before applying. See the root-level deployment plan (in the session that built this stack) for the cost breakdown against the AWS free-tier credit.

## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow

```bash
tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn   # → repo secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name         # → repo variable ECS_CLUSTER
tofu output -raw frontend_url             # → sanity-check reachability
```

```bash
gh secret set AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN --body "$(tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn)"
gh variable set ECS_CLUSTER --body "$(tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name)"
gh variable set AWS_REGION --body "$(tofu output -raw -json | jq -r .aws_region.value 2>/dev/null || echo us-east-2)"
```

The companion `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` uses these to
`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` via OIDC, then runs the same sequence
the Azure `deploy.yml` runs, adapted to ECS:

1. build + push both images to GHCR under the immutable tag `aws-<commit sha>`
   (bare `<sha>` belongs to the Azure deploy.yml, `main-<sha>` to
   publish-images.yml — three workflows, three disjoint tag namespaces);
2. register a new `dataq-app-migrate` task-definition revision on the new
   image and `run-task` it with the api service's live network configuration,
   **waiting for exit 0** before anything rolls (fail-closed);
3. register new api/worker/frontend revisions, `update-service`, and
   `wait services-stable`, then verify the primary deployment's image really
   is the new tag (a circuit-breaker rollback to the old image must fail the
   run, not pass as "stable");
4. optional public-surface smoke (healthz/SPA 200, `/api` 401) — runs only
   when the `AWS_FRONTEND_URL` repo variable is set, since the CloudFront URL
   is deployment-specific and deliberately not tracked in the repo (#730).
   Set it with `gh variable set AWS_FRONTEND_URL --body "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)"`.

It is `workflow_dispatch`-only (Azure stays primary prod), takes an optional
`image_tag` input (blank → `aws-<sha>`), and needs no AWS-side registry
credential — the GHCR packages are public and ECS pulls them anonymously.

## State encryption

Same discipline as the Azure stack (`versions.tf`'s `encryption {}` block):
the local state holds the generated RDS/ElastiCache passwords in plaintext
without it. `state_encryption_passphrase` is a **data-at-rest key**, not a
credential — it cannot be revoked or re-minted, and losing it makes
`terraform.tfstate` permanently unreadable. Keep a second copy off this
machine. A wrong/missing passphrase fails closed
(`cipher: message authentication failed`) without corrupting the file.

## Verify

```bash
# Confirm exactly what got created, tagged for this stack:
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources \
  --tag-filters Key=Purpose,Values=dataq-app-aws

# Reachability (through the frontend — the sole public surface):
curl -s "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)/healthz"
```

Then in a browser: sign in through Cognito end-to-end, confirm `/api` and
`/mcp` return 401 unauthenticated without a credential, and run one real
suite against a live datasource to confirm the worker path.

## Known gaps in this pass (deliberately deferred, not silently skipped)

- No custom domain — the public URL is the CloudFront distribution's own
  `*.cloudfront.net` domain (HTTPS, default cert — #1345). Once a domain is
  chosen: Route53 + ACM cert + an `aliases` entry on the distribution.
- No private-subnet/NAT hardening — see `main.tf`'s decision note.
- No `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` yet — this stack only provisions the
  infra the workflow will drive.
- The Cognito `client_id`-vs-`aud` accommodation in `OidcBearerScheme`
  (backend) needs confirming against a real token from **this** pool once
  it's live — see `cognito.tf`'s comment.

content.content:
1	"""Request/task span instrumentation (WEEK7 A3 — App Insights spans).
2	
3	OTel-neutral core (ADR 0010): the OpenTelemetry SDK + FastAPI/Celery
4	instrumentations are vendor-neutral; the exporter backends live behind the
5	shared seam in ``otel.py`` (Azure Monitor and/or generic OTLP/HTTP — #589),
6	resolved from settings. Tracing is on when **any** backend resolves an exporter
7	(``otel.build_span_exporters``) — none ⇒ a complete no-op, matching the log
8	pipeline's gate. Spans and logs (#524) now share the same seam and Resource
9	(service.name).
10	
11	Deliberately the **exporter-only** Azure package (`azure-monitor-
12	opentelemetry-exporter`), NOT the `azure-monitor-opentelemetry` distro: the
13	distro auto-configures the logging pipeline and would double-configure the
14	structlog log bridge in ``logging.py``.
15	
16	All exporter imports are lazy (repo convention, see ``secrets.py``) so
17	deployments without telemetry never pay the import cost.
18	
19	Call-ordering constraint (learned the hard way in review): FastAPI
20	instrumentation patches ``app.build_middleware_stack``, and Starlette builds
21	the middleware stack on the FIRST ASGI call — which is the *lifespan scope
22	itself*. So ``instrument_fastapi`` MUST run at module scope (before the app
23	serves anything), never from inside the lifespan handler, or it silently
24	instruments nothing. ``backend/tests/core/test_tracing.py`` pins this with a
25	regression test against the real ``backend.app.main`` wiring.
26	"""
27	
28	from __future__ import annotations
29	
30	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Final
31	
32	from backend.app.core import otel
33	from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
34	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
35	
36	if TYPE_CHECKING:
37	    from fastapi import FastAPI
38	    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
39	    from opentelemetry.trace import Span
40	
41	log = get_logger(__name__)
42	
43	# URLs whose server spans are never recorded. Comma-separated regexes in the
44	# opentelemetry-util-http `excluded_urls` format: each part is `re.search`ed
45	# against the full request URL (scheme://host/path — the query string is not
46	# part of the match), so patterns must be ANCHORED to path boundaries or a
47	# hostname containing e.g. "healthz" would silently exclude every span.
48	# - `/healthz$` — probe noise.
49	# - `/api/v1/orchestration/events/` — the webhook receivers carry a secret in
50	#   the query string (`?token=<secret>`, ADR 0006 / #494) which must never
51	#   land in span attributes; exclusion happens before the span is created.
52	EXCLUDED_URLS: Final = "/healthz$,/api/v1/orchestration/events/"
53	
54	# Span attributes (old + new HTTP semconv) that may embed the request URL.
55	# `_scrub_query_hook` rewrites them to the path so query strings — which can
56	# carry PII (e.g. /users/search?q=<email>) — never reach App Insights. Same
57	# posture as the request log: path only (#494).
58	_URL_ATTRS: Final = ("http.url", "http.target", "url.full", "url.query")
59	
60	_provider: TracerProvider | None = None
61	
62	
63	def configure_tracing(service_name: str) -> None:
64	    """Install a TracerProvider exporting to the configured backend(s), or no-op.
65	
66	    Backends (Azure Monitor and/or generic OTLP/HTTP — #589) come from the shared
67	    ``otel`` seam. Idempotent per process (the global tracer provider can only be
68	    set once); safe to call from both the API module scope and the Celery
69	    worker-process-init signal.
70	    """
71	    global _provider
72	    if _provider is not None:
73	        return
74	    settings = get_settings()
75	    try:
76	        exporters = otel.build_span_exporters(settings)
77	        if not exporters:
78	            return
79	
80	        from opentelemetry import trace
81	        from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
82	        from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
83	
84	        provider = TracerProvider(resource=otel.build_resource(service_name))
85	        for exporter in exporters:
86	            provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
87	        trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
88	        _provider = provider
89	        log.info("tracing_configured", service_name=service_name, exporters=len(exporters))
90	    except Exception:
91	        # Same posture as the log bridge: an observability misconfig (bad OTLP
92	        # endpoint/headers, SDK drift) must not crash the API lifespan or the celery
93	        # worker-init signal. Leave _provider None so instrument_* no-op.
94	        log.warning("tracing_setup_failed", service_name=service_name, exc_info=True)
95	
96	
97	def _scrub_query_hook(span: Span, scope: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
98	    """server_request_hook: overwrite URL-bearing attributes with the path only."""
99	    if span is None or not span.is_recording():
100	        return
101	    path = str(scope.get("path", ""))
102	    for attr in _URL_ATTRS:

"""Request/task span instrumentation (WEEK7 A3 — App Insights spans).

OTel-neutral core (ADR 0010): the OpenTelemetry SDK + FastAPI/Celery
instrumentations are vendor-neutral; the exporter backends live behind the
shared seam in ``otel.py`` (Azure Monitor and/or generic OTLP/HTTP — #589),
resolved from settings. Tracing is on when **any** backend resolves an exporter
(``otel.build_span_exporters``) — none ⇒ a complete no-op, matching the log
pipeline's gate. Spans and logs (#524) now share the same seam and Resource
(service.name).

Deliberately the **exporter-only** Azure package (`azure-monitor-
opentelemetry-exporter`), NOT the `azure-monitor-opentelemetry` distro: the
distro auto-configures the logging pipeline and would double-configure the
structlog log bridge in ``logging.py``.

All exporter imports are lazy (repo convention, see ``secrets.py``) so
deployments without telemetry never pay the import cost.

Call-ordering constraint (learned the hard way in review): FastAPI
instrumentation patches ``app.build_middleware_stack``, and Starlette builds
the middleware stack on the FIRST ASGI call — which is the *lifespan scope
itself*. So ``instrument_fastapi`` MUST run at module scope (before the app
serves anything), never from inside the lifespan handler, or it silently
instruments nothing. ``backend/tests/core/test_tracing.py`` pins this with a
regression test against the real ``backend.app.main`` wiring.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Final

from backend.app.core import otel
from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from fastapi import FastAPI
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    from opentelemetry.trace import Span

log = get_logger(__name__)

# URLs whose server spans are never recorded. Comma-separated regexes in the
# opentelemetry-util-http `excluded_urls` format: each part is `re.search`ed
# against the full request URL (scheme://host/path — the query string is not
# part of the match), so patterns must be ANCHORED to path boundaries or a
# hostname containing e.g. "healthz" would silently exclude every span.
# - `/healthz$` — probe noise.
# - `/api/v1/orchestration/events/` — the webhook receivers carry a secret in
#   the query string (`?token=<secret>`, ADR 0006 / #494) which must never
#   land in span attributes; exclusion happens before the span is created.
EXCLUDED_URLS: Final = "/healthz$,/api/v1/orchestration/events/"

# Span attributes (old + new HTTP semconv) that may embed the request URL.
# `_scrub_query_hook` rewrites them to the path so query strings — which can
# carry PII (e.g. /users/search?q=<email>) — never reach App Insights. Same
# posture as the request log: path only (#494).
_URL_ATTRS: Final = ("http.url", "http.target", "url.full", "url.query")

_provider: TracerProvider | None = None


def configure_tracing(service_name: str) -> None:
    """Install a TracerProvider exporting to the configured backend(s), or no-op.

    Backends (Azure Monitor and/or generic OTLP/HTTP — #589) come from the shared
    ``otel`` seam. Idempotent per process (the global tracer provider can only be
    set once); safe to call from both the API module scope and the Celery
    worker-process-init signal.
    """
    global _provider
    if _provider is not None:
        return
    settings = get_settings()
    try:
        exporters = otel.build_span_exporters(settings)
        if not exporters:
            return

        from opentelemetry import trace
        from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
        from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

        provider = TracerProvider(resource=otel.build_resource(service_name))
        for exporter in exporters:
            provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
        trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
        _provider = provider
        log.info("tracing_configured", service_name=service_name, exporters=len(exporters))
    except Exception:
        # Same posture as the log bridge: an observability misconfig (bad OTLP
        # endpoint/headers, SDK drift) must not crash the API lifespan or the celery
        # worker-init signal. Leave _provider None so instrument_* no-op.
        log.warning("tracing_setup_failed", service_name=service_name, exc_info=True)


def _scrub_query_hook(span: Span, scope: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """server_request_hook: overwrite URL-bearing attributes with the path only."""
    if span is None or not span.is_recording():
        return
    path = str(scope.get("path", ""))
    for attr in _URL_ATTRS:
        span.set_attribute(attr, path if attr != "url.query" else "")


def instrument_fastapi(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Emit a server span per request (minus EXCLUDED_URLS). No-op when tracing is off.

    MUST be called at module scope, before the app's first ASGI call — see the
    module docstring's call-ordering constraint.
    """
    if _provider is None:
        return
    from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor

    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(
        app,
        tracer_provider=_provider,
        excluded_urls=EXCLUDED_URLS,
        server_request_hook=_scrub_query_hook,
    )


def instrument_celery() -> None:
    """Emit a span per Celery task run/publish. No-op when tracing is off.

    Must run on BOTH sides: the worker (task/consumer spans, via
    worker_process_init) AND the API process (producer spans + traceparent
    header injection on publish — without it, task spans are orphaned root
    traces unlinked from the triggering request).
    """
    if _provider is None:
        return
    from opentelemetry.instrumentation.celery import CeleryInstrumentor

    CeleryInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=_provider)


def tag_request_id(request_id: str) -> None:
    """Stamp the request_id onto the current span so App Insights spans can be
    joined to the structlog lines keyed on the same id. No-op when tracing is
    off or no span is recording."""
    if _provider is None:
        return
    from opentelemetry import trace

    span = trace.get_current_span()
    if span.is_recording():
        span.set_attribute("dataq.request_id", request_id)

| `aws_cognito_user_pool.app` + SPA client | OIDC identity provider, validated by the backend's provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026 amendment) — not Azure AD |

# exists before applying:
IMG_SHA=$(git log origin/main -1 --format=%H -- backend frontend pyproject.toml)
docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:main-${IMG_SHA}" > /dev/null  # must succeed

tofu plan -input=false -out=tfplan \
  -var="image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}" \

# DataQ on AWS — Terraform (OpenTofu) runbook

A second, parallel deployment of DataQ (Azure stays the deployed prod — see
`deploy/terraform/azure/`), into a fresh, dedicated AWS account. Unlike the
Azure stack, nothing here is shared with another stack: this account exists
only for this deployment.

## What it creates

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| VPC, 2 public subnets, IGW, route table | Networking. No NAT Gateway (decision: public-subnets-no-NAT, ~$33/mo saved — ECS tasks get no public inbound access, only the ALB→frontend path is internet-reachable) |
| `aws_ecs_cluster.app` + 3 Fargate services (api, worker, frontend) + 1 task def (migrate) | The app itself. api is internal-only (Cloud Map DNS `api.dataq.local`); frontend is the sole public surface (behind the ALB); worker runs embedded celery-beat, `desired_count=1` always (cannot scale to zero) |
| `aws_cloudfront_distribution.app` → `aws_lb.app` (ALB, HTTP :80) | Public ingress. CloudFront terminates HTTPS on its default `*.cloudfront.net` cert (#1345 — Cognito requires an HTTPS redirect URI); the ALB admits only CloudFront's origin-facing ranges and forwards to the frontend target group |
| `aws_db_instance.app` (RDS Postgres, `db.t4g.micro`) | The app's own database — this stack creates it directly (no shared-server bootstrap dance like the Azure stack, since this account is dedicated) |
| `aws_elasticache_replication_group.app` (`cache.t4g.micro`, TLS + auth token) | Celery broker + rate-limit store |
| `aws_cognito_user_pool.app` + SPA client | OIDC identity provider, validated by the backend's provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026 amendment) — not Azure AD |
| `aws_secretsmanager_secret.*` (2, infra-owned) + IAM grants | `database-url`/`redis-url` (infra-owned, referenced by ARN in task defs) + the app's own runtime grant under `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX` (`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`) |
| `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` + `aws_iam_role.github_deploy` | GitHub Actions → AWS auth for the Deploy workflow, OIDC federation, no stored access keys |
| CloudWatch Log Groups (6) | Container logs (4) + `/dataq-app/otel` (app OTel logs via the collector) + `/dataq-app/adot` (the collector's own stdout) |
| ADOT collector sidecars (in the api + worker task defs, `adot.tf`) | APM/tracing (#1369): the app's vendor-neutral OTLP export (`core/otel.py`, #589) points at `localhost:4318`; the sidecar ships traces → **X-Ray**, OTel logs → CloudWatch. Config injected via `AOT_CONFIG_CONTENT` (minimal two-pipeline config, minimal IAM) |

## Prerequisites

- **OpenTofu** (`tofu`), not Terraform — same ADR 0024 rationale as the Azure stack.
- **AWS CLI credentials** for a **scoped IAM user**, never root. This repo's own bring-up used `AWS_PROFILE=dataq-deploy` (set as the default in the operator's shell) — see the session notes for the IAM bootstrap steps (create user, attach a policy, remove root's access keys/login session).
- A **GitHub repo** with Actions enabled (for the OIDC federation to have something to trust).
- Nothing else pre-exists — this stack creates its own VPC, database, cache, etc. from scratch, unlike the Azure stack's shared-resource dependencies.

## Apply

```bash
cd deploy/terraform/aws
tofu init
# state_encryption_passphrase comes from your terraform.tfvars — see
# terraform.tfvars.example.
#
# Image tags (#1349): the services RUN these images from the first apply.
# publish-images.yml tags main merges as `main-<full sha>` (the bare `<sha>`
# tag is owned by the manual Azure deploy.yml and usually does NOT exist), and
# its `paths` filter skips merges that don't change image content — so use the
# last IMAGE-BEARING main commit, not the branch tip, and verify the tag
# exists before applying:
IMG_SHA=$(git log origin/main -1 --format=%H -- backend frontend pyproject.toml)
docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:main-${IMG_SHA}" > /dev/null  # must succeed
TF_VAR_app_db_password="REDACTED" \
tofu plan -input=false -out=tfplan \
  -var="image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}" \
  -var="frontend_image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}"
tofu apply -input=false tfplan
```

**Cost starts here.** `tofu apply` creates real, billable AWS resources (Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, ALB). Review the plan before applying. See the root-level deployment plan (in the session that built this stack) for the cost breakdown against the AWS free-tier credit.

## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow

```bash
tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn   # → repo secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name         # → repo variable ECS_CLUSTER
tofu output -raw frontend_url             # → sanity-check reachability
```

```bash
gh secret set AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN --body "$(tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn)"
gh variable set ECS_CLUSTER --body "$(tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name)"
gh variable set AWS_REGION --body "$(tofu output -raw -json | jq -r .aws_region.value 2>/dev/null || echo us-east-2)"
```

The companion `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` uses these to
`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` via OIDC, then runs the same sequence
the Azure `deploy.yml` runs, adapted to ECS:

1. build + push both images to GHCR under the immutable tag `aws-<commit sha>`
   (bare `<sha>` belongs to the Azure deploy.yml, `main-<sha>` to
   publish-images.yml — three workflows, three disjoint tag namespaces);
2. register a new `dataq-app-migrate` task-definition revision on the new
   image and `run-task` it with the api service's live network configuration,
   **waiting for exit 0** before anything rolls (fail-closed);
3. register new api/worker/frontend revisions, `update-service`, and
   `wait services-stable`, then verify the primary deployment's image really
   is the new tag (a circuit-breaker rollback to the old image must fail the
   run, not pass as "stable");
4. optional public-surface smoke (healthz/SPA 200, `/api` 401) — runs only
   when the `AWS_FRONTEND_URL` repo variable is set, since the CloudFront URL
   is deployment-specific and deliberately not tracked in the repo (#730).
   Set it with `gh variable set AWS_FRONTEND_URL --body "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)"`.

It is `workflow_dispatch`-only (Azure stays primary prod), takes an optional
`image_tag` input (blank → `aws-<sha>`), and needs no AWS-side registry
credential — the GHCR packages are public and ECS pulls them anonymously.

## State encryption

Same discipline as the Azure stack (`versions.tf`'s `encryption {}` block):
the local state holds the generated RDS/ElastiCache passwords in plaintext
without it. `state_encryption_passphrase` is a **data-at-rest key**, not a
credential — it cannot be revoked or re-minted, and losing it makes
`terraform.tfstate` permanently unreadable. Keep a second copy off this
machine. A wrong/missing passphrase fails closed
(`cipher: message authentication failed`) without corrupting the file.

## Verify

```bash
# Confirm exactly what got created, tagged for this stack:
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources \
  --tag-filters Key=Purpose,Values=dataq-app-aws

# Reachability (through the frontend — the sole public surface):
curl -s "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)/healthz"
```

Then in a browser: sign in through Cognito end-to-end, confirm `/api` and
`/mcp` return 401 unauthenticated without a credential, and run one real
suite against a live datasource to confirm the worker path.

## Known gaps in this pass (deliberately deferred, not silently skipped)

- No custom domain — the public URL is the CloudFront distribution's own
  `*.cloudfront.net` domain (HTTPS, default cert — #1345). Once a domain is
  chosen: Route53 + ACM cert + an `aliases` entry on the distribution.
- No private-subnet/NAT hardening — see `main.tf`'s decision note.
- No `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` yet — this stack only provisions the
  infra the workflow will drive.
- The Cognito `client_id`-vs-`aud` accommodation in `OidcBearerScheme`
  (backend) needs confirming against a real token from **this** pool once
  it's live — see `cognito.tf`'s comment.

# Shared ECS deploy helpers for deploy-aws.yml — source this, don't execute it.
# Requires: aws + jq on PATH, and scripts/ci/retry.sh sourced first (retry()).
#
# One implementation of the describe → image-swap → register → update →
# wait → verify roll, so the migrate, api/worker, and frontend steps cannot
# silently diverge (PR #1365 review). Values are returned via shell variables
# assigned INSIDE the retried functions — retry() logs ::warning:: lines to
# stdout, so `var=$(retry fn)` would swallow them into the captured value.

# Register a new revision of task-definition family $1 with its (single)
# container's image swapped to $2. Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN.
ecs_register_revision() {
  local family=$1 image=$2 td new_td
  td=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$family" \
         --query taskDefinition --output json)
  # del(): the output-only fields describe returns that register rejects.
  new_td=$(jq --arg img "$image" \
    '.containerDefinitions[0].image = $img
     | del(.taskDefinitionArn, .revision, .status, .requiresAttributes,
           .compatibilities, .registeredAt, .registeredBy, .deregisteredAt)' \
    <<<"$td")
  _ecs_register() {
    ECS_REGISTERED_ARN=$(aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json "$new_td" \
      --query 'taskDefinition.taskDefinitionArn' --output text)
  }
  retry _ecs_register
}

# Roll service $2 on cluster $1 to image $3 (service name == family name in
# this stack). Sets ECS_REGISTERED_ARN to the revision it rolled to.
ecs_roll_service() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3
  ecs_register_revision "$service" "$image"
  _ecs_update() {
    aws ecs update-service --cluster "$cluster" --service "$service" \
      --task-definition "$ECS_REGISTERED_ARN" \
      --query 'service.serviceName' --output text >/dev/null
  }
  retry _ecs_update
  echo "$service -> $ECS_REGISTERED_ARN"
}

# Wait for the listed services on cluster $1 to stabilise. TWO waiter laps
# (each 15s x 40 = 10 min): a perfectly normal rollout can exceed one lap
# because the ALB target group's default 300s deregistration drain sits on
# the deployment-complete path — a converging deploy must not spuriously
# fail on the waiter's fixed cap (PR #1365 review).
ecs_wait_stable() {
  local cluster=$1
  shift
  if ! aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"; then
    echo "::warning::services-stable waiter lap 1 timed out — one more lap (ALB drain can push a normal rollout past 10 min)"
    aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$cluster" --services "$@"
  fi
}

# Verify service $2's PRIMARY deployment on cluster $1 actually runs image $3:
# an ECS deployment-circuit-breaker rollback to the old image reports stable,
# and "stable on the old code" must fail the deploy, not pass it.
ecs_verify_image() {
  local cluster=$1 service=$2 image=$3 live_td live_img
  live_td=$(aws ecs describe-services --cluster "$cluster" --services "$service" \
              --query 'services[0].deployments[0].taskDefinition' --output text)
  live_img=$(aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition "$live_td" \
               --query 'taskDefinition.containerDefinitions[0].image' --output text)
  if [[ "$live_img" != "$image" ]]; then
    echo "::error::$service image mismatch after rollout: $live_img (wanted $image)"
    return 1
  fi
}

1	# DataQ on AWS — Terraform (OpenTofu) runbook
2	
3	A second, parallel deployment of DataQ (Azure stays the deployed prod — see
4	`deploy/terraform/azure/`), into a fresh, dedicated AWS account. Unlike the
5	Azure stack, nothing here is shared with another stack: this account exists
6	only for this deployment.
7	
8	## What it creates
9	
10	| Resource | Purpose |
11	|---|---|
12	| VPC, 2 public subnets, IGW, route table | Networking. No NAT Gateway (decision: public-subnets-no-NAT, ~$33/mo saved — ECS tasks get no public inbound access, only the ALB→frontend path is internet-reachable) |
13	| `aws_ecs_cluster.app` + 3 Fargate services (api, worker, frontend) + 1 task def (migrate) | The app itself. api is internal-only (Cloud Map DNS `api.dataq.local`); frontend is the sole public surface (behind the ALB); worker runs embedded celery-beat, `desired_count=1` always (cannot scale to zero) |
14	| `aws_cloudfront_distribution.app` → `aws_lb.app` (ALB, HTTP :80) | Public ingress. CloudFront terminates HTTPS on its default `*.cloudfront.net` cert (#1345 — Cognito requires an HTTPS redirect URI); the ALB admits only CloudFront's origin-facing ranges and forwards to the frontend target group |
15	| `aws_db_instance.app` (RDS Postgres, `db.t4g.micro`) | The app's own database — this stack creates it directly (no shared-server bootstrap dance like the Azure stack, since this account is dedicated) |
16	| `aws_elasticache_replication_group.app` (`cache.t4g.micro`, TLS + auth token) | Celery broker + rate-limit store |
17	| `aws_cognito_user_pool.app` + SPA client | OIDC identity provider, validated by the backend's provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026 amendment) — not Azure AD |
18	| `aws_secretsmanager_secret.*` (2–3, infra-owned) + IAM grants | `database-url`/`redis-url` (infra-owned, referenced by ARN in task defs) + the app's own runtime grant under `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX` (`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`) + when `alert_email` is set, `<prefix>/channel-email-password` (infra-written, app-read — the SES SMTP password, #1368) |
19	| `aws_ses_email_identity` + `aws_iam_user.ses_smtp` (+key/policy) — only when `alert_email` set | Email alert channel (#1368): SES identity (sandbox — sender = recipient = `alert_email`, needs the one-time verification click) + a send-only SMTP credential |
20	| `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` + `aws_iam_role.github_deploy` | GitHub Actions → AWS auth for the Deploy workflow, OIDC federation, no stored access keys |
21	| CloudWatch Log Groups (6) | Container logs (4) + `/dataq-app/otel` (app OTel logs via the collector) + `/dataq-app/adot` (the collector's own stdout) |
22	| ADOT collector sidecars (in the api + worker task defs, `adot.tf`) | APM/tracing (#1369): the app's vendor-neutral OTLP export (`core/otel.py`, #589) points at `localhost:4318`; the sidecar ships traces → **X-Ray**, OTel logs → CloudWatch. Config injected via `AOT_CONFIG_CONTENT` (minimal two-pipeline config, minimal IAM) |
23	
24	## Prerequisites
25	
26	- **OpenTofu** (`tofu`), not Terraform — same ADR 0024 rationale as the Azure stack.
27	- **AWS CLI credentials** for a **scoped IAM user**, never root. This repo's own bring-up used `AWS_PROFILE=dataq-deploy` (set as the default in the operator's shell) — see the session notes for the IAM bootstrap steps (create user, attach a policy, remove root's access keys/login session).
28	- A **GitHub repo** with Actions enabled (for the OIDC federation to have something to trust).
29	- Nothing else pre-exists — this stack creates its own VPC, database, cache, etc. from scratch, unlike the Azure stack's shared-resource dependencies.
30	
31	## Apply
32	
33	```bash
34	cd deploy/terraform/aws
35	tofu init
36	# state_encryption_passphrase comes from your terraform.tfvars — see
37	# terraform.tfvars.example.
38	#
39	# Image tags (#1349): the services RUN these images from the first apply.
40	# publish-images.yml tags main merges as `main-<full sha>` (the bare `<sha>`
41	# tag is owned by the manual Azure deploy.yml and usually does NOT exist), and
42	# its `paths` filter skips merges that don't change image content — so use the
43	# last IMAGE-BEARING main commit, not the branch tip, and verify the tag
44	# exists before applying:
45	IMG_SHA=$(git log origin/main -1 --format=%H -- backend frontend pyproject.toml)
46	docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:main-${IMG_SHA}" > /dev/null  # must succeed
47	TF_VAR_app_db_password="REDACTED" \
48	tofu plan -input=false -out=tfplan \
49	  -var="image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}" \
50	  -var="frontend_image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}"
51	tofu apply -input=false tfplan
52	```
53	
54	**Cost starts here.** `tofu apply` creates real, billable AWS resources (Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, ALB). Review the plan before applying. See the root-level deployment plan (in the session that built this stack) for the cost breakdown against the AWS free-tier credit.
55	
56	## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow
57	
58	```bash
59	tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn   # → repo secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
60	tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name         # → repo variable ECS_CLUSTER
61	tofu output -raw frontend_url             # → sanity-check reachability
62	```
63	
64	```bash
65	gh secret set AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN --body "$(tofu output -raw github_deploy_role_arn)"
66	gh variable set ECS_CLUSTER --body "$(tofu output -raw ecs_cluster_name)"
67	gh variable set AWS_REGION --body "$(tofu output -raw -json | jq -r .aws_region.value 2>/dev/null || echo us-east-2)"
68	```
69	
70	The companion `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` uses these to
71	`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` via OIDC, then runs the same sequence
72	the Azure `deploy.yml` runs, adapted to ECS:
73	
74	1. build + push both images to GHCR under the immutable tag `aws-<commit sha>`
75	   (bare `<sha>` belongs to the Azure deploy.yml, `main-<sha>` to
76	   publish-images.yml — three workflows, three disjoint tag namespaces);
77	2. register a new `dataq-app-migrate` task-definition revision on the new
78	   image and `run-task` it with the api service's live network configuration,
79	   **waiting for exit 0** before anything rolls (fail-closed);
80	3. register new api/worker/frontend revisions, `update-service`, and
81	   `wait services-stable`, then verify the primary deployment's image really
82	   is the new tag (a circuit-breaker rollback to the old image must fail the
83	   run, not pass as "stable");
84	4. optional public-surface smoke (healthz/SPA 200, `/api` 401) — runs only
85	   when the `AWS_FRONTEND_URL` repo variable is set, since the CloudFront URL
86	   is deployment-specific and deliberately not tracked in the repo (#730).
87	   Set it with `gh variable set AWS_FRONTEND_URL --body "$(tofu output -raw frontend_url)"`.
88	
89	It is `workflow_dispatch`-only (Azure stays primary prod), takes an optional
90	`image_tag` input (blank → `aws-<sha>`), and needs no AWS-side registry
91	credential — the GHCR packages are public and ECS pulls them anonymously.
92	
93	## Rolling task-definition changes (env vars, sidecars)
94	
95	The api/worker/frontend task definitions carry `lifecycle { ignore_changes =
96	[container_definitions] }` (CI rolls images out-of-band), so a Terraform-side
97	change to env vars or sidecar containers is **silently ignored by a plain
98	apply**. To roll one:
99	
100	```bash
101	tofu apply -replace=aws_ecs_task_definition.api ... # forces a new revision from config
102	aws ecs update-service --cluster dataq-app --service dataq-app-api \
103	  --task-definition dataq-app-api --force-new-deployment   # family name → latest revision
104	```

class SuiteNotificationUpdate(ApiModel):
    enabled: bool = True
    # Default 'warn' matches the no-config fallback, so an omitted threshold
    # doesn't silently tighten delivery (a saved config keeps the prior behaviour).
    alert_on: Literal["fail", "warn", "always"] = "warn"
    # Each override is tri-state: omit/null = leave the stored value unchanged;
    # "" = clear (fall back to the workspace config); a value = set it. The https /
    # host / email-format checks live in the service (clean DataQError 422s), not
    # Pydantic validators (whose ValueError ctx isn't JSON-serializable here).
    webhook: str | None = None  # per-suite Teams webhook (write-only secret)
    slack_webhook: str | None = None  # per-suite Slack webhook (write-only secret, #633)
    email_recipients: str | None = None  # per-suite email recipients, comma-separated (#633)


def _read(config: SuiteNotification | None) -> SuiteNotificationRead:
    if config is None:

            enabled=True,
            alert_on=svc.DEFAULT_ALERT_ON,
            has_webhook=False,
            has_slack_webhook=False,

        has_webhook=config.webhook_secret_ref is not None,
        has_slack_webhook=config.slack_webhook_secret_ref is not None,

# SES — the email alert channel (#1368), the AWS-native counterpart of the
# SMTP creds the Azure stack keeps in Key Vault. Everything here is gated on
# var.alert_email: empty (the default) creates nothing and the app's email
# channel stays off (config.py enables it only when EMAIL_TO + EMAIL_USERNAME
# + EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME are all set).
#
# Sandbox posture, stated honestly: a fresh SES account can only send FROM and
# TO verified identities, so alert_email is both the sender and the sole
# recipient — fine for a single-operator deployment; production fan-out needs
# an SES production-access request (an AWS support form, not Terraform).
#
# The identity requires a ONE-TIME human step: SES emails a verification link
# to alert_email at create time, and sends fail with "Email address is not
# verified" until it is clicked. Check with:
#   aws ses get-identity-verification-attributes --identities <alert_email>

locals {
  # One gate for every resource in this file (PR #1370 review — the condition
  # was copy-pasted per resource, so a future edit could invert one silently).
  ses_enabled = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
}

resource "aws_ses_email_identity" "alert" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  email = var.alert_email
}

# Dedicated IAM user for SMTP: SES SMTP credentials ARE an IAM access key —
# the username is the key id and the password is Terraform's derived
# ses_smtp_password_v4 (the documented SigV4 derivation, region-specific).
# Scoped to SendRawEmail only (what SMTP submission uses), from this identity.
resource "aws_iam_user" "ses_smtp" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  name  = "dataq-app-ses-smtp"
  tags  = { Name = "dataq-app-ses-smtp" }
}

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ses_smtp" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  statement {
    actions   = ["ses:SendRawEmail"]
    resources = [aws_ses_email_identity.alert[0].arn]
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_user_policy" "ses_smtp" {
  count  = local.ses_enabled
  name   = "dataq-app-ses-smtp-send"
  user   = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ses_smtp[0].json
}

resource "aws_iam_access_key" "ses_smtp" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  user  = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
}

# The SMTP password goes into Secrets Manager UNDER THE APP PREFIX
# (dataq/channel-email-password): the task env's EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME
# already names `channel-email-password`, which the app resolves through its
# own SecretStore (SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager + AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX
# = dataq/) at send time — same read path as every connection credential, no
# extra task-definition secret injection.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "channel_email_password" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  name  = "${var.aws_secrets_manager_prefix}/channel-email-password"
  # The app's sweep/rotation owns secrets under dataq/, but this one is

  # with a soft-deleted name.
  recovery_window_in_days = 0
}

}

# SES — the email alert channel (#1368), the AWS-native counterpart of the
# SMTP creds the Azure stack keeps in Key Vault. Everything here is gated on
# var.alert_email: empty (the default) creates nothing and the app's email
# channel stays off (config.py enables it only when EMAIL_TO + EMAIL_USERNAME
# + EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME are all set).
#
# Sandbox posture, stated honestly: a fresh SES account can only send FROM and
# TO verified identities, so alert_email is both the sender and the sole
# recipient — fine for a single-operator deployment; production fan-out needs
# an SES production-access request (an AWS support form, not Terraform).
#
# The identity requires a ONE-TIME human step: SES emails a verification link
# to alert_email at create time, and sends fail with "Email address is not
# verified" until it is clicked. Check with:
#   aws ses get-identity-verification-attributes --identities <alert_email>

locals {
  # One gate for every resource in this file (PR #1370 review — the condition
  # was copy-pasted per resource, so a future edit could invert one silently).
  ses_enabled = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  # Recipient defaults to the sender; a distinct alert_email_to needs its OWN
  # verified identity while the account is in the SES sandbox.
  alert_email_to = var.alert_email_to != "" ? var.alert_email_to : var.alert_email
}

  count = local.ses_enabled

gh issue create --title "SES send-only IAM policy denies sandbox recipients — ses:SendRawEmail is authorized against recipient identity ARNs too" --label "bug,ops,priority/P2" --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --body "Live E2E of the #1368 email channel with a distinct recipient (#1372, \`alert_email_to=royarijit04@outlook.com\`) failed at the real send with:

\`\`\`
SMTPDataError: (554, \"Access denied: User 'arn:aws:iam::...:user/dataq-app-ses-smtp' is not authorized to perform 'ses:SendRawEmail' on resource 'arn:aws:ses:...:identity/royarijit04@outlook.com'\")
\`\`\`

\`ses.tf\` scopes the SMTP user's \`ses:SendRawEmail\` to the **sender** identity ARN only. That was reviewed in #1372 and explicitly assessed as correct ('SES evaluates SendRawEmail against the From identity, not recipients') — **the live send disproves that**: in the sandbox, each recipient identity is also an authorization resource for the send. Worked when sender == recipient (one ARN covered both roles), broke the moment they differed — invisible to validate/plan/review, the #953 class again.

**Fix:** include every identity this file creates (sender + all \`alert_to\` recipients) in the policy resources." 2>&1 | tail -1

# SES — the email alert channel (#1368), the AWS-native counterpart of the
# SMTP creds the Azure stack keeps in Key Vault. Everything here is gated on
# var.alert_email: empty (the default) creates nothing and the app's email
# channel stays off (config.py enables it only when EMAIL_TO + EMAIL_USERNAME
# + EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME are all set).
#
# Sandbox posture, stated honestly: a fresh SES account can only send FROM and
# TO verified identities. alert_email is the sender (and the default
# recipient); alert_email_to sets distinct recipient(s), each getting its own
# verified identity below. Production fan-out to arbitrary addresses needs an
# SES production-access request (an AWS support form, not Terraform).
#
# The identity requires a ONE-TIME human step: SES emails a verification link
# to alert_email at create time, and sends fail with "Email address is not
# verified" until it is clicked. Check with:
#   aws ses get-identity-verification-attributes --identities <alert_email>

locals {
  # One gate for every resource in this file (PR #1370 review — the condition
  # was copy-pasted per resource, so a future edit could invert one silently).
  ses_enabled = var.alert_email == "" ? 0 : 1
  # Recipients default to the sender; every distinct recipient needs its OWN
  # verified identity while the account is in the SES sandbox. EMAIL_TO is
  # comma-separated on the backend (config.py), so the identity set is built
  # per address — a comma list handed to one VerifyEmailIdentity would fail
  # the apply (PR #1372 review).
  alert_email_to = var.alert_email_to != "" ? var.alert_email_to : var.alert_email
  alert_to_identities = local.ses_enabled == 1 ? toset([
    for a in split(",", local.alert_email_to) : trimspace(a)
    if trimspace(a) != "" && trimspace(a) != var.alert_email
  ]) : toset([])
}

# The channel only turns on when the SENDER exists (config.py gates on
# EMAIL_USERNAME, which derives from alert_email) — setting only the recipient
# is a silent no-op, so say so at plan time (PR #1372 review).
check "alert_email_to_requires_sender" {
  assert {
    condition     = var.alert_email_to == "" || var.alert_email != ""
    error_message = "alert_email_to is set but alert_email is empty - the email channel stays OFF (no sender identity/SMTP credential is created and EMAIL_USERNAME stays empty). Set alert_email too."
  }
}

resource "aws_ses_email_identity" "alert" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  email = var.alert_email
}

# Sandbox rule: every RECIPIENT must be verified too, so each distinct TO
# address gets its own identity (its own one-time verification click).
# Collapses to nothing when alert_email_to is unset/equal to the sender.
resource "aws_ses_email_identity" "alert_to" {
  for_each = local.alert_to_identities
  email    = each.value
}

# Dedicated IAM user for SMTP: SES SMTP credentials ARE an IAM access key —
# the username is the key id and the password is Terraform's derived
# ses_smtp_password_v4 (the documented SigV4 derivation, region-specific).
# Scoped to SendRawEmail only (what SMTP submission uses), from this identity.
resource "aws_iam_user" "ses_smtp" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  name  = "dataq-app-ses-smtp"
  tags  = { Name = "dataq-app-ses-smtp" }
}

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ses_smtp" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  statement {
    actions   = ["ses:SendRawEmail"]
    resources = [aws_ses_email_identity.alert[0].arn]
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_user_policy" "ses_smtp" {
  count  = local.ses_enabled
  name   = "dataq-app-ses-smtp-send"
  user   = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ses_smtp[0].json
}

resource "aws_iam_access_key" "ses_smtp" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  user  = aws_iam_user.ses_smtp[0].name
}

# The SMTP password goes into Secrets Manager UNDER THE APP PREFIX
# (dataq/channel-email-password): the task env's EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME
# already names `channel-email-password`, which the app resolves through its
# own SecretStore (SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager + AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX
# = dataq/) at send time — same read path as every connection credential, no
# extra task-definition secret injection.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "channel_email_password" {
  count = local.ses_enabled
  name  = "${var.aws_secrets_manager_prefix}/channel-email-password"
  # The app's sweep/rotation owns secrets under dataq/, but this one is
  # infra-owned: recovery_window 0 so a destroy/recreate cycle doesn't collide
  # with a soft-deleted name.
  recovery_window_in_days = 0
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "channel_email_password" {
  count         = local.ses_enabled
  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.channel_email_password[0].id
  secret_string = aws_iam_access_key.ses_smtp[0].ses_smtp_password_v4
}

locals {
  # Consumed by ecs.tf's app env. Region-matched SMTP endpoint; STARTTLS :587
  # (the app's email_smtp_port default).
  ses_smtp_host  = "email-smtp.${var.aws_region}.amazonaws.com"
  email_username = var.alert_email == "" ? "" : aws_iam_access_key.ses_smtp[0].id
}

Skill "code-review" completed (forked execution).

Result:
The diff is a single Terraform statement change in `deploy/terraform/aws/ses.tf`. Running the angles inline (per the standing sequential/no-agents budget note), since the scope is one hunk.

**Angle A (line-by-line):** `concat([aws_ses_email_identity.alert[0].arn], [for identity in aws_ses_email_identity.alert_to : identity.arn])` — the `alert[0]` index is safe because the enclosing `data` block has `count = local.ses_enabled`, so it's never evaluated when the identity doesn't exist. Iterating a `for_each` resource yields values in deterministic key order, so the rendered policy JSON is stable across applies (no perma-diff). `tofu validate` was run clean per the PR body.

**Angle B (removed behavior):** the sender-only scoping was the bug being fixed (#1373, proven by a live 554); the sender ARN is retained in the new list. Nothing narrowed.

**Angle C (cross-file):** `aws_ses_email_identity.alert_to` is gated to empty via the `local.alert_to_identities` ternary when `ses_enabled == 0`, and `local.alert_to_identities` already excludes the sender and blank entries — so no duplicate ARNs and no dangling reference. `ecs.tf`'s `EMAIL_TO` consumes the same `local.alert_email_to`, so the identity set and the policy resources move together with the env var on every apply.

**Reuse/Simplification/Efficiency:** the `[for ...]` over a two-element concat is idiomatic HCL for a for_each resource; `values(...)[*].arn` would be equivalent, not simpler. No waste.

**Altitude:** the fix is at the right depth — it generalizes the resource list from "sender" to "sender + every managed recipient identity" rather than special-casing one recipient. One inherent side effect I examined and judged non-actionable: listing recipient identity ARNs also permits the SMTP user to use those identities as *From* addresses (SES IAM can't distinguish sender-use from recipient-use of an identity ARN), but that widening is unavoidable for the fix, all identities are account-owned, and the user is a dedicated alerts-only SMTP principal.

**Conventions:** no CLAUDE.md rule touches this — the comment documents the live-evidence rationale (`#1373`, "only-live-is-evidence"), consistent with the repo's practice.

Sequencing is **subscription-driven**: Weeks 1–3 extract everything that needs the expiring Snowflake (lapses within days) and Azure (~2026-07-25) subscriptions, then wind down gracefully; Weeks 4–6 run the roadmap's recommended opening sequence (Theme-1 `schema_drift` + `anomaly` → scale-aware execution G-b → incident/lineage design G-d — the G-d design half, #596, was pulled forward and done in W3, 2026-07-10) on cloud-independent infra; W7 is the stretch/burn-down buffer. See [Cycle plan](#cycle-plan--v11-6-weeks--stretch-2026-07-04--2026-08-22) below. |

(Previous — **43** open repo-wide / **26** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-12 after a two-batch quick-fruit sweep of small `v1.1 Backlog` issues, six PRs total, none merged out of order — each opened, CI-verified, mandatory `/code-review`'d, and (for two of the six) corrected against a real review finding before merge. **Batch 1** — [#1305](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1305) closed [#1264](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1264) (lineage floor-denial message named the wrong grant + a `NoReturn` docstring overstated its own effect — both cosmetic/wording; review's own sibling-bug check found the identical mislabeling also affects the ACCESS_HISTORY tier, left unfixed and filed as [#1309](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1309) since #1264's scope was OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES specifically), [#1306](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1306) closed [#1266](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1266) (psycopg2-only `connect_args` keys had no driver guard — added a shared `psycopg_connect_args()` helper; review caught two real bugs in the fix's own first pass, both corrected before merge: a `drivername.startswith("postgresql+psycopg")` prefix check misclassified a bare `postgresql://` URL as non-psycopg even though SQLAlchemy resolves it to psycopg2 by default — the single most common `DATABASE_URL` shape — silently dropping `connect_timeout`/keepalives for it; and the `options` lock-timeout key was left unconditional with a false "portable across drivers" comment, still crashing a genuinely non-psycopg driver on the exact `TypeError` the guard was built to prevent), [#1308](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1308) closed [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation warnings — `Modal.maskClosable`→`mask.closable`, `Select.onDropdownVisibleChange`→`onOpenChange`, `Drawer.width`→`size` — verified against the installed antd 6.5.1 types; review's git-history trace found the `Drawer.width` pattern had already been fixed once codebase-wide by #516, and both new sites were written *after* that PR landed, i.e. a genuine regression with nothing to stop a third recurrence — filed as [#1310](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1310)); **#1307** filed alongside #1305/#1306, a deferred-by-design robustness nit (the #1306 message-substitution's string-equality coupling to the classifier's literal return value). **Batch 2** — [#1311](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1311) closed [#936](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/936) (3-part `catalog.schema.table` names left the catalog/schema unquoted, so a mixed-case Unity Catalog namespace silently folded; fixed by threading an explicit `dialect` through `core_table` and quoting each part via the dialect's own `identifier_preparer` — CI caught a missed third call site, `dataset_reader.py`'s ADR-0015 comparison-kind reader, not found by the original grep sweep, fixed same-PR before merge), [#1312](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1312) closed [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261) (centralized the #1226 already-logged-traceback downgrade into a new structlog processor instead of duplicating the opt-in check per caller; review found the processor only rewrote the *stdout* JSON body, leaving the raw stdlib `LogRecord` — which the OTel/App-Insights export handler reads directly — still at ERROR severity with the full traceback attached, silently reintroducing #1226's duplicate-alert-noise problem on the telemetry channel alone; the first fix attempt, written to the review's literal prescription, did nothing and was caught by its own regression test — the real mechanism turned out to be `record.levelno` staying fixed at the moment `.exception()` is called, independent of anything a processor writes to the event dict, not `record.exc_info` as first assumed; fixed by downgrading the raw record in `_RedactingOTelLogHandler.emit()`, proven with tests against the real exported `LogRecord` via `InMemoryLogRecordExporter`, mutation-verified), [#1313](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1313) closed [#1270](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1270) (swept the remaining ~31 files of hand-rolled `SecretStore` test doubles onto the shared `FakeSecretStore`, generalizing its constructor with `raise_on_get`/`raise_on_set` to match a richer shape one file had already proven; full backend suite green in isolation — an interim run against the shared local test Postgres had shown 70 failures from a `create_all`/`drop_all` collision with another concurrent agent session hitting the same DB, root-caused and ruled out, not a defect in the diff); **#1314** filed alongside #1312, a lower-confidence `LOG_LEVEL=ERROR`-filtering edge case below the review's posting threshold, documented with a docstring caveat rather than silently dropped. **Same-session regression, found+fixed+filed together, net zero on the count:** #1311 and #1313 both touched `backend/tests/services/test_anomaly.py` and merged independently without either rebasing onto the other — #1311's branch predated #1313's `SecretStore`-double consolidation, so its own new test still constructed the now-deleted `_FakeStore()`, an undefined-name regression (Ruff F821) invisible to either PR's own CI and only surfaced when a completely unrelated docs-only PR's CI ran against the new `main`. Filed as [#1316](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1316), fixed same-session via [#1317](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1317) (swap to `FakeSecretStore()` — the store is never read in that test, connection-open is monkeypatched). (Previous — **45** open repo-wide / **28** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PRs [#1283](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1283)/[#1287](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1287)/[#1288](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1288) merged (each filed and closed its own issue — #1282/#1286/#1285 — in the same session, so the count is unmoved) and earlier after PR [#1276](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1276) merged, closing [#1273](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1273) (`decimal.Decimal` values in a failed range/threshold check on a Snowflake/UC NUMERIC column crashed the whole result's JSONB insert — `sanitize_json` had no `Decimal` branch — silently discarding the entire run's results; found live during a real-user pre-deploy QA pass against Snowflake `RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER`, confirmed **pre-existing** in already-deployed prod commit `7018d772`, not a regression. Fixed by mirroring the existing numpy/pandas coercion pattern in `backend/app/core/jsonsafe.py`; 3 new unit tests, each mutation-verified to fail for the right reason against the unfixed code; live-reproduced end-to-end pre- and post-fix against real Snowflake data) — offset by filing [#1274](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1274) (Iceberg connection over S3-compatible storage, e.g. MinIO: pyarrow's `S3FileSystem` gets `ACCESS_DENIED` reading table metadata using the same credentials the connection's own Test Connection and the sibling boto3-based `s3` connection type both accept; Test Connection never actually reads a table, so this is invisible until a real run. Scoped to S3-compatible Iceberg backends — DataQ's own Azure prod uses ADLS-backed Iceberg, likely unaffected) and [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation console warnings — `Modal.maskClosable`, `Select.onDropdownVisibleChange`, `Drawer.width` — cosmetic, batch-fixable). All three findings came from the same session's real-user Playwright QA pass (2 fresh OTP users, all 4 datasource types, deliberate PASS/FAIL/ERROR + edge-case scenarios) ahead of a prod deploy of the 56-commit `7018d772..1758cf8a` delta; that pass also confirmed [#1208](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1208) (RunDetail Observed-column bounding) holds and that [#1184](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1184)'s own fix is unrelated to what the user was still seeing in prod — #1184 was already deployed; #1208, its follow-up correction for `schema_drift`/`comparison` observed values, was merged but not yet deployed, which is what was actually stretching. (Previous — **30** open repo-wide / **26** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PRs [#1263](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1263) (closes [#1228](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1228)), [#1265](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1265) (closes [#1221](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1221)), [#1268](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1268) (closes [#1253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1253)), [#1269](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1269) (closes [#1230](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1230)), and [#1271](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1271) (closes [#1251](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1251)) all merged — five closes offset by filing [#1266](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1266) (the #1221 review's deferred driver-guard finding — `connect_args`'s psycopg2-specific keys have no driver-family guard, a pre-existing gap #1221 amplified rather than introduced) and [#1270](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1270) (the #1251 review's repo-wide SecretStore-fake sweep follow-up — corrected from an initial 10-file scope to ~31 files after a second review pass found the first undercounted by roughly 2x). **#1228** (merged earlier this session, its docs recount deferred to this batch — the two remaining lineage abort-instead-of-descend sites in the Snowflake pull, `_from_access_history`'s bare `raise` and a floor-failure-after-successful-traversal path, now skip just the affected tier and return the traversal's own edges as a degraded non-prunable result instead of discarding real observed lineage). **#1221** (DB pool keepalives): a warm pooled connection surviving a silent network partition could hang a read forever — `pool_pre_ping`'s own `SELECT 1` has no OS-level floor under it. Fixed with TCP keepalives (`keepalives_idle`/`interval`/`count`) on the shared engine's `connect_args`, one layer under #1102's `connect_timeout`. Review found the migrate-job engine (`alembic/env.py`, its own independent engine, exposed to the same gap and test-enforced-parity-tracked per its own docstring) hadn't been mirrored — fixed same-PR with a matching AST regression test; the driver-guard gap was deferred to #1266 above rather than fixed inline, to keep the PR focused. **#1253** (`observed_value` retention sweep): `purge_expired_sample_failures` scrubbed `sample_failures` but never the sibling list-shaped `observed_value` JSONB — correctly redacted on every read since #1252, but persisting indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep. Fixed with a shared `_purge_column` helper reused across both columns. **#1230** (PII classifier evidence-window, option 2 chosen): the #1196 sample cap narrowed the classifier's evidence to 20 rows at capture time for pandas-backed datasources, which can flip a genuinely-PII column to "not PII" on a noisy 20-row window. Fixed by persisting a compact per-column `value_signal_summary` (5 small ints) over the FULL pre-cap population alongside the capped rows, which the classifier prefers when present and validates before trusting (rejects a summary with an inflated/inconsistent sub-count). A `/code-review` round live-verified a real crash — `_valid_summary`'s except clause didn't catch `OverflowError`, so a persisted JSONB summary with a huge float (`"n": 1e400` → `inf`) 500'd the entire read path instead of degrading to "no summary" — and found the summary wasn't threaded into the sibling `partial_unexpected_list`'s redaction (only `unexpected_index_list`'s), leaving a column masked on one list still shown on the other for the same run; both fixed and mutation-checked same-PR. **#1251** (consolidate hand-rolled `SecretStore` test doubles): five files each hand-rolled a near-identical class implementing the `SecretStore` Protocol, folded into one shared `backend/tests/support/fake_secret_store.py::FakeSecretStore`. The migration surfaced a real bug along the way — FastAPI's dependency-override resolution introspects the override CALLABLE's own signature, so a bare class (not a lambda) with constructor params, even all-defaulted ones, gets those params bound as request-level params and corrupts body validation for the endpoint under test; a bare `_WriteFailStore()` override was making `POST /connections` 422 instead of ever reaching the route. Review found the fix was patched inline at only the two call sites that hit it rather than encoded at the seam — promoted into a shared `override_secret_store(app, store)` helper (documented in the module docstring) in a same-PR follow-up commit, and `test_admin.py`'s pre-existing `_with_store` now delegates to it instead of duplicating the same lambda wrap. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1260](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1260) merged, closing [#1226](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1226) — net unchanged, offset by filing [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261). **#1226**: when every alert channel failed, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` logged a full traceback per failing channel and then the caller (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) logged the SAME last-channel traceback a second time via its own bare `except Exception:`. Fixed with a plain marker attribute (`mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` in `alerting/base.py`, the same stash-on-the-object technique already used by `celery_app.py`'s `_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR`) the composite sets on the re-raised error, so both callers downgrade to a warning for an error the composite already reported, while anything the composite never saw still gets a full traceback. Two full `/code-review` rounds (8 agents total) found zero correctness defects — three concrete "could this fail" scenarios (setattr on `__slots__`-based exceptions, marker loss across the `asyncio.to_thread` hop, exception-identity loss via re-wrapping) were each traced and ruled out with evidence, not assumed away — but did surface real polish gaps, all fixed same-PR: the downgraded warning in `main.py` carried zero identifying fields (now carries `error_type`); a comment overstated what `run_poll_staleness_check` does with the exception (it never catches it — corrected); a test file had invented a THIRD near-identical "channel that raises" double instead of reusing the one two files over (deduped); and a `# pragma: no cover` on the except block had gone stale now that both branches are directly tested (removed, verified via a real coverage run that both lines are hit). One idea deliberately deferred rather than acted on: centralizing the downgrade in the structlog processor chain (the CLAUDE.md §10 "redact at the logger, not the call site" precedent) — reasonable for 3+ callers, premature for the 2 that exist today — filed as #1261. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1258](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1258) merged, closing [#1242](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1242) (Snowflake's privilege-filtered `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` made a zero-table sync indistinguishable from a never-synced or healthy one — fixed with two additive columns, `inventory_sync_last_table_count` + `inventory_sync_zero_since`, giving "0 tables" its own honest, non-alarming state distinct from the N>0→0 privilege-loss transition). `/code-review` found no correctness defects (verified independently by two agents across the full previous-count × table-count × failure-interleaving truth table) — only two doc-accuracy nits (wrong PR number, overstated test count), fixed in a same-PR follow-up commit. (Previous — **45** open repo-wide / **28** in the `v1.1 Backlog` milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after closing [#1030](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1030) and [#1032](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1032) (both had actually been fixed and live-verified as far back as 2026-07-27 — the harness's dbt/ADF Snowflake auth moved from password to `DATAQ_LOADER_PAT` and the two missing grants were applied and confirmed effective the same day; neither issue had ever been re-checked against `docs/ops-log.md`'s own record, so they sat open for two weeks describing already-fixed state) and filing [#1257](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1257) (the one legitimate follow-up recorded in ops-log at the time — `DATAQ_LOADER`'s account-wide `MANAGE GRANTS` should be narrowed to the two-schema need — that had never been promoted to its own tracked issue). (Previous — **29** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone (46 open repo-wide as of 2026-08-09, re-counted with `gh issue list` AFTER PR [#1252](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1252) (closed [#1229](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1229)) and PR [#1255](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1255) (closed [#1254](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1254)) both merged — net unchanged (46), because closing #1229 (-1) was offset by filing [#1253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1253) (+1, retention-sweep gap below) and #1254 was filed-then-closed same session (net 0). **#1229** (`results.observed_value` unbounded/unredacted for set-oriented GX expectations, e.g. `expect_column_distinct_values_to_be_in_set` — every distinct value a high-cardinality column ever saw persisted with no cap and no column-redaction, unlike `sample_failures` which #1196 already covered) was fixed by #1252: a capture-time cap (`gx_runner._bounded_observed_value`, reusing `SAMPLE_ROW_CAP`) plus read-time classification/redaction (`run_service.redact_observed_value` gained a `tested_column` param, threaded through the 3 read paths — `GET /runs/{id}`, the alert builder, `/mcp`'s `get_suite_results`) that classifies over the FULL persisted list before capping what's emitted, matching the established `redact_sample_failures` pattern; kept consistent with #1203's already-merged handling of the adjacent `{"error": ...}` branch in the same function. `/code-review`'s 5-agent pass found nothing above the 80-confidence bar — two sub-80 items (a doc overclaim, fixed in-PR; the retention-sweep scope question, filed as #1253 rather than scope-crept in) were still acted on per CLAUDE.md §11. Mutation-checked: reverted just the two source files, confirmed all new tests fail for the right reason, restored the fix. **#1253** (filed, open, `v1.1 Backlog`): `purge_expired_sample_failures` only scrubs `sample_failures`, never `observed_value` — a list-shaped `observed_value` is now correctly redacted on every READ (#1252) but the raw JSONB persists indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep, unlike its sibling column. Deliberately NOT folded into #1252 — the original #1229 issue's own suggested fix shape asked only for the cap + redaction halves. **#1254** (filed AND closed same session, via #1255): CI on #1252 hit a *pre-existing, unrelated* flaky Vitest test — `SuiteForm.test.tsx`'s "reopens an existing batch target in batch mode" test renders a form whose target is `active` from first mount, so the real 400ms preview debounce (#1193) fires; the test never mocked `previewBatchTarget`'s resolution (unlike siblings that do), so when CI load let the timer win the race against RTL's unmount cleanup, the un-implemented `vi.fn()` returned `undefined` and `.then()` on `undefined` threw — `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then') at Timeout._onTimeout SuiteForm.tsx:387:9`. Confirmed unrelated to #1252 (its diff is backend-only) and confirmed NOT a one-off — a first CI retry reproduced the identical failure, ruling out "just a flake, retry past it." Root-caused precisely (two more sibling tests in the same describe block had the identical latent exposure, not just the one that happened to fail) and reproduced deterministically pre-fix via a scratch forced-delay experiment that threw the exact CI error, then fixed all three vulnerable tests by mocking `previewBatchTarget`'s resolution, matching the idiom used elsewhere in the file. Merged as #1255, then merged into #1252's branch so its CI could go green. Both PRs milestoned/labelled after the fact (an oversight caught mid-session — new issues/PRs must get labels+milestone per the repo's GitHub-hygiene convention, not just inherit one from a linked issue). (Previous — **29** in the v1.1 Backlog milestone, 46 open repo-wide, re-counted with `gh issue list` AFTER PR [#1235](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1235) merged rather than predicted from it — net +1, because it closed [#1199](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1199) and filed two: [#1247](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1247) (the near-miss read side re-derives the write side's candidate tuples and hash-probes `workspace_health`, so the two derivations are coupled by a prose comment plus one round-trip test rather than by shared code) and [#1248](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1248) (four of #1193's batch-preview tests fail under `SECRET_STORE=openbao`, the local-stack default since #1159 — reproduced on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so pre-existing, and it costs every contributor a false-alarm triage round). #1199 gave the #1186/#1194 env near-miss signal a read path: it had been write-only, a `workspace_health` row visible only via `psql`. Two `/code-review` rounds caught six defects, and the first was the one that mattered: **`GET /orchestration/near-misses` shipped auth-only**, by analogy to its `/orchestration/pipelines` neighbour. The analogy was wrong — `pipeline_runs` is workspace-wide orchestrator telemetry with no suite-ownership concept, whereas a near-miss is derived *wholly* from `trigger_binding` rows, which are suite-owned config the sibling `GET /trigger-bindings` already scopes. As written, any signed-in user could enumerate the `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, binding_env)` of bindings on suites they cannot see. It now applies the same `accessible_suite_ids` filter, with `include_all` for a workspace admin. Three more were honesty-of-display: the panel picked the FIRST matching near-miss with `.find()`, so a second live mismatch on the same binding — two orchestrator connections reporting one DAG id against two different wrong envs, i.e. literally the #1186 ambiguity the feature exists to catch — was hidden behind the first; a failed near-miss fetch rendered identically to "no mismatch", so an outage read as healthy on the very screen built to surface it (the ADR-0039 lesson, in a new place); and the tooltip asserted the present tense ("runs keep landing in X … this binding has not fired and won't") for anything inside the 48h window while `updated_at` was fetched, typed, threaded through and never rendered — so a binding fixed an hour ago kept being told it was still broken.
