the frontend two-step sign-in + HttpOnly cookie + server-side revocation, plus a new fully-local `frontend/e2e-otp/` lane ([#1148](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1148)); the SMTP pre-flight test endpoint ([#1143](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1143)); a latency floor on `otp/verify` closing the narrower enumeration channel [#1141](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1141) left open after the request-side floor ([#1154](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1154)); SMTP TLS mode + private-CA bundle for the mailer, closing [#1146](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1146) ([#1155](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1155)); and a per-admin throttle on the SMTP pre-flight endpoint, closing [#1147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1147) ([#1156](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1156)). **Then, unplanned again — both local/eval compose stacks flipped to OTP-by-default** ([#1150](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1150), [#1159](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1159)): a bundled **Mailpit** mail catcher (MIT, pinned `v1.30.6`) at `localhost:8025` removes the SMTP relay that made `otp` unusable as a default, so both stacks now boot into email codes instead of dev-bypass, gated by one switch — `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` set = OTP on, explicitly empty = the dev-bypass downgrade, unset = the stack refuses to start rather than picking for you. `scripts/setup.sh` asks for the address; see [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) for the full flow. A same-day test-flake fix ([#1161](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1161)) closed out the track. Full slice-by-slice detail — including the five review-caught defects (an `smtplib.__exit__` that replaces in-flight errors, a compose `environment:`-beats-`env_file:` precedence trap, an ACCESS-EXCLUSIVE-lock doc error, and two more) — is in [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md) under "Backlog track — ADR 0032 email OTP sign-in". **v1.1 Week 5 — `anomaly` monitor kind + metric trends — CLOSED 2026-08-01, 8/8, a week early:** one orchestrated batch, 10 PRs [#1113](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1113)–[#1122](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1122) — threshold-ordering validation (#568, #1113, closing a `schema_drift` dry-run bypass the review found); the results runs-fetch dedupe + shared date-window presets (#349, #1114, fixing a background-poll-wipes-the-tab bug along the way); an explicit failing-sample redaction state (#424, #1115 — full/partial/none/null, computed read-time via a `_RedactionTracker` so old rows get the correct label for free); Test Connection for unsaved connection drafts (#351, #1116 — `POST /connections/test`, structurally cannot persist; review also surfaced the `*_secret_name` SSRF/exfiltration class on the same auth gate, filed [#1118](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1118), mitigation deferred to RBAC #740–#744); the **`anomaly` monitor kind itself** (#593, #1117 backend + #1119 authoring UI) — rolling z-score baseline with optional seasonality over `metric_value` history, reusing the existing `monitor_baselines` table (no migration), `skip` on cold start, dimension deliberately underivable → NULL (ADR 0038); the per-check metric trend view (#594, #1121) with threshold bands plus a second anomaly-baseline panel, seasonality-aware; check-version restore (#283, #1120), minting a new version rather than delegating to the PATCH-semantics `update_check`; and a zero-dependency PDF report export of a run (#345, #1122). **Live-verified 2026-08-01 against both live warehouses** (the #953 rule — for anything crossing a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence): Snowflake `RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER` row_count=34680.0 + freshness `ORDER_TS`=132.28h; Unity Catalog `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment` row_count=180.0 + freshness `scored_at`=132.48h — z-scores computed cleanly over both. Every PR carried the mandated `/code-review` agent flow; 15+ real defects were caught pre-merge, including two concurrency bugs (a baseline-UPDATE lost-update race, a stale "Connected" badge) and two honesty-of-display bugs (an under-reported redaction state, a threshold-band caption overclaiming below 2 eligible points); the one deferred finding is #1118 above. **Unplanned, shipped + live-verified 2026-07-28/29 — three batches in one orchestrated session (#1096–#1112, 10 PRs):** Batch 2 reliability (beat **crontabs** #1099 — a 24h interval never fires under embedded beat; **staleness signals** #1100 — stale-lineage surface + de-configured-pull purge + the API-side workspace dead-poll alert on the new `workspace_health` table) and Batches 3+4 assets/lineage (**ADR [0040](docs/adr/0040-warehouse-inventory-sync-table-enumeration-seam.md)** — the table-enumeration seam + opt-in per-connection **inventory sync** #1103, so a table with no suite/run/edge is visible-unmonitored instead of invisible (the prod `reference`-schema report); asset **paging + honest truncation** #1105; S3-compatible **endpoint identity** #1106; **GET_LINEAGE per-seed traversal + Snowpark scratch stitching** #1110 — prod's Snowflake lineage lifted from view-level to full tier, live-verified). The recurring lesson bit twice more (#1112): mocked tests stayed green through **two stacked driver-boundary crashes** in one SQL literal (pyformat `%`, then Snowflake's own string parser eating `ESCAPE '\'`) — for warehouse SQL, run the exact statement live before push. **Unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — IaC CLI moved Terraform → OpenTofu (ADR 0024 amendment):** Terraform has been BUSL-1.1 since v1.6 and was the one source-available binary still touching a project ADR 0031 puts on record as MIT-distributed. **Nothing was in violation** — rule 40 governs the dependency tree (what DataQ *ships*) and the CLI never enters an image — so this is coherence, not compliance; the timing argument is #505, since converting one Azure stack is contained and converting three is not. **The acceptance bar was equivalence, not a clean plan**, because the stack already carries pre-existing drift (#1086 — prod's ADR-0034 lineage env vars are absent from `containerapps.tf`, so an apply would DELETE them; the rendered plan hides this behind a positional `env` shuffle and only `show -json` reveals it): both CLIs were run against live Azure, plans exported with `-out`, rendered via `show -json`, and the normalized `resource_changes` diffed — **byte-for-byte identical** (40 changes, `no-op=38 update=2`), provider versions preserved exactly, only the registry host + hashes moved. The *rendered* text plans DO differ (branding, refresh ordering, column alignment, hidden-attribute counts), which is why eyeballing them would not have settled it. State, providers, and the `deploy/terraform/<cloud>/` path are unchanged — `terraform {}` is OpenTofu's own block name. Harness stack converted in the same pass, **plan-only** (a blanket harness apply arms ADF triggers). The swap is **convention, not enforcement** — nothing is OpenTofu-exclusive yet, which is what keeps it reversible; the `encryption {}` follow-up is the one-way door and is deliberately separate. **Unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — S3-compatible endpoints (#1063/#1065):** optional `endpoint_url` + `addressing_style` on the `s3` datasource **and** the `dbt` provider, via one shared `core/s3_endpoint.py`; unlocks MinIO / Ceph / R2 / Wasabi / Backblaze. `auto` → **path** addressing when an endpoint is set is load-bearing (MinIO serves the bucket in the path only, so boto3's virtual-host default fails every read), and `endpoint_url` rejects an embedded credential per the #754/#826 rule. **Live-proven against MinIO** — suite 4/4 over 643 real rows, arrival-time freshness read off `LastModified` — because a non-AWS server is a different implementation and those values cross a driver boundary. It arose from an **Azure-free harness readiness exercise** (local Airflow + MinIO landing zone, all flows green incl. a live Snowflake load; Azure untouched, all five harness apps stayed `Stopped`), whose Snowflake half also produced a standing rule: **nothing in the harness may require a commercial licence** — stricter than rule 40, which governs only what DataQ *ships* — after LocalStack for Snowflake was evaluated and rejected (no community tier; image exits 55). fakesnow (Apache-2.0) is the stand-in, and probing it with DataQ's real code paths found **#1067**: a Snowflake connection with no Role tests green (the test is GX-free) and fails every suite run, since GX requires a `role` query param. See [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). Follow-ups #1064/#1066. **The four open ADR-0039 follow-ups were then closed the same day (#1069/#1070/#1071):** GHCR `:latest` now republishes on merge (the eval compose is fetched from `main` while the image moved only on dispatch — verified live); the pooled secret-store clients are released on cache reset, with the AKV **credential** closed alongside the client since they hold separate transport sessions; an **orphan-secret sweep** that reports by default and purges only when configured, because what it deletes is a live warehouse credential; and **AppRole auth** (ADR 0039 phase 2) with proactive renewal and one re-login on 403, so a revoked token self-heals instead of 403ing until restart. Two lessons worth carrying: the sweep's ownership registry was wrong **twice** (Slack and Teams are separate refs on one row; `*_secret_name` keys live in JSONB) and its introspection guard was a **tautology** — it iterated the models already registered, so a new model was invisible to it; and #435 was assessed and left open with a corrected AC, since Azure CMK is **creation-time-only** and our IaC stack does not own the Postgres server. **Also unplanned, shipped 2026-07-27 — the secret-store seam (ADR [0039](docs/adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md), #1056/#1061):** a fourth `SecretStore` speaking the **KV v2 HTTP API, not a vendor SDK**, so one mode serves OpenBao / Vault Community / Enterprise / HCP — this closes the last seam where Azure was the only production implementation, which #505 (AWS/GCP IaC) would have walked straight into. **OpenBao** (MPL-2.0) is shipped and pinned; Vault Community is BUSL-1.1 and therefore rule-40-forbidden as a *distributed* component, supported only as a target. `SECRET_STORE=openbao` **replaces `redis`** — the plaintext store was the configured default of the published eval stack, i.e. evaluators were putting real warehouse credentials into an unencrypted key-value store. **Redis stays** (Celery broker + ADR 0035 rate limits). Two defects the review caught are worth carrying forward: **an outage must never be reportable as a state** — every caller branches on the exception TYPE and none reads the message, so folding "vault sealed" into `SecretNotFoundError` made an admin page render "not set" and silently skipped alert delivery (`AzureKeyVaultStore` had shipped that since Week 2); and a **`Settings` validator now fails a bad secret-store config at boot**, because the store built lazily and would otherwise die mid-run in a worker. Prod's 13 `conn-*` Key Vault keys were also renamed to one readable convention (`conn-<type>-<qualifier>-<env>-<shortid>`) — copy → read-back verify → repoint → re-test → purge, piloted on one connection first, 11/11 re-verified, and both Airflow connections verified on Key Vault **and** OpenBao. See [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). **DEPLOYED + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-19** (then `dff6d958`; prod redeployed to `c401572d` 2026-07-26; prod redeployed again to `bb40f0b7` 2026-08-03 — all three Container Apps (api/worker/frontend) rolled via the Deploy workflow ([run 30789647178](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/30789647178)), migrate job Succeeded, post-deploy smoke green (healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401 gates hold, authenticated `/me` verified, beat+watchdog clean on the new revision); **prod redeployed to `7018d772` 2026-08-08** — the 2026-08-08 session's eleven merges (#1185/#1188–#1192/#1194/#1198/#1201/#1204 — six-issue fix batch incl. the UC custom-SQL fix, identifier-column display, batch-target UI) rolled via [run 31261342996](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31261342996), migrate no-op (no schema change), full smoke green + a UC suite run 7/7 on the new revisions — see below): the W4 work is on prod and exercised against real datasources. **Prod redeployed to `f637a18e` 2026-08-09** — a full real-user pre-deploy QA pass (2 fresh OTP users, all 4 datasource types, deliberate PASS/FAIL/ERROR + edge-case scenarios via Playwright, no DB shortcuts) found and fixed a live, pre-existing production defect: **#1273** — `decimal.Decimal` values in a legitimately-failed Snowflake/UC NUMERIC-column check crashed the entire result's JSONB insert (`sanitize_json` had no `Decimal` branch), silently discarding the run's results; a passing check on the same column never surfaces the bug, which is why it went unnoticed since `jsonsafe.py` shipped. Fixed in [#1276](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1276) mirroring the file's existing numpy/pandas coercion pattern; mutation-verified regression tests + a live pre/post-fix repro against real Snowflake data. Two more findings filed, both non-blocking: [#1274](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1274) (Iceberg over S3-compatible storage — pyarrow's own S3 client rejects credentials boto3 accepts; scoped to non-ADLS Iceberg backends, likely not this deployment) and [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation warnings, cosmetic). Also attempted to resolve the user-reported "columns still stretched" report — **that diagnosis was wrong and is corrected below** ([#1282](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1282)): the claim recorded here was that [#1184](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1184)'s own fix was already live and only [#1208](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1208) (the RunDetail "Observed" column) was undeployed. Both halves were false. The user re-reported the stretched columns against this very deploy, and pulling the live prod chunks settled it: **both fixes were in the shipped bundle and neither had ever worked, in any environment.** Every DataQ table renders `scroll={{ x: 'max-content' }}`, which rc-table turns into `width: max-content` on the `<table>`; an intrinsic-sizing keyword sizes the table from its content, neutering `table-layout: fixed` and demoting the `<colgroup>` width to a non-binding hint — so a column's `width` + `ellipsis` are **inert**, and a long ADF error rendered ~1917px wide against a declared 260px. The covering test asserted `toHaveClass('ant-table-cell-ellipsis')` — true, and meaningless, because jsdom performs no layout. Fixed by bounding the **inner element** (`boundedTextStyle`) rather than the column, with the regression assertion moved to Playwright where widths can actually be measured. **Standing practice this produced: "merged" is not "deployed", and "deployed" is not "works" — verify a fix against the running artifact AND against observed behavior before reporting it as done.** Rolled via [run 31342076551](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31342076551), migrate job Succeeded, post-deploy smoke green (healthz/SPA/deep-link 200, `/api`+`/mcp` 401 gates hold, `/docs` serves the SPA shell not Swagger, authenticated `/me` verified, beat+watchdog clean, Key Vault secret store initialized on the new revision) — **plus a live suite run** ("Snowflake — Orders (all paths)", 7 checks, 6 pass/1 fail/1 skip, `succeeded`) confirming the #1273 fix holds against real prod data. **Prod redeployed twice more the same day — to `77068358`, then to `eba60b4d` (current)** ([run 31347217502](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31347217502), [run 31350288817](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31350288817)); both migrate jobs no-op (zero migration files in either delta), both smokes green, and the fixes **verified in the running artifact and in the browser**, not merely merged: the deployed chunk `ellipsisColumn-*.js` carries `boundedTextStyle`, and the Failure-reason cell that had rendered ~1917px now measures 260px with 3423px of content clipped, Observed 220px, the pipeline table 1379px instead of 2969px. The second roll carried two post-deploy-smoke findings from the first: **#1286** (the fix’s own regression — a 150px bound wrapped the copy button and grew every pipeline-runs row 56px→77px; measured the threshold on live prod and shipped 120) and **#1285** (pre-existing — orchestration poll failures were classified through the datasource message set, so both Airflow connections said “missing warehouse or role … check the suite’s run target” while the harness Airflow app was simply Stopped; an orchestration connection has none of those four things). Both confirmed live afterwards: 20/20 Provider-run cells clipped at 120px with a uniform 56px row height, and the 02:51Z poll wrote the new orchestration-shaped reason. A live suite run on each revision (8 checks) confirmed the worker path against real Snowflake. **Verification lesson from this session, now standing practice: “merged” is not “deployed”, and “deployed” is not “works” — a stale-looking grep in the wrong chunk nearly produced a second wrong answer, and the first poll after the roll still showed the old message because the draining revision served it.** Orchestration (Airflow trigger → poll → dispatch) was also verified end-to-end in the local harness this session, after fixing a stale `DATAQ_LOADER`-scoped Snowflake credential in the harness's own (untracked, separate-repo) local stack — see [docs/ops-log.md](docs/ops-log.md). **ADLS** — volume read 643 rows off the resolved batch and arrival-time freshness reported 531.8h from the blob's last-modified: the harness genuinely stopped producing, which is precisely the incident #520 exists to catch and which an in-file MAX cannot see. **Snowflake** — `order_ts` (lower-case, emitted unquoted so the warehouse folds it) and `ORDER_TS` (upper-case, now quoted) returned **identical** timestamps, proving #937 both fixes mixed case and preserves the fold; volume over 32,840 real rows. **Unity Catalog** — freshness works **for the first time ever** (239.06h, lower/UPPER identical, confirming the backtick dialect). The dimension backfill (#952) classified **all 30 real prod checks, zero unclassified**, and real asset scorecards show genuine signal. **Live testing found a bug three green suites could not: UC freshness had NEVER worked** (#953) — the Databricks connector returns a TIMESTAMP's MAX as a **str** and the age math accepted only datetime/date, so a datasource the feature matrix marks ✅ produced no reading since #426. No unit test could see it: the type comes from the **driver**, and every fixture hands in a real datetime — the same fixture-encodes-our-model shape as #823 and the #520 Parquet bug. **Lesson: for anything whose type or value crosses a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence.** Also filed [#954](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/954): two prod Snowflake PATs are dead, and a **datasource** connection with a dead credential has no visible state until a run fails — I had to read worker logs to find out why, since #839's health signal covers only *orchestration* connections. That is the #828 blindness in a new place. **W4 CLOSED 2026-07-19, 8/8** — `schema_drift` (#592) shipped 2026-07-17, and this session cleared the remaining four in two groups. **Flat-file (#476, #520):** every backend CSV read hardcoded the pandas default comma, so a `;`/tab/pipe file parsed as ONE column named after the whole header — silently; all four reads now share one sniffing seam ([#934](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/934)). #476's casing half was **relocated by checking the code instead of the ticket** — the profiler's Core builders already quoted correctly; the only unquoted path was `monitors.py`'s f-string, fixed by returning a Core `Select` so the CONNECTION's dialect quotes it ([#937](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/937)); hand-rolled `"` quoting would have been actively wrong on UC, which uses backticks. Flat files gained freshness/volume monitors incl. **arrival-time freshness** — the case a warehouse can't express, since an in-file MAX is blind to a producer that stopped sending files ([#940](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/940)). **Dimension & score (#124, #889):** ADR [0038](docs/adr/0038-dq-dimension-classification.md) — seven canonical dimensions, closed vocabulary, derived default → stored → overridable, derivation deliberately partial so **NULL means unclassified and renders as a coverage gap** ([#945](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/945)); then `services/rollup.py` as the one histogram + score + latest-run query ([#948](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/948)) and the asset scorecard on top ([#950](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/950)).

content.text:
**All four tracks done and live-verified, plus the S3 datasource you asked for mid-flight.** Six PRs merged (#1367, #1370–#1372, #1374, + docs #1375), issues #1364/#1368/#1369/#1373 all closed with live evidence, repo clean.

## 1. Sign-out fixed (#1364 → [#1367](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1367))
New runtime flag `DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE=cognito` (a config flag, not issuer sniffing — ADR 0028): the client now builds Cognito's `client_id`+`logout_uri` logout URL from the discovered end-session endpoint. Verified in a real browser on the AWS deployment: Sign out returns to the app (no more "Client does not exist" page), and the next Sign in **prompts for credentials** — the hosted-UI session is genuinely terminated. Azure's standard flow is untouched. The review caught an ordering bug in my own fix (local session must clear before the network-dependent discovery fetch) — fixed with a regression test.

## 2. SES alerts ([#1370](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1370)/[#1372](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1372)/[#1374](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1374))
Sender `theurgicduke771@gmail.com`, recipient `royarijit04@outlook.com` (both verified — thanks for the clicks), SMTP password derived in Terraform and stored in Secrets Manager under the name the app already reads. A deliberately-failing check on the live Snowflake suite produced **`email_alert_sent`** — the alert email is in your outlook inbox. Two live-only lessons: SES sandbox authorizes sends against the **recipient's** identity ARN too (a real 554 disproved the review's "sender-only scoping is correct" — filed and fixed same-session as #1373), and alert dedup consumes its key even on a *failed* send, so each retest needed a fresh failing check.

## 3. APM/tracing ([#1371](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1371))
Correction first: the app half already existed — `core/otel.py` (#589) is vendor-neutral OTLP; my parity table's "Azure-exporter-only" claim was stale. So this was infra only: ADOT collector sidecars (pinned v0.49.0, minimal two-pipeline config, loopback bind) in the api+worker task defs. Verified live: **X-Ray shows api request traces and worker Celery traces** (`run/run_suite`, the beat tasks), and CloudWatch `/dataq-app/otel` carries the OTel log records with `trace_id`s matching their X-Ray traces — the span↔log join works on AWS like it does on App Insights.

## 4. MCP tested
Full protocol E2E against live `/mcp/` over a PAT (minted, used, and deleted entirely inside the browser so it never touched the transcript): initialize, all **8 tools listed**, and real calls — `list_suites`, `get_health_score`, `trigger_suite_run` (a genuine Snowflake run that `succeeded` on the worker), `get_run_status`, `get_suite_results`.

## 5. S3 datasource (your mid-session ask)
Created bucket `dataq-landing-251783195294` (orders CSV, 800 rows, public access blocked), a read-only IAM user, and the **"Retail S3 Landing"** connection in the app — the secret access key traveled via a temp Secrets Manager entry straight onto the connection's secret ref, never through the transcript. Test Connection green; suite **"AWS S3 — Orders Header CSV" ran 3/3** including arrival-time freshness (file age ~35s, exactly right).

## Worth knowing
- Task-def changes on this stack need `tofu apply -replace` + `update-service` (the `ignore_changes` CI-rollout tradeoff) — now documented in the AWS README.
- SES is still in **sandbox** (verified addresses only); production access is an AWS support form when you want arbitrary recipients.
- The E2E user's password was rotated back to an unknown random after the browser tests; Forgot-password reclaims it.
- Deploys along the way went through `deploy-aws.yml`, which also proved out the two-container roll logic the ADOT review demanded.

content.text: So, for AWS what are the pending tasks?

Short list — the AWS stack is functionally complete; what's left is hardening and paperwork:

**Tracked issues (open):**
1. **[#1355](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1355) — CloudFront origin secret verified at nginx.** Today any third party could point their own CloudFront distribution at the ALB's DNS name (the SG only restricts to CloudFront's shared origin-facing ranges). Needs a secret custom-origin header checked in the frontend nginx — a frontend image change plus a Terraform header on the distribution.
2. **[#1338](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1338) — AWS runbook docs.** `SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`, `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX`, and the AWS env-var set aren't yet in `deploy/README.md` / the env reference (the stack README exists; the user-facing deploy docs don't cover AWS).
3. **[#1363](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1363) — generic `rediss://` ssl_cert_reqs default.** The #1361 fix landed only in the AWS Terraform; any BYOL deployment with a TLS redis still crash-loops. Preferred fix is an app-level safe default in `celery_app.py`, plus a docs note.

**Small verifications (no code):**
4. **Confirm `RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS=3`** against one real logged X-Forwarded-For — it's reasoned-correct (CloudFront→ALB→nginx) but never observed live.
5. **SES production access** when you want alerts to arbitrary recipients — the account is in sandbox (verified addresses only); it's an AWS support form, not Terraform.

**Only if AWS is to become primary prod** (the full-switch list from the parity review, unchanged):
6. **Custom domain** — Route 53 + ACM on CloudFront; pick it before migrating users since OIDC redirect URIs, webhooks, and MCP configs all key off the URL.
7. **Durability hardening** — RDS backups are 1 day with no deletion protection, single-AZ, public-subnets/no-NAT, no ElastiCache snapshots. All deliberate cost choices for a parallel deployment; not prod-grade.
8. **CloudWatch alarms** — traces/logs now flow, but nothing *alerts* on service health, beat liveness, or 5xx (Azure Monitor plays that role today).
9. **Data + identity migration** — `pg_dump` → RDS, re-mint every per-connection secret into Secrets Manager (the one-credential-becomes-N trap), recreate users in Cognito, re-point ADF/Airflow/dbt webhooks.

My suggested order if you keep going: #1355 first (it's the one real security gap), then #1338 + the XFF check (cheap), #1363 when convenient. Items 6–9 only get pulled if you decide to actually switch.

def _rediss_safe_url(url: str) -> str:
    """A ``rediss://`` URL celery will accept: default ``ssl_cert_reqs=required``.

    Celery's redis backend hard-raises ``ValueError`` on any ``rediss://`` URL
    without an explicit ``ssl_cert_reqs`` query parameter, so a TLS redis
    (ElastiCache, Azure Cache, managed Vault-adjacent redis) crash-loops the
    worker at boot and kills the api's producer on first dispatch (#1361 —
    which fixed only the AWS Terraform's URL; this is the generic guard,
    #1363). ``required`` is never weaker than what the operator asked for:
    it is full certificate verification, and an explicit parameter — any
    value, including a deliberate ``CERT_NONE`` — is left untouched.
    Non-rediss URLs pass through byte-identical.
    """
    from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

    parts = urlsplit(url)
    if parts.scheme != "rediss" or "ssl_cert_reqs" in parse_qs(parts.query):
        return url
    separator = "&" if parts.query else "?"
    return f"{url}{separator}ssl_cert_reqs=required"


def create_celery_app() -> Celery:
    settings = get_settings()
    app = Celery(
        "dataq",
        broker=_rediss_safe_url(settings.redis_url),
        backend=_rediss_safe_url(settings.redis_url),
    )

# Troubleshooting

Common problems and where to look. For deeper telemetry (logs, traces, where they land) see
[Observability](observability.md); for deploy-time issues see the
[Deployment](deployment.md) checklists.

## Connections

**"Test" fails on a connection.**

- Re-check the credential and that the account/host/warehouse names are exact.
- The credential must be reachable **from where DataQ runs** (network / firewall), not just
  from your laptop.
- Use **Rotate credential** (re-auth) if the secret expired.
- A missing/expired warehouse or role usually shows as a config/permission error.

**A connection card shows "credential expires in Nd" / "credential expired".**

Some credentials state their own expiry — an Azure SAS carries it in the token — so DataQ
reads it and warns while there is still time to act. Rotate the credential (**Rotate
credential** / re-auth) and the badge clears on the same request.

The badge is **absent** for most credential types, and absence is not a clean bill of
health: an S3 access key, a Snowflake key-pair, and a Databricks PAT carry no readable
lifetime, so DataQ says nothing rather than guessing a date. Track those expiries wherever
you issue them. DataQ PATs get the same warning on the **Profile → Access tokens** panel,
where they are stored with a known expiry.

The date is re-read daily, so a credential rotated outside DataQ (in the Azure portal, say)
updates within a day rather than needing a re-save here.

## Runs

**A run shows `failed` (not just failing checks).**

`failed` means the run couldn't *execute* (distinct from a check failing). The run detail now
shows a **redaction-safe reason** — one of:

- *config* — the connection or run target looks misconfigured (missing warehouse/role, or a
  table/path that doesn't exist). Fix the connection or the suite's target.
- *connectivity* — the datasource couldn't be reached (network/DNS/TLS/timeout).
- *permission* — credentials rejected or a grant is missing. Rotate the credential / add the
  grant.

**A check is `error` or `skip`, not pass/fail.** These are *operational* statuses, kept
distinct from data failures: `error` = the check couldn't be evaluated (e.g. a missing
column); `skip` = a precondition wasn't met (e.g. a batch file hasn't landed yet).

**`checks_total` reads 0 / `—`.** A run that failed before any check executed evaluated
nothing, so its data-quality outcome is empty — that's truthful, distinct from the suite's
defined check count shown on the progress view.

**Dry-run returns a 502.** The datasource couldn't be reached or the query couldn't run; the
error detail carries a safe *reason* (config / connectivity / permission). The raw adapter
error is never echoed (it can carry credential fragments) — check the server logs for detail.

## Schedules

**A scheduled run didn't fire.** Confirm the schedule is **enabled**, the cron + timezone are
right, and remember DataQ does **no backfill** — a missed window isn't retried, the next one
runs. See [Scheduling](scheduling.md).

## Triggers / orchestration

**A pipeline succeeded but no suite ran.** Check there's an **enabled trigger binding** matching
`(provider, pipeline/DAG/job, env)` exactly, and that the webhook is configured (or the
10-minute poll fallback can reach the artifacts/REST API). Failure events **alert but never
trigger** a run — by design. See [Orchestration](orchestration.md).

## Alerts

**No alert arrived for a failing run.**

- Check the suite's **Notifications** threshold — the default is warn-and-worse; `fail-only`
  suppresses warns.
- **Dedup** is intentional: you're alerted on the first breach (and on escalation), not on
  every run. A red suite that's "quiet" is usually dedup working — the **Results** page is the
  ground truth.
- Check the channel isn't **snoozed** for that check.
- Confirm the channel secret/webhook is set (Settings → Webhooks / per-suite config).

## Sign-in & API

- **401 on the API or MCP** = no/invalid token. For scripts, mint a fresh [PAT](api-keys.md);
  it expires and can be revoked.
- **SSO won't complete** — confirm the IdP app registration + redirect URIs match the deployed
  frontend URL.

2	
3	GX suite runs are dispatched from FastAPI and executed here so the request
4	thread returns immediately (run created as ``queued``, worker drives it to
5	``running`` → ``succeeded``/``failed``).
6	
7	The CLAUDE.md observability rule requires ``request_id`` correlation to flow
8	FastAPI → Celery → GX. We carry it on the task message headers: the caller
9	injects the active request_id on publish, and the worker restores it into the
10	same ``request_id_var`` ContextVar the structlog processor chain reads from, so
11	worker log lines correlate with the request that triggered them.
12	"""
13	
14	import uuid
15	from typing import Any
16	
17	from billiard.exceptions import Terminated, WorkerLostError
18	from celery import Celery
19	from celery.schedules import crontab

21	    beat_init,
22	    before_task_publish,
23	    setup_logging,
24	    task_failure,
25	    task_postrun,
26	    task_prerun,
27	    worker_process_init,
28	    worker_ready,
29	)
30	
31	from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
32	from backend.app.core.logging import configure_logging, get_logger, request_id_var
33	from backend.app.core.tracing import configure_tracing, instrument_celery
34	
35	# Message-header key carrying the originating request_id across the broker.
36	REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "request_id"
37	# Attribute on task.request where prerun stashes the ContextVar reset handle
38	# for postrun. Deliberately avoids the word "token" so it isn't mistaken for a
39	# secret by Bandit / Ruff (B105 / S105).
40	_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR = "_dataq_request_id_reset"
41	
42	
43	def create_celery_app() -> Celery:
44	    settings = get_settings()
45	    app = Celery(
46	        "dataq",
47	        broker=settings.redis_url,
48	        backend=settings.redis_url,
49	    )
50	    app.conf.update(
51	        task_serializer="json",
52	        result_serializer="json",
53	        accept_content=["json"],
54	        timezone="UTC",
55	        enable_utc=True,
56	        # Surface a 'started' state so the run-status read-back can distinguish
57	        # queued from running without waiting for completion.
58	        task_track_started=True,
59	        # Recycle a prefork child once it has grown past this resident size, so a
60	        # big materialisation cannot ratchet the baseline up run-over-run and drop
61	        # the effective ceiling for everything after it (#755 measured 956 -> 1188
62	        # -> 1666 MiB across three runs). The child is replaced BETWEEN tasks, so
63	        # this never interrupts a run in flight; it only stops memory creep.
64	        # 0 disables.
65	        worker_max_memory_per_child=settings.worker_max_memory_per_child_kb or None,
66	        # Deliberately NOT acks_late. With early ack (the default) a task the broker
67	        # has already delivered is not redelivered when the child dies — which is
68	        # exactly what stops an OOM-killing run from being handed straight back to a
69	        # fresh child and killing it too (#755's poison-pill ask; a local crash loop
70	        # of 25 restarts). Late ack would trade that for at-least-once delivery we
71	        # do not want here: a half-executed suite re-run is worse than a failed one,
72	        # and the run row is already driven to a terminal state by the
73	        # `task_failure` handler below.
74	        task_acks_late=False,

76	        # every 10 min as the success channel for runs that produced no webhook;
77	        # the task looks back further than the interval so nothing slips the gap.

80	        # is no separate beat process, and beat state does not survive a restart.
81	        #

86	        # lineage sat 10 days stale with beat's every-minute tasks running fine.
87	        # A crontab fires at a wall-clock moment, indifferent to restarts. The

1	# DataQ — deployment guide
2	
3	How DataQ v1 is deployed to Azure. Infrastructure is **in-repo OpenTofu**
4	(`deploy/terraform/azure/`, applied — [ADR 0024](../docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md));
5	the app rolls out via the **`Deploy`** workflow
6	([.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml), `workflow_dispatch`).
7	The stack is **live** — this is the runbook to provision a fresh environment and to
8	deploy a new image. Related: [ADR 0025](../docs/adr/0025-production-image-pip-slim.md)
9	(slim+pip image), [ADR 0023](../docs/adr/0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR).
10	
11	Azure is **one** deploy target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013) — the
12	manifests here are infra config, not business logic. No Azure resource names are
13	hardcoded in app code; they live only as OpenTofu vars + workflow `vars`/`secrets`.
14	
15	## Before you deploy: production prerequisites
16	
17	Read this before a production rollout. It's the "what must change, what access you
18	need, and what your cloud must provide" checklist; the [provisioning runbook](#one-time-provisioning)
19	below is the how.
20	
21	### 1. What you must change (never ship the eval/dev defaults)
22	
23	The prebuilt-image quickstart ([docs/getting-started](../docs/getting-started.md)) boots
24	into **email-OTP sign-in by default** (#1150) — a bundled Mailpit catcher stands in for
25	an SMTP relay, uses a passwordless DB, and binds to loopback. Dev-bypass (no
26	authentication at all) is an **explicit two-variable downgrade**
27	(`DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL= DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass`), not the default — and leaving
28	`DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` unset entirely refuses to start rather than silently picking a
29	mode for you. A production deployment must flip all of the following. Values live in
30	[`deploy/.env.app.prod.example`](.env.app.prod.example) (app settings) +
31	[`deploy/terraform/azure/variables.tf`](terraform/azure/variables.tf) (infra):
32	
33	| Setting | Eval default | Production |

43	| `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | keep **`true`** — the fixed-window throttle on every public surface (REST + webhooks + `/mcp`), ADR 0035. Fail-open (a Redis outage disables it, logged); set `false` only to fully disable. |

1	# Troubleshooting
2	
3	Common problems and where to look. For deeper telemetry (logs, traces, where they land) see
4	[Observability](observability.md); for deploy-time issues see the
5	[Deployment](deployment.md) checklists.
6	
7	## Connections
8	
9	**"Test" fails on a connection.**
10	
11	- Re-check the credential and that the account/host/warehouse names are exact.
12	- The credential must be reachable **from where DataQ runs** (network / firewall), not just
13	  from your laptop.
14	- Use **Rotate credential** (re-auth) if the secret expired.
15	- A missing/expired warehouse or role usually shows as a config/permission error.
16	
17	**A connection card shows "credential expires in Nd" / "credential expired".**
18	
19	Some credentials state their own expiry — an Azure SAS carries it in the token — so DataQ
20	reads it and warns while there is still time to act. Rotate the credential (**Rotate
21	credential** / re-auth) and the badge clears on the same request.
22	
23	The badge is **absent** for most credential types, and absence is not a clean bill of
24	health: an S3 access key, a Snowflake key-pair, and a Databricks PAT carry no readable
25	lifetime, so DataQ says nothing rather than guessing a date. Track those expiries wherever
26	you issue them. DataQ PATs get the same warning on the **Profile → Access tokens** panel,
27	where they are stored with a known expiry.
28	
29	The date is re-read daily, so a credential rotated outside DataQ (in the Azure portal, say)
30	updates within a day rather than needing a re-save here.
31	
32	## Runs
33	
34	**A run shows `failed` (not just failing checks).**
35	
36	`failed` means the run couldn't *execute* (distinct from a check failing). The run detail now
37	shows a **redaction-safe reason** — one of:
38	
39	- *config* — the connection or run target looks misconfigured (missing warehouse/role, or a
40	  table/path that doesn't exist). Fix the connection or the suite's target.
41	- *connectivity* — the datasource couldn't be reached (network/DNS/TLS/timeout).
42	- *permission* — credentials rejected or a grant is missing. Rotate the credential / add the
43	  grant.
44	
45	**A check is `error` or `skip`, not pass/fail.** These are *operational* statuses, kept
46	distinct from data failures: `error` = the check couldn't be evaluated (e.g. a missing
47	column); `skip` = a precondition wasn't met (e.g. a batch file hasn't landed yet).
48	
49	**`checks_total` reads 0 / `—`.** A run that failed before any check executed evaluated
50	nothing, so its data-quality outcome is empty — that's truthful, distinct from the suite's
51	defined check count shown on the progress view.
52	
53	**Dry-run returns a 502.** The datasource couldn't be reached or the query couldn't run; the
54	error detail carries a safe *reason* (config / connectivity / permission). The raw adapter
55	error is never echoed (it can carry credential fragments) — check the server logs for detail.
56	
57	## Schedules
58	
59	**A scheduled run didn't fire.** Confirm the schedule is **enabled**, the cron + timezone are
60	right, and remember DataQ does **no backfill** — a missed window isn't retried, the next one
61	runs. See [Scheduling](scheduling.md).
62	
63	## Triggers / orchestration
64	
65	**A pipeline succeeded but no suite ran.** Check there's an **enabled trigger binding** matching
66	`(provider, pipeline/DAG/job, env)` exactly, and that the webhook is configured (or the
67	10-minute poll fallback can reach the artifacts/REST API). Failure events **alert but never
68	trigger** a run — by design. See [Orchestration](orchestration.md).
69	
70	## Alerts
71	
72	**No alert arrived for a failing run.**
73	
74	- Check the suite's **Notifications** threshold — the default is warn-and-worse; `fail-only`
75	  suppresses warns.
76	- **Dedup** is intentional: you're alerted on the first breach (and on escalation), not on
77	  every run. A red suite that's "quiet" is usually dedup working — the **Results** page is the
78	  ground truth.
79	- Check the channel isn't **snoozed** for that check.
80	- Confirm the channel secret/webhook is set (Settings → Webhooks / per-suite config).
81	
82	## Sign-in & API
83	
84	- **401 on the API or MCP** = no/invalid token. For scripts, mint a fresh [PAT](api-keys.md);
85	  it expires and can be revoked.
86	- **SSO won't complete** — confirm the IdP app registration + redirect URIs match the deployed
87	  frontend URL.
88	
89	## AI assistants (MCP)
90	
91	- **401 on `/mcp/`** = auth (expected without a token) — see [MCP setup](mcp-setup.md).
92	- **307** = missing trailing slash; use `/mcp/`.
93	- **421 Misdirected Request** = the transport's DNS-rebind Host guard rejecting the proxied
94	  Host — a deployment-side config issue (the server allow-lists the proxied hosts); it is not
95	  something a client can fix.
96	
97	## Still stuck?
98	
99	Check [Observability](observability.md) for where logs/traces land, and the
100	[Runbook & FAQ](runbook-faq.md) for known limitations.

# ── Secret store ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 'openbao' = OpenBao / Vault over the KV v2 API (default; ADR 0039). Lets the API
#             and Celery worker share a credential the API writes at runtime —
#             needed by connection-driven worker runs (#86) — and, unlike the
#             plaintext Redis store it replaced, encrypts at rest behind an auth
#             boundary. api + worker both load this file, so they agree on the mode.
#             `docker compose up` starts the vault; it is DEV MODE (in-memory), so
#             a restart drops stored credentials and connections need re-entering.
# 'env'     = read connection secrets from KV_SECRET_<NAME> env vars (per-process,
#             so it CANNOT serve the compose stack — the worker won't see what the
#             api wrote). Host-only dev.
# 'azure_key_vault' = read from Azure Key Vault (staging / prod); requires
#                     AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL. Auth via DefaultAzureCredential.
#
# 'redis' was REMOVED in ADR 0039 (it kept credentials in plaintext). Setting it
# raises at startup with the migration path rather than failing obscurely.
SECRET_STORE=openbao
AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL=

# rejects guests with "Guest users not allowed"). Set true when users sign in

# ── Production app env reference (.env.app for prod) ──────────────────────────
# The prod values for backend Settings (backend/app/core/config.py). In Azure,
# set these as Container Apps env vars / secret refs on the api + worker apps —
# do NOT commit a filled-in copy. Secret VALUES live in Key Vault and are
# injected as Container Apps secrets; this file only documents the keys + shape.
# (Same discipline as .env.app.example: secret keys ship blank.)
#
# This file shows the prod-specific *values*; the **complete** key reference (every
# Settings key, grouped) is the canonical ../.env.app.example. Keep both in step.

ENVIRONMENT=prod
LOG_LEVEL=INFO

# Postgres (managed, e.g. Azure Database for PostgreSQL). Secret — inject the
# full URL (with password) as a Container Apps secret, not a literal here.
#   REDACTED
DATABASE_URL=
# Redis (managed). Secret — inject via Container Apps secret.
#   REDACTED
REDIS_URL=

# ── Observability (ADR 0010) — spans (A3) + logs (#524) via OpenTelemetry ─────
# Two exporter backends, either or both. Neither set ⇒ telemetry is off.
#
# Azure Monitor / App Insights connection string. Secret.
APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING=
# Generic OTLP/HTTP endpoint (#589) — standard OTel contract. When set, spans AND
# logs also export here (base-endpoint semantics: /v1/traces + /v1/logs appended),
# so any OTLP consumer works — Grafana/Tempo, Jaeger, Datadog, an OTel Collector.
# Setting BOTH exports to App Insights and the OTLP consumer at once (parity).
# Standard sibling vars (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS/_TIMEOUT/…) are honoured.
#   OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=

# ── Lineage emission (ADR 0034, #758) — OpenLineage RunEvents, dark by default ─
# Unset ⇒ zero emission (no client, no network). When set, every suite run emits
# START + terminal events with data-quality facets to the OL receiver (Marquez,
# DataHub's native OL endpoint, …). Advanced transports (Kafka, config file) go
# via the library-owned OPENLINEAGE__TRANSPORT__* / OPENLINEAGE_CONFIG env vars.
# OPENLINEAGE_DISABLED=true forces the dark path even with a URL set.
#   OPENLINEAGE_URL=http://marquez:5000
OPENLINEAGE_URL=
OPENLINEAGE_DISABLED=

# ── Lineage catalog pull (ADR 0034, #762) — dark by default ───────────────────
# Set LINEAGE_PROVIDER=marquez + MARQUEZ_URL to pull the catalog's graph back into
# the lineage_edges cache (daily beat). Unset ⇒ no pull, no client.
#   LINEAGE_PROVIDER=marquez
#   MARQUEZ_URL=http://marquez:5000
LINEAGE_PROVIDER=
MARQUEZ_URL=

SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS=30

# ── Azure AD SSO (real auth in prod — AUTH_DEV_BYPASS must be false) ──────────
AZURE_TENANT_ID=
AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID=
AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID=
AZURE_API_SCOPE=user_impersonation
# Allow guest (B2B / external) identities in the tenant to sign in (default false
# rejects guests with "Guest users not allowed"). Set true when users sign in
# with a guest account invited into the tenant.
AZURE_ALLOW_GUEST_USERS=false
AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false

# Comma-separated workspace-admin emails.
WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS=

# ── Secret store: Key Vault in prod ──────────────────────────────────────────
SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault
# Vault URL (non-secret identifier). The app authenticates via
# DefaultAzureCredential (the Container App's managed identity needs Key Vault
# Secrets User on this vault).
AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL=

# ── CORS: only if the SPA calls the API cross-origin ─────────────────────────
# Leave blank if the Static Web App proxies /api to the backend (same-origin —
# preferred). Set to the SPA origin(s) only if the SPA calls the API directly.
#   CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=https://app.example.com
CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=

# ── Webhook secret names (Key Vault keys, not values) ────────────────────────
REDACTED
REDACTED
REDACTED
# Workspace Teams webhook (the per-suite-webhook fallback). Unset = no Teams
# alerting unless a suite configures its own webhook. The VALUE (the URL) lives
# in Key Vault under this key; this is just the key name.
TEAMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME=
# Slack + email alert publishers (#413). Webhook URL / SMTP password live in Key
# Vault by name; unset = that channel off. (*_ALLOWED_HOSTS default sensibly —
# see ../.env.app.example.)
SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME=
EMAIL_USERNAME=
EMAIL_FROM=
EMAIL_TO=
EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME=

# ── Stuck-run reaper (#309) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Runs left non-terminal past this many minutes are failed by the beat janitor.
STUCK_RUN_THRESHOLD_MINUTES=60

# ── Connection poll-health alerting (#837) ──────────────────────────────────
# Consecutive failed orchestration polls before DataQ alerts (fires on the crossing
# and on recovery only; 0 disables the push).
ORCHESTRATION_POLL_FAILURE_ALERT_THRESHOLD=3

## AWS deployment

DataQ also runs as a **parallel deployment on AWS** (live since 2026-08-15; Azure
stays primary prod). Everything Azure-specific above has an AWS counterpart behind
the same app seams (ADR 0010/0013/0028) — no app code differs between the clouds.

- **Infra runbook:** [`deploy/terraform/aws/README.md`](terraform/aws/README.md) —
  the OpenTofu stack (ECS Fargate api/worker/frontend + migrate task, RDS,
  ElastiCache, Cognito, Secrets Manager, CloudFront→ALB ingress, SES alerts, ADOT
  sidecars → X-Ray), the apply recipe, the state-encryption rules, and the
  `-replace` procedure for rolling task-definition changes.
- **Deploy workflow:** [`deploy-aws.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml)
  (`workflow_dispatch`) — build → GHCR (`aws-<sha>` tags) → migrate RunTask gated
  on exit 0 → ECS rolls verified against the primary deployment's image → optional
  CloudFront smoke.

The AWS-shaped values for the production-prerequisites table above (all set by the
Terraform, listed here so the table's Azure values aren't mistaken for the only shape):

| Setting | AWS value |
|---|---|
| `SECRET_STORE` | `aws_secrets_manager` + `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX` (default `dataq/`) — reads/writes Secrets Manager under the prefix via the **ECS task role**; no stored credential. Datasource credentials land as `<prefix>/conn-<type>-<qualifier>-<env>-<shortid>`, same naming convention as Key Vault. |
| OIDC (backend) | `OIDC_ISSUER` = the Cognito pool issuer, `OIDC_AUDIENCE` = the SPA client id — the provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026 amendment); Cognito access tokens carry no `email`, resolved via the userinfo endpoint (#1346). |
| Frontend auth | `DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE="openid email profile"` (#1347 — Cognito rejects `offline_access`) and `DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE=cognito` (#1364 — Cognito's non-conformant `/logout`). |
| `REDIS_URL` | `rediss://…?ssl_cert_reqs=required` (ElastiCache TLS; the app also defaults the parameter when absent — #1363). |
| `RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS` | `3` (CloudFront → ALB → nginx each append to `X-Forwarded-For`). |
| Email alerts | SES via `alert_email` (sender) / `alert_email_to` (recipients) Terraform vars — sandbox identities need a one-time verification click each (#1368). |
| Observability | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318` → ADOT sidecar → X-Ray traces + CloudWatch OTel logs (#1369); container logs in CloudWatch `/dataq-app/*`. |

1	# DataQ — deployment guide
2	
3	How DataQ v1 is deployed to Azure. Infrastructure is **in-repo OpenTofu**
4	(`deploy/terraform/azure/`, applied — [ADR 0024](../docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md));
5	the app rolls out via the **`Deploy`** workflow
6	([.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml), `workflow_dispatch`).
7	The stack is **live** — this is the runbook to provision a fresh environment and to
8	deploy a new image. Related: [ADR 0025](../docs/adr/0025-production-image-pip-slim.md)
9	(slim+pip image), [ADR 0023](../docs/adr/0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR).
10	
11	Azure is **one** deploy target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013) — the
12	manifests here are infra config, not business logic. No Azure resource names are
13	hardcoded in app code; they live only as OpenTofu vars + workflow `vars`/`secrets`.
14	
15	## Before you deploy: production prerequisites
16	
17	Read this before a production rollout. It's the "what must change, what access you
18	need, and what your cloud must provide" checklist; the [provisioning runbook](#one-time-provisioning)
19	below is the how.
20	
21	### 1. What you must change (never ship the eval/dev defaults)
22	
23	The prebuilt-image quickstart ([docs/getting-started](../docs/getting-started.md)) boots
24	into **email-OTP sign-in by default** (#1150) — a bundled Mailpit catcher stands in for
25	an SMTP relay, uses a passwordless DB, and binds to loopback. Dev-bypass (no
26	authentication at all) is an **explicit two-variable downgrade**
27	(`DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL= DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass`), not the default — and leaving
28	`DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` unset entirely refuses to start rather than silently picking a
29	mode for you. A production deployment must flip all of the following. Values live in
30	[`deploy/.env.app.prod.example`](.env.app.prod.example) (app settings) +
31	[`deploy/terraform/azure/variables.tf`](terraform/azure/variables.tf) (infra):
32	
33	| Setting | Eval default | Production |
34	|---|---|---|
35	| `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` | `true` in the compose file, but **inert by default** — email OTP (`DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL`) wins over it in `auth.py` whenever OTP is configured, which it is out of the box (#1150). It only takes effect once you explicitly clear `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` (the documented downgrade). | **`false`** — this is the master auth switch; leaving it on means **no authentication at all**. |
36	| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` / `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` / `AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID` | empty | your Azure AD tenant + the two app registrations (API + SPA). |
37	| **Frontend auth config** | `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=otp` (eval default — compose sets `${DATAQ_AUTH_MODE:-otp}`) | the **same generic image**, reconfigured at **runtime** — `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` + `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` / `DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` (ADR 0028). **No rebuild** — nginx injects `/config.js` from env. See [frontend/Dockerfile](../frontend/Dockerfile). Optional `DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE` (#1347) **replaces** the requested OAuth scope string entirely for IdPs with a different scope vocabulary — AWS Cognito rejects the default list's `offline_access` (`invalid_scope`), so a Cognito deployment sets `openid email profile`; leave unset for Azure AD. Optional `DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE` (#1364) selects the sign-out dialect: unset = standard OIDC RP-Initiated Logout (Azure AD); `cognito` = AWS Cognito's non-conformant `/logout`, which requires `client_id` + `logout_uri` and 400s on the standard parameters. |
38	| `SECRET_STORE` | `openbao` (local/eval — ADR 0039) | **`azure_key_vault`** + `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL` + the managed identity's `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` (#408). |
39	| `DATABASE_URL` / `REDIS_URL` | inline, passwordless | Key Vault-backed Container Apps secrets — **never literals**; real credentials. A TLS redis uses the `rediss://` scheme; celery requires an explicit `ssl_cert_reqs` query parameter on it and the app defaults `ssl_cert_reqs=required` when absent (#1363 — without the default, a bare `rediss://` URL crash-loops the worker at boot with `ValueError: A rediss:// URL must have parameter ssl_cert_reqs`, the #1361 failure). An explicit value, even a weaker one, is never rewritten. |
40	| `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` | n/a (same-origin) | empty — the frontend Container App proxies `/api` same-origin (ADR 0028); set the SPA origin only if you split them. |
41	| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | n/a | the public origin — used to assemble inbound webhook URLs **and** the "View run" deep links in Slack/email alerts (#416); unset → alerts omit the link. |
42	| `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` | seeded dev user | a **minimal** real allowlist — admins can read every suite's failing-row samples (see [Operational notes](#operational-notes)). |
43	| `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | keep **`true`** — the fixed-window throttle on every public surface (REST + webhooks + `/mcp`), ADR 0035. Fail-open (a Redis outage disables it, logged); set `false` only to fully disable. |
44	| `RATE_LIMIT_AUTHENTICATED_PER_MINUTE` / `RATE_LIMIT_UNAUTHENTICATED_PER_MINUTE` / `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_PER_MINUTE` | `300` / `120` / `120` | per-minute caps, keyed per `sha256(bearer)` (authenticated) or client-IP (rest). The webhook cap is **per provider + IP** (#785) — each of adf/airflow/dbt has its own bucket at this cap; the per-IP webhook *total* is `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_IP_PER_MINUTE`. Defaults are generous; **tighten `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_PER_MINUTE`** to your orchestrator's real callback cadence. |
45	| `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_IP_PER_MINUTE` | `240` | per-IP ceiling across **all** webhook buckets from one IP (#785) — bounds the aggregate a single IP can spend by rotating provider segments; without it, per-provider buckets would multiply the per-IP webhook budget. |
46	| `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_PER_MINUTE` | `10` | strict per-IP cap for `/api/v1/auth/*` (OTP mint/verify, #1127) — checked **before** the bearer branch, so a token can't dodge it. This is the per-IP **backstop**; the tight screw is `AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_PER_EMAIL_PER_10MIN` below. **Tuning note (NAT pools):** per-IP buckets fold onto `RATE_LIMIT_IPV4_PREFIX` (default /24), so an entire corporate-NAT or campus egress range shares these 10 requests/minute — a burst of simultaneous sign-ins from one office can lock the pool out for the window. If your users sign in from behind one egress, **raise this** (30–60 is still a meaningful cap) rather than narrowing the global prefix to /32, which would strip NAT-evasion protection from the `webhook` and `unauth` classes too. The per-email counter is what actually bounds abuse per mailbox, and it is unaffected by NAT. |

# DataQ frontend image — build the Vite SPA, serve the static dist via nginx.
# Build context = frontend/ :  docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile frontend/
#
# ONE generic image, nothing baked in (ADR 0028): no cloud, no secret, no
# auth-bypass. Auth config is injected at RUNTIME — nginx serves /config.js from
# the DATAQ_AUTH_* env below (envsubst at startup), and the SPA reads it before
# the bundle runs. So the same image serves the eval stack (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass)
# and a real deployment (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc + authority/clientId/scope) — set the
# env at `docker run`, no rebuild. Replaces the #472 two-image (:latest/:dev) split.
#
# The deploy workflow builds + pushes this image and rolls the `dataq-app-frontend`
# Container App (ADR 0028 §5 cutover — the Static Web App is gone; SWA couldn't
# inject runtime config). See deploy/terraform/azure/frontend.tf.

# Pin the build stage to the native BUILD platform (amd64 on CI runners) even for
# an arm64 target image: a Vite SPA compiles to architecture-independent static
# assets, so there's no reason to run `pnpm build` under arm64 QEMU emulation — it
# only made the multi-arch publish pathologically slow / flaky (12min good case →
# 45min stall, #512). buildx cross-builds: this stage runs native, and only the
# tiny per-arch nginx `serve` stage below is built for each target platform, with
# the arch-independent dist COPYed in. $BUILDPLATFORM is a buildx-predefined arg.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
RUN corepack enable

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

COPY . .
RUN pnpm build

FROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve
# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages, lets the
# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push it, and inherits anonymous-pull visibility —
# ADR 0023, mirrors backend/Dockerfile).
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ frontend (React SPA served by nginx)"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
# Template (not a static conf): the nginx entrypoint envsubst's it at startup so
# the API upstream + auth config are runtime-configurable.
COPY nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template
# Opt into the nginx image's built-in resolver detection: its
# 15-local-resolvers.envsh only exports ${NGINX_LOCAL_RESOLVERS} (the
# /etc/resolv.conf nameservers, used by the proxy `resolver` directive) when this
# flag is set. Cloud-neutral (ADR 0028) — no resolver IP baked in; works in
# compose (127.0.0.11) and ACA/K8s (cluster DNS) alike.
ENV NGINX_ENTRYPOINT_LOCAL_RESOLVERS=1
# Runtime config env (ADR 0028) — MUST be defined (even if empty) so envsubst
# always substitutes them in /config.js; empty → SPA is unconfigured (fail-closed),
# bypass needs an explicit DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass. DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM defaults to
# the compose `api` service.
ENV DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api:8000 \
    DATAQ_AUTH_MODE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE="" \
    DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE=""
EXPOSE 8080

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# ALB behind CloudFront (#1345) — CloudFront is the sole public surface
# (ADR 0028 §5's api-goes-internal posture, one hop further out). Only the
# frontend target group exists; api/worker have no ALB listener and are
# reached only via Cloud Map internal DNS (ecs.tf).
#
# The listener stays plain HTTP :80: TLS terminates at CloudFront (Cognito
# requires an HTTPS redirect URI, and there is no custom domain — see
# cloudfront.tf). The security group admits only CloudFront's origin-facing
# ranges (AWS-managed prefix list), so the ALB is not reachable from an
# arbitrary internet address. Stated honestly: those ranges are shared by ALL
# CloudFront distributions, so a third party could still origin-point their
# own distribution at this ALB's (discoverable) DNS name; what that yields is
# plain-HTTP origin access through their edge — no auth bypass (the app
# validates Cognito tokens itself) and no XFF spoofing (the trusted-hops
# depth counts appends, which their edge also performs). Full closure is a
# secret custom origin header verified at nginx — follow-up #1355.

# AWS-managed, auto-updated list of CloudFront origin-facing IP ranges.
data "aws_ec2_managed_prefix_list" "cloudfront_origin" {
  name = "com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing"
}

resource "aws_security_group" "alb" {
  name        = "dataq-app-alb"
  description = "ALB - inbound HTTP from CloudFront origin-facing ranges only"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id

  ingress {
    description     = "HTTP from CloudFront"
    from_port       = 80
    to_port         = 80
    protocol        = "tcp"
    prefix_list_ids = [data.aws_ec2_managed_prefix_list.cloudfront_origin.id]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-alb" }
}

resource "aws_lb" "app" {
  name               = "dataq-app"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "application"
  subnets            = aws_subnet.public[*].id
  security_groups    = [aws_security_group.alb.id]

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-alb" }
}

resource "aws_lb_target_group" "frontend" {
  name        = "dataq-app-frontend"
  port        = 8080
  protocol    = "HTTP"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
  target_type = "ip" # required for Fargate tasks (no EC2 instance id)

  health_check {
    # `/` (the SPA index), NOT `/healthz` — nginx PROXIES /healthz to the api,
    # so checking it here made frontend target health mean "the api is up":
    # an api outage would have had the ALB recycling perfectly healthy
    # frontend tasks in a loop, masking the real failure (#1349). `/` is
    # served by nginx locally; frontend health now means "nginx + bundle up".
    # The api's own health stays observable via its ECS service + /healthz
    # through the site.
    path                = "/"
    healthy_threshold   = 2
    unhealthy_threshold = 3
    interval            = 15
    timeout             = 5
  }

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-frontend" }
}

resource "aws_lb_listener" "http" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.app.arn
  port              = 80
  protocol          = "HTTP"

  default_action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.frontend.arn
  }
}

locals {
  # No custom domain yet — CloudFront's own domain is the deployment's public
  # HTTPS URL (#1345). Depends only on the distribution (which depends only on
  # the ALB), so nothing later in the graph waits on the ECS service itself —
  # mirroring the Azure stack's deterministic-FQDN trick that breaks the
  # frontend<->api circular dependency.
  frontend_url     = "https://${aws_cloudfront_distribution.app.domain_name}"
  api_internal_url = "http://api.dataq.local:8000"
}

2	# prebuilt UI image works same-origin without Azure Static Web App "linking"

4	#

6	# /etc/nginx/templates/*.template at startup, so ${DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM} is filled
7	# from the env (default http://api:8000, set in frontend/Dockerfile; overridable
8	# in compose). Only env vars that are actually set are substituted, so nginx's
9	# own $uri / $host / $scheme runtime vars are left untouched.
10	
11	# The client-facing scheme, forwarded upstream (#1138). NOT `$scheme`.
12	#
13	# This container never terminates TLS — it listens on plain HTTP :8080 and the
14	# edge in front of it (Azure Container Apps' Envoy ingress, or whatever proxy a
15	# BYO deployment puts there) does. So `$scheme` here is *deterministically*
16	# `http` on every request, including ones the browser made over HTTPS. Sending
17	# `X-Forwarded-Proto: $scheme` doesn't merely lose information — `proxy_set_header`
18	# REPLACES the edge's correct `https` with our wrong `http`, so the API sees a
19	# plaintext request and marks the OTP session cookie **without `Secure`** on a
20	# live HTTPS deployment (ADR 0032; the backend's `_cookie_secure()` infers from
21	# exactly this header).
22	#
23	# So: prefer what the edge told us, and fall back to `$scheme` only when there is
24	# no edge header at all — the direct-connection case (compose, `docker run -p
25	# 8080`), where `$scheme` genuinely IS the client-facing scheme.
26	#
27	# Trust boundary, stated plainly: this makes nginx trust an inbound header. That
28	# is sound *because a client cannot reach this hop directly* — ACA's ingress is
29	# the only route in, and Envoy sets `X-Forwarded-Proto` itself from the TLS
30	# state, overwriting whatever the client sent. If you deploy this image with NO
31	# TLS-terminating proxy in front and expose it straight to the internet, a client
32	# CAN dictate the value; the only thing it influences is cookie-`Secure`
33	# inference (it grants no authentication and no authorization), and the
34	# belt-and-braces answer is to set `AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true` explicitly
35	# on the API — which stops consulting the header at all.
36	#
37	# `map` lives in the `http` context: this template renders into conf.d/, which
38	# nginx includes inside `http { }`, so a top-level directive here is valid.
39	map $http_x_forwarded_proto $dataq_forwarded_proto {
40	    default $http_x_forwarded_proto;
41	    ""      $scheme;
42	}
43	
44	# ── Origin-secret guard (#1355) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
45	# When DATAQ_ORIGIN_SECRET is set, every request must carry the matching
46	# X-DataQ-Origin-Secret header or it is 403'd. The intended sender is a fronting
47	# CDN/edge that stamps the header on origin fetches (AWS: CloudFront's custom
48	# origin header, set in deploy/terraform/aws/cloudfront.tf) — closing the gap
49	# where a THIRD PARTY's distribution origin-points at this container's
50	# (discoverable) load-balancer DNS: their edge doesn't know the secret. Note
51	# CloudFront overwrites any viewer-sent header of the same name with its own
52	# configured value, so the secret cannot be probed through the legitimate
53	# distribution either.
54	#
55	# When the variable is EMPTY (compose, BYOL, Azure — where ACA ingress is the

# CloudFront — the HTTPS front for the ALB (#1345).
#
# Cognito requires redirect URIs to be HTTPS (http:// is allowed only for
# localhost), so the original HTTP-only-ALB design could never complete an
# OIDC sign-in. With no custom domain chosen (that decision stands), the
# cheapest valid HTTPS origin is CloudFront's own *.cloudfront.net domain with
# the default certificate — additive to swap out later: pick a domain, add an
# ACM cert + alias here, and the ALB/ECS layers don't change.
#
# This is a pass-through, not a CDN in anger: the default behavior disables
# caching entirely (the app is a dynamic SPA + API; index.html must never be
# stale, /api must never be cached) and forwards the full request via the
# managed AllViewer policy. Static-asset caching can be added as a dedicated
# /assets/* behavior later if it ever matters — nginx already serves
# fingerprinted files.

data "aws_cloudfront_cache_policy" "caching_disabled" {
  name = "Managed-CachingDisabled"
}

data "aws_cloudfront_origin_request_policy" "all_viewer" {
  name = "Managed-AllViewer"
}

resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "app" {
  enabled         = true
  comment         = "DataQ frontend — HTTPS front for the ALB (no custom domain)"
  is_ipv6_enabled = true
  # Cheapest edge-location class (NA + EU) — this is an HTTPS terminator, not
  # a latency play.
  price_class = "PriceClass_100"

  origin {
    domain_name = aws_lb.app.dns_name
    origin_id   = "alb"

    # Origin secret (#1355): stamped on every origin fetch and verified by the
    # frontend nginx (DATAQ_ORIGIN_SECRET) — closes the residual gap alb.tf
    # documents, where a third party's OWN distribution could origin-point at
    # this ALB's discoverable DNS name through the shared CloudFront
    # origin-facing ranges. CloudFront overwrites any viewer-sent header of
    # the same name, so the value can't be probed through this distribution.
    # (Visible in the distribution config to anyone with CloudFront read
    # access — an origin-authentication token, not a user credential.)
    custom_header {
      name  = "X-DataQ-Origin-Secret"
      value = random_password.origin_secret.result
    }

    custom_origin_config {
      http_port  = 80
      https_port = 443
      # The ALB listener is plain HTTP :80; TLS terminates at CloudFront. The
      # ALB's security group admits only CloudFront's origin-facing address
      # ranges (alb.tf) — see that file's note on what that does and does not
      # guarantee (#1355).
      origin_protocol_policy = "http-only"
      origin_ssl_protocols   = ["TLSv1.2"]
      # Long warehouse-bound API calls (column profiler, dry-run, test-
      # connection against a cold warehouse) routinely exceed CloudFront's 30s
      # default; match the ALB's 60s idle timeout so CloudFront isn't the
      # tightest hop (/code-review finding).
      origin_read_timeout      = 60
      origin_keepalive_timeout = 60
    }
  }

  default_cache_behavior {
    target_origin_id       = "alb"
    viewer_protocol_policy = "redirect-to-https"
    allowed_methods        = ["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "PUT", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"]
    cached_methods         = ["GET", "HEAD"]
    compress               = true

    cache_policy_id          = data.aws_cloudfront_cache_policy.caching_disabled.id
    origin_request_policy_id = data.aws_cloudfront_origin_request_policy.all_viewer.id
  }

  restrictions {
    geo_restriction {
      restriction_type = "none"
    }
  }

  viewer_certificate {
    cloudfront_default_certificate = true
  }

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-cloudfront" }
}

# Alphanumeric only (`special = false`): the nginx guard's map key uses ":" as
# its delimiter and the value must stay free of nginx map metacharacters.
resource "random_password" "origin_secret" {
  length  = 40
  special = false
}

# Injected into the frontend task via the `secrets` block (execution-role read,
# same pattern as database-url/redis-url) rather than plaintext task-def env.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "origin_secret" {
  name                    = "dataq-app-infra/origin-secret"
  recovery_window_in_days = 0
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "origin_secret" {
  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.origin_secret.id
  secret_string = random_password.origin_secret.result
}
